532834|2026-06.headline: Camlin Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to INR5,199 million, but EBITDA margin collapsed to about 4% from 45% last quarter on raw material costs and vanillin under-utilisation.
532834|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR5,199 million, up about 28% YoY and about INR1,000 million QoQ, but margins fell sharply on raw material, freight and logistics costs tied to the West Asia conflict. The company reorganised reporting into Specialty Ingredients, Aroma and Performance Chemicals, with Aroma and Performance Chemicals both EBITDA-negative or near zero in the quarter. Ethyl vanillin ramp-up ran at low utilisation, and FY27 vanillin volume guidance was cut to about 3,000 tons from 3,600-4,000 tons. Management cut FY27 EBITDA margin guidance to 10-12% while keeping revenue guidance, and debt was flat at about INR640 crore gross.

segments.name: Specialty Ingredients (blends and straights)
segments.commentary: Revenue above INR4,000 million with blends above INR3,000 million; EBITDA margin 6.35%. Management says about 4-5% of gross margin was lost to raw material costs and Brazil air-freight, with Brazil's shortfall of about INR8 crore expected to correct in Q2.

segments.name: Aroma (vanillin)
segments.commentary: Sold about 560 tons (350 t ethyl, 200 t methyl from channel stock) against 6,000-ton capacity; produced ~400 tons. Quarterly EBITDA negative at INR4-4.5 crore on fixed cost absorption; management expects positive EBITDA in Q2.

segments.name: Performance Chemicals
segments.commentary: Gross segment revenue about INR175 crore, of which ~INR130 crore is internal transfer, leaving ~INR40 crore external sales. EBITDA margin 2.5% with diphenol plant shut; management expects positive EBITDA from Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance: INR2,200-2,300 crore, versus earlier INR2,000-2,400 crore; management says top line is secure.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance cut to 10-12% (10-11% per CFO/MD), implying about INR220-230 crore EBITDA, versus earlier INR250-280 crore.
Analyst read-back: average run rate of about INR70 crore EBITDA per quarter for remaining quarters; management did not dispute this.
Q3 FY27 expected to return to double-digit consolidated EBITDA margin; H2 margin of 13-15% floated by an analyst, not disputed.
FY28 EBITDA margin in the range of 12-14%.
Vanillin FY27 volume about 3,000 tons (earlier 3,600-4,000); 4 campaigns planned, Q2 volume 500-600 tons, Q3 1,000+ tons. Capacity 6,000 tons, achievable 5,000 tons with 3 campaigns.
Blends growth of at least 20% in FY27; budget assumes 25-30%.
capex_capacity: Vanillin capacity 6,000 tons per year; ethyl vanillin campaign of about 750 tons ran through mid-August, with about 350 tons sold and over 300 tons produced; methyl vanillin campaign to follow after roughly two weeks of changeover.
Diphenol plant shut because phenol and raw material prices are high; hydroquinone secured from China for the next two quarters; decision on alternate use or restart by Q3 FY27.
Working capital cycle about 100 days on a consolidated basis; each INR1 crore of revenue growth needs about one-third as working capital support.
CFS Europe in liquidation with no further cash burn beyond legal costs; China subsidiary liquidation expected to cost INR10-20 million in Q1.
demand_pricing: Channel stocks in the US and China described as cleared; management sees demand picking up and is negotiating quarterly, half-yearly and annual contracts with F&F customers.
US and Europe ethyl vanillin realisations stated at about $13-14/kg; methyl vanillin raw material cost $7-8/kg, with conversion cost about INR7 crore/month fixed.
Management sees a supply gap of about 5,000-6,000 tons in US and Europe that must be imported; Syensqo (Solvay) is the market leader; Chinese imports priced around $15 against Solvay's $18.
Pass-through of raw material increases to blends customers is lagging by one quarter; management expects to recover about half of the cost increase in Q2.
Trade financing (dealer finance) on purchase and sales sides costs an estimated 1-1.5% and is hitting gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 EBITDA guidance achievable given Q1 EBITDA of about INR9 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management restated guidance as INR2,200-2,300 crore revenue with 10-11% margin, which it said is within reach on the current cost structure; it expects about 10% margin over the next nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Aroma EBITDA negative and what is its normalised economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said low utilisation (about 400 tons produced vs 1,500-ton quarterly capacity) left fixed cost unabsorbed. Management said 70-80% utilisation would make the business profitable and gave about 7% EBITDA at $13/kg on 3,000 tons.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt reduction and what external funding is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt is INR640 crore, down from INR670 crore on 31 March. The CFO said INR100-200 crore of working capital lines are expected within 1-1.5 months, and equity or other capital is being considered without a decision yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 vanillin volume cut from 3,600-4,000 tons to about 3,000?
qa_highlights.answer: The ethyl vanillin ramp-up was slower to secure quality, with 95% customer approval. Each campaign switch costs about a month, and four campaigns are planned this year.

qa_highlights.question: What would Q1 EBITDA have been under normal conditions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 4-5% of gross margin was lost, which would have lifted EBITDA to roughly INR37-40 crore, an analyst's figure that management confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Will raw material cost pressure persist into Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects elevated raw material prices to persist through Q2 and guidance assumes about three months of elevated costs, not six or nine months.

The whole issue is on the margins.
So, on sales side, it's not a problem at all. The whole issue is on the purchase side.

The third is, of course, capital, which we are looking at different various options to be able to raise that capital.
532834|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on top-line delivery and on a margin recovery from Q2-Q3, but cautious on raw material costs, the Aroma ramp-up and funding. Several answers were hedged, with capital raising described as undecided, and the margin guidance was cut twice in the call's framing.

532834|2026-09.headline: Camlin Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to about 2.5% as liquidity strain hit margins; board approved a ~INR250 crore rights issue.
532834|2026-09.overview: Management said the quarter was weak because liquidity constraints forced reliance on channel financing and stretched payables, which raised costs and cut gross margin from INR2,142 million to INR1,958 million. Aroma revenue fell from INR774 million to INR472 million after the switch from methyl vanillin to ethyl vanillin, and the diphenol plant has been closed since May 2026. The board approved a rights issue of about INR250 crore, backed by promoters, to fund working capital, with money expected by end-calendar 2026 or early 2027. Management guided Q3 only marginally better than Q2 and Q4 to over INR600 crore turnover and EBITDA of INR60 crore-plus.

segments.name: Blends (specialty ingredients)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,970 million vs INR3,086 million prior quarter; EBITDA margin about 11-12%, with Europe subsidiaries Vitafor and Vinpai cited as growth levers. Gross margin range 35-40%.

segments.name: Straights (specialty ingredients)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose to INR1,109 million from INR927 million as volumes recovered despite local price competition; average EBITDA margin about 8%.

segments.name: Aroma (vanillin)
segments.commentary: Revenue fell to INR472 million from INR774 million after the methyl-to-ethyl vanillin changeover; management cited realisation near $12/kg and an EBITDA of about zero at current selling prices.

segments.name: Performance chemicals (diphenol/hydroquinone)
segments.commentary: Diphenol plant (18,000 MT) closed since May 2026; maintenance cash burn fell to INR5 crore in the quarter from INR8-9 crore, targeted at INR25 million per quarter by end-Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27: margin expected to be a tad better than Q2, not a major improvement.
Q4 FY27: turnover above INR6,000 million (INR600 crore) and EBITDA around 10%, or INR60 crore-plus, assuming current raw material prices.
Rights issue of about INR250 crore: pricing, cut-off and issue size to be decided after SEBI/exchange approval of the draft letter of offer; funds expected by end-calendar 2026 or early 2027.
Management says the rights issue could add about INR500 million of blends revenue in Q4 at about 35% gross margin, and about 1,000 MT per quarter of vanillin at about $12/kg.
Management estimated that the rights issue funding could release about INR180-190 crore of interest-related cost (about 3-4% of cost) by unwinding channel financing and overdue payables.
FY27 target of about INR2,000 crore turnover at 10% EBITDA (about INR200 crore) was acknowledged as unlikely by management, confirmed in response to an analyst question.
capex_capacity: Diphenol plant (18,000 MT capacity) closed since May 2026 due to phenol price doubling; no visibility on restart given Chinese capacity pricing well below cost.
Vanillin utilisation: about $10/kg cost at 70% utilisation; management has visibility to run at 70%.
Vanillin inventory about 175-200 MT.
Fixed costs about INR20 crore per quarter, which must be absorbed by volumes.
Vanillin visibility: about 2,500-2,700 MT from the US and 1,300-1,500 MT from Europe for next calendar year; target about 1,000 MT per quarter by Q4 FY27/Q1 next calendar year.
Rights issue proceeds to be used for working capital (about INR130 crore of existing credit), with the rest for growth next calendar year; no further borrowing expected per management.
demand_pricing: Vanillin net realisation about $12-12.5/kg after tariffs and distribution costs; blended ethyl and methyl about $13.7/kg; management says realisation is muted by Chinese material rerouted via Thailand and Malaysia.
Vanillin EBITDA per kg about $2 at 70% utilisation before fixed costs; essentially zero at current volumes.
Raw materials (phenol-linked) have roughly doubled since February; TBHQ and BHA input costs up 15-20%, not passed through due to local competition.
Freight costs almost doubled in the quarter, attributed to the war situation.
Natural blends pricing largely stable; petrochemical-linked blends pass-through lagging. Blends gross margin stays at 35-40%.
Large US distributors reportedly exiting Chinese-origin material due to legal risk; supply starting, expected to grow from Q1 of next calendar year.

qa_highlights.question: What would have been the incremental revenue and gross margin had the rights issue been done a quarter earlier?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales would have been about INR100 crore higher and EBITDA margin about INR60 crore better.

qa_highlights.question: Are promoters participating in the rights issue, and what dilution is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoters will subscribe to their share (cited as 48%); pricing not yet decided, so total dilution depends on final pricing expected in the next few weeks.

qa_highlights.question: Why return to B2B distributor channel given credit cycles, and why is vanillin realisation only about $12-12.5?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said distributors pay in about 30 days versus 90-120 days for large direct customers, saving working capital; muted realisation reflects rerouted Chinese supply and should improve over three to four quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 reach the INR200 crore EBITDA target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no, that is correct, given the H1 run-rate; Q4 is the first quarter with liquidity, with turnaround expected.

qa_highlights.question: How do Aroma EBITDA margin of -23% and $2/kg EBITDA reconcile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said $2/kg is at 70% utilisation before about INR20 crore of quarterly fixed costs; at current selling prices and Q2 volumes EBITDA per ton was zero, and the Aroma loss was about INR11 crore on 300 MT after fixed overheads.

qa_highlights.question: How much further capital is needed after the INR250 crore issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the issue should stabilise working capital and fund growth, and no additional borrowings are expected if plans proceed on schedule.

qa_highlights.question: Are there excess inventories in the US vanillin market due to Thailand rerouting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory is being cleared, with destocking expected by year-end.

risks_watch: Liquidity: reliance on channel financing and long-overdue payables (above 90 days carry about 3-4% extra cost); INR250 crore rights issue pricing, timing and final dilution still undetermined.
Q3 guidance is only marginally better than Q2; Q4 turnaround to INR600 crore turnover and 10% EBITDA depends on the rights issue closing on time and raw material prices holding.
Input cost volatility: phenol-linked inputs doubled since February; management assumes current prices for Q4 and says any worsening will hit margins.
Chinese diphenol/hydroquinone and vanillin oversupply and rerouting; anti-dumping duty dependence and reliance on distributors for vanillin volumes.
Working capital: management says the cycle is about 200 days, and the balance sheet relies on credit lines (about INR130 crore) during the liquidity squeeze.
532834|2026-09.management_tone: Candid and cautious on the quarter, which management called not encouraging, attributing weakness to liquidity constraints, input cost inflation and local competition. Confident on recovery through the rights issue and the Q4 turnaround, but many forward numbers rely on assumptions rather than booked orders.
key_quotes: So it looks like we have to be -- we have to fight for this third quarter to stay afloat and at least give a similar result, we would have liked a much better EBITDA.
Q4 will be the first quarter with the liquidity with us. The turnaround will happen in Q4.
So our general working capital cycle is 200 days, and that's looking lower because we have INR130-odd crores of credit.
Yes. That's right. That's right.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.why: No new product, brand or molecule launch discussed; ethyl vanillin changeover is an existing product swap.

532835|2026-03.headline: ICRA Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 28.4% YoY, led by Research & Analytics (+56.8%) with Fintellix consolidated from October 2025.
532835|2026-03.overview: ICRA reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue up 28.4% YoY, with Research and Analytics up 56.8% on the Fintellix acquisition and Ratings up 10.6%. Q4 consolidated PBT before exceptional items and tax was INR 72.8 crores. For FY26, revenue grew 20.4% and PBT grew 10%, with exceptional charges from the new Labour Code excluded for comparability. Management flagged moderation in the Knowledge Services business and a margin-mix shift toward product-led businesses, and it sees near-term bond market softness offset by bank credit growth. Capital allocation questions (buyback, cash of over INR 700 crores, acquisition IRRs) were largely deflected, with the dividend raised and a special dividend declared.

segments.name: Ratings
segments.commentary: Revenue up 10.6% in Q4 and 14.2% for FY26. Management said the segment is a leverage play on economic activity, and Q4 growth was below some peers, which management attributed to a different base and strategic focus on growth segments.

segments.name: Research and Analytics
segments.commentary: Revenue up 56.8% in Q4 and 29.8% for FY26, driven by Fintellix (consolidated from October 2025, roughly 26% EBITDA margin per notes). Excluding Fintellix, Knowledge Services grew modestly; Risk Management and Market Data grew healthily and turned profitable.

segments.name: Knowledge Services (KnowTech)
segments.commentary: Stable in core areas but growth moderated due to discontinued engagements and automation. Management expects a structural margin shift as non-KnowTech businesses, with different margin profiles, gain mix.

segments.name: Moody's-related non-ratings work
segments.commentary: Growth has been muted over the last couple of years and management expects moderation, with no higher double-digit growth expected. Some periodic in-sourcing by the parent continues.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue or margin guidance given; management cited a BankTech product-led EBITDA range of 20% to 35%, depending on geography mix.
Management expects Fintellix to drive reasonable growth over the next 2 to 3 years, partly offsetting Knowledge Services moderation, without quantifying it.
ICRA projects India GDP growth moderating to 6.2% in real terms in FY27, assuming average crude of $95 per barrel.

Management expects bank credit to drive most ratings growth in the near term, with bond market activity subdued due to higher yields; no significant slowdown seen in the first couple of months of FY27.
Bank transition to the expected credit loss framework from 1 April 2027 is expected to sustain demand for risk modelling and compliance solutions.
Management expects roughly INR 180 to 200 crores of cash flow generation in FY27, per an analyst's figure that management did not dispute.
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were discussed on the call.
Research and Analytics reorganised into KnowTech, BankTech and CapTech, supported by a unified IT and product engineering organisation.
Ongoing investment in analytics platforms, compliance capabilities and AI-powered agents; AI layer being integrated into subsidiary analytical tools.
demand_pricing: Ratings demand is tied to bank credit and bond issuance; the first couple of months of FY27 showed no significant slowdown, but geopolitical headwinds persist.
Fintellix competitors cited: Regnology and Nasdaq Technologies (global, PE or public-backed, acquisition-driven), plus system integrators and some Indian CRAs with risk and regulatory solutions.
About USD 18 million of FY26 revenue is dollar-denominated (roughly one-third of about INR 600 crores revenue, per management's figure); dollar-denominated costs are not significant.
Fintellix shift from one-time licence plus smaller recurring fee toward annuity or subscription model is in progress, but not all clients are ready to adopt it.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Ratings growth materially lower than peers, and what is the non-ratings growth ex-Fintellix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ICRA is in a similar band to peers, with double-digit growth over the last 4 years, and that growth-segment focus is the strategy. Ex-Fintellix, Knowledge Services grew modestly while Risk Management and Market Data grew healthily.

qa_highlights.question: Is a buyback under consideration given over INR 700 crores of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to a rising dividend (normal dividend INR 60 to INR 70 per share plus special dividend) and said alternative capital allocation options are being evaluated, subject to Board approval and tax changes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Ratings outlook for FY27, and what are April-May borrowing trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects bond activity to stay subdued given higher yields, with bank credit driving growth. No significant slowdown was seen in the first couple of months of FY27. No revenue growth guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How will R&A margins evolve as the mix shifts, and could Ratings margins exceed 40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no margin guidance. It said product-led BankTech-type businesses earn 20% to 35% EBITDA margins, and that double-digit Ratings revenue growth typically brings margin expansion as employee cost growth stays below 10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Moody's-related work and in-sourcing from the parent?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth has been muted and is expected to moderate, with no higher double-digit growth expected. Periodic in-sourcing continues, with new project work arriving on an ongoing basis.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Fintellix segment profit and business description?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give Fintellix-specific contribution, citing parity of disclosure, but referred to notes to accounts showing around 26% EBITDA margin. Fintellix was described as RiskTech and RegTech, covering regulatory reporting and credit analytics for banks, insurers and asset managers.

risks_watch: Elevated energy prices from the West Asia conflict and a possible weak monsoon could weigh on FY27 growth and credit demand.
Knowledge Services growth moderation and automation trends could continue to pressure segment margins during the mix shift.
Limited disclosure of acquisition returns and Fintellix-specific financials, which shareholders have asked about.
Ratings margin gap versus other CRAs; management intends to close it through sales growth.
Capital allocation: whether cash above INR 700 crores is returned to shareholders via buyback or other means, pending Board decision.

532835|2026-09.headline: ICRA's Risk & Analytics mix reached 50% of group revenue in FY26, with Ratings growing 15.2% in H1 FY27 while non-Ratings run-rate stayed near INR 80 crore a quarter.
532835|2026-09.overview: Management chose to focus on five strategic pillars rather than the quarter's numbers, which were covered in the investor presentation and press release. Ratings revenue reached INR 336 crore in FY26 (12.4% CAGR since FY21) with operating margin of 37.6%. Risk & Analytics (non-Ratings) revenue rose to INR 313 crore in FY26 from INR 114.9 crore five years earlier, but its quarterly run-rate has been flat at about INR 80 crore for the last few quarters, and margin is compressing as BankTech and CapTech gain mix. Management said D2K and Fintellix are still loss-making, that D2K became 100% owned only about 4-5 months ago, and that no profitability timeline will be guided.

qa_highlights.question: Why has non-Ratings profit mix fallen while revenue share rose to 50%, and what does this mean for acquisition IRR, especially Fintellix?

qa_highlights.question: How much risk does a bond-yield spike pose to Ratings revenue, given ICRA's bond exposure?

532843|2026-03.headline: Fortis FY26 consolidated revenue rose 17.3% to INR9,128 crores and EBITDA margin expanded to 22.8%; FY27 guidance is 15%+ hospital revenue growth.
532843|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue reached INR9,128 crores (+17.3%), with hospital revenue up 19.1% to INR7,773 crores and consolidated operating EBITDA up 31.3% to INR2,085 crores (22.8% margin vs 20.4%). Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR2,365 crores (+17.8%) and PAT rose 44.2% to INR271 crores. Management flagged softer Q4 occupancy at several large hospitals, attributed to a drop in international patients and a government price cap on oncology drugs affecting CGHS/ECHS business in Punjab. Net debt rose to INR2,334 crores (1.09x net debt/EBITDA) on acquisitions and investments.

segments.name: Hospitals
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR7,773 crores (+19.1%), operating EBITDA margin 22.2% vs 20.5%; ~85% of consolidated revenue and EBITDA. Q4 revenue INR2,023 crores (+19%), Q4 EBITDA margin 22.1%. Occupancy 68% vs 69%; ARPOB up 3.4% to INR2.51 crores.

segments.name: Diagnostics (Agilus)
segments.commentary: FY26 gross revenue INR1,527 crores (+8.5%), operating EBITDA INR360 crores (23.6% margin vs 17.7%; 23.2% ex one-offs). Q4 gross revenue INR387 crores (+11.1%), EBITDA INR85 crores, margin 22%; Q4 tests ~10 million (+5%). Preventive health 13% of mix vs 11%; B2C:B2B 52:48 for FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 hospital revenue growth guided at 15%+ on an ongoing (organic) basis; acquisitions excluded and additive.
FY27 hospital EBITDA margin expected to improve by about 150 bps; long-term target of 25% by FY28 reaffirmed, with management seeing 1.5%-2% annual improvement.
Diagnostics FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 23%-24%; revenue growth targeted at double digits (currently ~8.5%), with ~70% volume and ~30% value mix.
Jaipur expected to grow ~15% in FY27 with 13%-14% EBITDA margin.
Brownfield bed additions of 500+ in FY27 and ~1,800 beds over the next 4 years; capex about INR900 crores annually (about 60% maintenance).
Dividend of INR1 per share (10% of face value), fourth consecutive year, subject to shareholder approval.
IHH reportedly plans to raise stake to 50% and infuse ~INR10,000 crores fresh equity; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR700 crores; ~250 beds added via brownfield (Manesar, Noida, Faridabad) and ~800 beds added in total including acquisitions.

Acquired People Tree Hospital (125 beds, Bengaluru, Jan 2026) with land for 300+ beds; Shrimann Super Specialty Jalandhar (228 beds, Jul 2025) with land for 450+ beds; 200-bed Greater Noida lease (Sep 2025); Adayu 36-bed mental health facility in Gurugram (Nov 2025).
FMRI new tower to be operationalised within about a week, opening ~100 beds in FY27 on a phased basis; FY27 brownfield additions of 400+ beds per earlier statement, with 500+ per later remark.
Shalimar Bagh expansion delayed pending approvals; ~300 beds moved from FY28 to FY29; Mohali, Shalimar Bagh and Amritsar large towers ~2.5-3 years away.
BG Road has ~100 beds of brownfield capacity uncommissioned until occupancy improves; Mulund considering another tower.
demand_pricing: Hospital occupancy 68% in FY26 vs 69%; occupied beds up 15% (management cited 3,270 to 2,838, a figure order inverted in the transcript). FMRI at 85-95% occupancy; BG Road at ~55% vs ~63-64% area norm.
International patient revenue +18.5% to INR639 crores (7.8% of hospital revenue); Q4 international growth ~11%. Management is diversifying to Africa and other markets.
Oncology drug price capping (~30% of MRP) under CGHS/ECHS led Fortis to stop some high-cost drug cases, mainly in Punjab; no timeline for resolution. Management said margin impact is limited.
Focus specialties grew 18.9% and make up 62% of hospital revenue; radiation therapy volumes +19%, robotic surgeries +66%.
Diagnostics: 40.8 million tests in FY26 vs 39.2 million; 50+ new tests added; Illumina NovaSeq X operational at Mumbai reference lab.

qa_highlights.question: Why are occupancies falling at large hospitals such as FMRI and BG Road, and how will this improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal attributed the drop mainly to lower international business (Q4 growth ~11% vs 18-20% for the year) and oncology drug capping in Punjab. He said BG Road is low due to TPA/cash mix, intense competition and a 55% level versus a 63-64% area norm, with a target above 60%.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins expand given new capacity and doctor cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashutosh Raghuvanshi said doctor costs rose slightly but further increases are not expected; the 25% FY28 margin target is intact, with 1.5-2% annual improvement now seen as more confident.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue did the 800 new beds contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said Q4 hospital revenue of INR2,000 crores would be INR1,928 crores excluding People Tree, Adayu and Jalandhar, so new-unit contribution is small.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue and EBITDA of Gleneagles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not consolidate Gleneagles and does not track full-year numbers; it is trending around INR70 per month.

qa_highlights.question: Is Diagnostics demerger being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said the focus is on profitability, this is not the time to lock value, and alternatives may be considered once the business matures.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Gleneagles transaction moving forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is under deliberation and evaluation; no timeline, and it would need majority-of-minority approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Manesar run-rate and FMRI ARPOB driver?
qa_highlights.answer: Manesar FY26 revenue was INR140 crores at ~48% occupancy (new beds being added) and reached EBITDA breakeven. FMRI ARPOB rise was attributed to gross-basis international business, MR Linac, Gamma Knife and day-care oncology.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Jaipur and FEHI improving, and why build a Bangalore hospital in a competitive market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited operational efficiency, new facilities and clinical talent at FEHI; Jaipur expected to grow ~15% at 13-14% margin. The People Tree site is a less competitive micro-market with underserved catchment, per Ashutosh Raghuvanshi.

Occupancy at large hospitals (FMRI, BG Road, Faridabad) and absorption of new beds in Gurgaon and Noida amid doctor cost pressure.
International patient growth slowing (Q4 ~11%) and sustainability of domestic growth offsetting it.

532843|2026-06.headline: Fortis Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 17.5% to INR 2,545 crore, but hospital EBITDA margin slipped to 21.5% from 22.1% on ESOP, ramp-up and legal costs.
532843|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 17.5% YoY to INR 2,545 crore, with hospital revenue up 19% to INR 2,187 crore and diagnostics gross revenue up 10.2% to INR 407 crore. Consolidated operating EBITDA pre-ESOP rose 15.8% to INR 568 crore, but margin eased to 22.3% from 22.6%, with hospitals at 21.5% versus 22.1%. Management said the margin dip reflects new ramp-up units, higher legal costs, higher doubtful-debt provisions and the new ESOP charge, and it maintained the FY28 target of about 25% margin, now framed as post-ESOP. Net debt rose to INR 2,233 crore (1.01x EBITDA) from INR 1,869 crore a year earlier.

financial_highlights.metric: Profit after tax before exceptional items

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 1,869 crore and 0.92x at 30 June 2025

segments.name: Hospitals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 2,187 crore (+19%) and operating EBITDA INR 471 crore at 21.5% margin versus 22.1%. Like-for-like margin excluding new Punjab, Bengaluru and Delhi NCR leased facilities was about 22%. Renal sciences grew 28%, neurosciences 27% and orthopaedics 23%.

segments.name: Diagnostics (Agilus)
segments.commentary: Gross revenue INR 407 crore (+10.2%) and operating EBITDA INR 97 crore at 23.9% margin versus 23.0%. B2C:B2B mix improved to 53:47 from 51:49; preventive share rose to 14% from 12% and specialised to 35% from 34%. About 10.5 million tests processed and over 200 customer touch points added in the quarter.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 174 crore, up 13.3% YoY, about 8% of consolidated revenue, broadly in line with Q1 FY26.

guidance_outlook: Hospital EBITDA margin target of about 25% in roughly two years (FY28); management said it is now aspired to be achieved after ESOP cost, and Q1 is a dip versus this path.
Management retained the consolidated margin guidance; analysts had cited 150-200 bps hospital margin expansion for FY27, which management did not restate as ESOP-inclusive.
ESOP charge expected around INR 40 crore per quarter for the rest of FY27 if headcount is unchanged, falling to about INR 30 crore per quarter and then about INR 25 crore per quarter in year three.
Diagnostics revenue growth of about 12-13% and EBITDA margin of 24-25% for the remainder of the year, per the CFO; the Agilus CEO reiterated double-digit revenue growth guidance.
Plan to add about 400 beds in the remaining three quarters of FY27, including about 200 beds at FMRI pending an occupancy certificate expected imminently. Q1 added about 100 beds.

Manesar radiation oncology equipment expected to be commissioned by November 2026, after which it becomes a comprehensive oncology centre; Manesar and Greater Noida expected to reach mid-teens EBITDA margin by year-end or higher.
Capex: growth is expected to consume about 50% of EBITDA through brownfield expansion, excluding acquisitions; proton therapy in Gurgaon estimated at about INR 252 crore.
capex_capacity: Q1 added about 100 operational beds through brownfield expansion at Noida, Amritsar and Jalandhar; Manesar has about 187 beds operational at about 60% occupancy.

Entered Odisha via an O&M agreement for a 300-bed greenfield hospital in Cuttack; no capital committed.
Oncology build-out: three units (Faridabad brownfield block, Amritsar and Jaipur) are starting work to become full cancer hospitals.
Company is pursuing inorganic deals in existing clusters (Bengaluru, Delhi NCR, Punjab, MMR, Kolkata); no details disclosed. Gleneagles O&M discussions with IHH ongoing.
demand_pricing: Hospital occupancy flat at 69% as occupied beds grew 17%; management said the core base consistently runs around 70% and levers can add 2-3 percentage points.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ESOP charge for FY27 and the next two years, and can consolidated margin improve by 100 bps in FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% margin target pre- or post-ESOP?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 25% target now aspires to be achieved after ESOP cost, expected in about two years, with levers including ramp-up of new units (from -0.4% drag to +1%), new doctor teams, lower legal costs and recovery of doubtful debt provisions.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Manesar and Greater Noida margins below 10%, and when will they reach 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Manesar had 187 beds operational at about 60% occupancy with radiation oncology due by November; management expects both hospitals to be in the mid-teens EBITDA margin by year-end or higher.

qa_highlights.question: Diagnostics growth lags industry; what are the challenges?
qa_highlights.answer: The Agilus CEO, in role about 10 days, said the company is reworking plans; B2C mix target rises to 55% and then 58%, and the company cited a rebrand and lab-network rationalisation affecting growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the oncology slowdown and is it chemo-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the chemo pricing mechanism with a 30% MRP discount for ECHS and CGHS beneficiaries is the cause; oncology growth fell to about 5% from 23-24%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex guidance and are acquisitions expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth capex is about 50% of EBITDA excluding acquisitions for the 2,000-bed expansion; inorganic deals are being pursued, expected to be in focus clusters, with no details yet.

qa_highlights.question: What are diagnostics margin and growth expectations for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO guided diagnostics revenue growth of about 12-13% and EBITDA margin of 24-25% for the remainder of the year.

532843|2026-09.headline: Fortis Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 17.3% to INR 2,735 crore, with operating EBITDA pre-ESOP up 19.2% to INR 663 crore.
532843|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR 2,735 crore in Q2 FY27, up 17.3% YoY, driven by the hospital business (up 18.6% to INR 2,340 crore). Operating EBITDA pre-ESOP was INR 663 crore at a 24.2% margin, up from 23.9%. Diagnostics (Agilus) grew more slowly at 12.2% on gross revenue, and management said it expects 12-13% growth for FY27. Management declined to guide FY28 margins, citing drug price capping on 137 oncology drugs, and guided FY27 post-ESOP margin to be flat at around 22%.

segments.name: Hospitals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 2,340 crore (+18.6%) and H1 INR 4,527 crore (+18.8%). Occupancy 72% (vs 71%), occupied beds 3,616 (+9%), ARPP INR 2.1 lakh (+6.8%). Renal, neuro and orthopaedics grew 27%, 28% and 30%.

segments.name: Diagnostics (Agilus)
segments.commentary: Gross revenue INR 448 crore (+12.2%); H1 INR 855 crore (+11.2%). Tests processed 11.39 million (+7.2%); patient volume +5.8% YoY. B2C:B2B mix 54:46; wellness revenue +28%, specialised testing +14%.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 190 crore (+12.4%), about 8% of Q2 revenue, flat share versus Q2 FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 hospital EBITDA margin expected to be flattish at around 22% post-ESOP, in line with FY26 (management confirmed post-ESOP basis).
No FY28 margin guidance given; management cited drug price capping circular (137 oncology drugs, effective November) as a negative for profitability, with impact not yet quantifiable.

Diagnostics: Genexus systems being deployed for next-generation sequencing and molecular diagnostics; 4,551 customer touch points at 30 Sep 2026.
demand_pricing: IP volume growth about 13% YoY; ARPP growth of 6.8% driven mainly by case mix (robotics, complex cases), with price contributing about 1.5 percentage points.

Digital revenue +18.6% to 29.5% of hospital revenue; 15 hospitals above 20% EBITDA margin, accounting for 84% of hospital revenue (vs 13 hospitals, 76%).
Around 300 doctors added QoQ; FMRI has no major attrition, with new clinical hires in head and neck, rheumatology and neurology.
Gleneagles O&M (Hyderabad, Chennai) operations almost flat in the first year, with improvement expected next year.
Drug-price capping: oncology drugs about one-third of oncology revenue; impact not yet quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Punjab and Mumbai growing slower, and is Fortis lagging listed peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said Punjab is capacity-constrained, with about 500+ beds coming from Amritsar and Mohali expansions; other clusters are growing fast. He declined to compare with competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Bangalore occupancy low and why buy a small 110-bed hospital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said small community hospitals complement larger flagships in a cluster. Bannerghatta Road is about 58% occupied, and TMI Yeshwanthpur is still ramping up. Suguna was bought via direct negotiation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of the 2,000 beds and the committed capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said the 2,000 beds are completed acquisitions and brownfield expansions, excluding Gleneagles and the 400-bed Delhi greenfield. Committed capex is about INR 3,500 crore over 3-3.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What returns hurdle does Fortis apply to acquisitions, and how is capital funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Board-approved benchmark is IRR of at least 15% and payback within 8-10 years, though strategic factors can override. IHH may take its stake above 50%, which could bring about INR 10,000 crore at current prices; management says capital is not a constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins and guidance be revised given drug-price capping?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said FY27 margin should be flattish at about 22% post-ESOP, with no FY28 guidance until the impact of the drug circular is clear. He reaffirmed that FY29 25% guidance holds if there is no impact.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for diagnostics growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Vijender Singh said FY27 growth is expected at 12-13%, with mid-teens growth in a few quarters, then industry growth. Brand transition impact is largely behind them.

risks_watch: Drug-price capping on 137 oncology drugs (circular effective November): profitability impact not yet quantified; management says oncology drugs are about one-third of oncology revenue.
Forensic audit ordered by court is ongoing; management expects completion within about six months of appointment.
Ramp-up drag from Manesar, People Tree and Bengaluru occupancy; FMRI new block approvals pending.
Diagnostics volume growth (5.3% H1 tests) lags peers; management targets improvement.
Rising debt: net debt INR 2,188 crore, with heavy debt expected this fiscal year; repayment in about two years in a steady state.
Gleneagles O&M contract flat operationally in year one.

532851|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose about 7% to INR2,140 crores while PAT slipped to INR139 crores on a INR9 crore deferred tax charge; Q4 grew about 19%.
532851|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of resilience, with full-year revenue up about 7% to INR2,140 crores, gross profit up about 5% to INR675 crores, and EBITDA up about 3% to INR227 crores. PAT fell slightly from INR142 crores to INR139 crores, which management attributed to a roughly INR9 crore increase in deferred tax. Q4 revenue grew about 19%, with premium products up about 24%, but May was sluggish and the company is waiting for monsoon rains. Management guided to positive top-line and bottom-line growth in FY27, with the first quarter as the first visible test, while raw material inflation of nearly 10% or more supports pricing.

financial_highlights.change: down from INR142 crores; deferred tax up ~INR9 crores
supported by B2C and B2B; premium products ~24%
per CFO; management also cited FY growth above 7%

segments.commentary: Contributed 22% of FY26 sales. Management says B2B held last year's level in April and expects growth in May and the rest of the year.

qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed, saying the company plans from Diwali to Holi and bought stock before the price rise; the benefit depends on converting that stock into sales as the kharif season starts in June.

qa_highlights.answer: Q4 volume grew 5% and value 14%; FY26 volume grew 5% and value 2%.

qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle target is 120 days from 140-150 days, which management called achievable. Management internally targets a 25-30% cut in finance cost; the FY26 consolidated finance cost was INR16.87 crores against INR6.86 crores in FY25, driven by higher inventory, bank limit use and INR94 crores of new-product investment.

qa_highlights.question: How is Kaeros positioned against the Tractor/IIL brand and the partner products?
qa_highlights.answer: Kaeros will run a parallel distribution network with its own brand and a sales-only team. It is positioned as a follower to IIL, which gets first access to partnership products from Corteva, Nissan and OAT. Kaeros is not positioned as a cheaper brand; it will sell at a 2-3% initial discount.

qa_highlights.question: What is the share of premium products and can it reach 70%?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium Maharatna and Focused Maharatna products are 60-63% of B2C. Management targets 60-70% in four years, so 70% will take three to four years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D success rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said success rates vary: about 9,000-10,000 molecules screened a year, with a dozen trial teams testing 500-600 products to yield roughly 10-15 launches. Reverse engineering has higher success rates. The first Indian patent filing is pending IUPAC name approval.

532851|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell 12% YoY to INR612 crore as volume dropped about 13% on a delayed monsoon; gross margin rose to 31.6%.
532851|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations declined 12% YoY to INR612 crore from INR691 crore, with management attributing the drop to a delayed and uneven monsoon and high temperatures that pushed back crop protection demand. Gross profit fell 4% to INR193.16 crore, but gross margin widened from 29% to 31.6%, which management linked to premium mix and inventory effects amid volatile raw material prices. EBITDA margin fell from 12.2% to 11.1% and PAT margin from 8.4% to 7.2%. Management said the season was deferred rather than lost and expects stronger execution over the remaining three quarters, but declined to give revised FY27 targets until after H1.

rows.why: Gross margin rose to 31.6% from 29% (+260bps) on about 2% price/mix, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.1% from 12.2% and management expects Q2 profitability to recover only with sales after August; solvent prices moved 25-30% week to week and price hikes were rolled back.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Sotanala technical plant (INR150 crore) targeted for production by Diwali 2026 and formulation (INR50 crore) around April-May 2027; Dahej new technical plant has 50-60% of equipment utilised with at least INR200 crore potential technical addition.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Volume fell about 13% in Q1 with value up about 2%, but management expects herbicide sales to recover in Q2 with most herbicides above last year's levels and B2B growing faster than B2C; FY27 herbicide 'dream' targets will not be met and no numeric growth target is given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Current projects (Sotanala about INR200 crore, about INR70 crore spent) are under way and maintenance capex is guided at INR30-40 crore per year once they complete; no new capex announcement guided, and no utilisation figure above 80% was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Numeric FY27 revenue targets were withdrawn until the H1 review, Q1 volume fell about 13%, and no significant price increase was realised through July.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Dream FY27 herbicide targets will not be met and Q2 recovery hinges on delayed kharif demand (first half over 60% of annual sales), with solvent and raw-material volatility and Kaeros running at single-digit normalised margins.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Over 40 Kaeros products commercialised, Granuvia crossed about INR5 crore in Q1 and targets about INR20 crore gross for FY27, Spinoace launched late July targeting INR10 crore-plus, and 5-6 molecules transfer to Sotanala in phase 1.

rows.label: Sales returns fall to at least half of last year's INR200 crore
rows.why: Management expects returns to fall to at least half of last year's level, with only one or two herbicides failing and lower placements this year.

rows.label: Inventory decline in Q2 and working capital cycle reduction
rows.why: June inventory was slightly elevated and management expects it to decline sharply in Q2 as the season normalises.

rows.label: Buyback or dividend decision after Q1
rows.why: Company historically buys back every 2-3 years and the decision is deferred until after Q1, with no amount given.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term growth (doubling in 4-5 years, Kaeros, Sotanala) but cautious on FY27, withholding revised targets until after H1 and calling Q1 a setback; analysts pressed on margins, returns and Kaeros economics.

532851|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 8% YoY to INR686 crore on value growth, with volumes down 6-7% and PAT at INR56.17 crore.
532851|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR686 crore, up 8% YoY from INR637 crore, driven by premium mix and price rather than volume. Management said volumes fell about 6-7% due to weak rains and El Nino, with value growth of 4-5%. Gross margin was 33.7% (vs 34.5%), EBITDA INR92.44 crore (13.5% margin) and PAT INR56.17 crore. H1 revenue declined about 2% YoY, with H1 EBITDA at INR161 crore (12.3% margin) and PAT near INR100 crore. Working capital days rose to 158 from 151, and management guided to a volume decline for the full year with H2 improvement in value.

financial_highlights.change: vs 31.7% in H1 FY26, about +100 bps

financial_highlights.value: INR814 crore / INR719 crore / INR533 crore
financial_highlights.change: vs INR744 crore / INR643 crore / INR420 crore a year earlier
vs INR966 crore at 30 Sep 2025 and INR828 crore at 31 Mar 2026

segments.name: Brand / Kaeros
segments.commentary: Kaeros gross brand turnover about INR75 crore in H1; total Kaeros sales about INR114 crore in H1. Target is brand turnover above INR125 crore this fiscal, with standalone Kaeros around INR200 crore and a doubling planned next year.

segments.name: Maharatna / Focused Maharatna / Gold
segments.commentary: Premium Maharatna and Focused Maharatna products are now above 60% of B2C mix, with a target of 70%. Gold products fell as farmers shifted to new-generation products; management said they are not pushed.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Exports are about 5% of revenue, mainly white-label formulations in more than 25 countries. Technical exports are starting, with more than 10 technicals registered and about 15 AIs in work. Long-term target is INR500 crore by five years out.

segments.name: B2B technicals
segments.commentary: B2B sales are above INR400 crore. Domestic portfolio has 28 technicals.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth not expected this fiscal; value growth expected, with H2 improvement from premium mix and pass-through of raw material costs.
Gross margin expected to hold around 33% this year; management aims to match best-in-industry over time, with a typical gain of about 1% a year.
Q3 and Q4 returns expected to be normal; H1 PAT loss not expected to be fully recovered, but H2 expected positive.
Dahej project to be fully capitalised by December 2026 (Q3). Sotanala formulation start targeted April 2027, possibly May; technical manufacturing and full formulation unit next fiscal.
Only 1-2 launches expected this fiscal, with 3-5 launches next fiscal. OAT Agrio product launch likely slips by a few months to next fiscal.
Post Sotanala completion, major capex cycle ends and interest costs normalise, with positive cash flow expected.
capex_capacity: Dahej plant partially in production and partially capitalised; full capitalisation expected in Q3 FY27 after a December shutdown and restart, with utility and electricity gaps fixed.
Sotanala: formulation start targeted April 2027 (possible 1-2 month slip due to NCR gas supply), technical manufacturing and complete formulation unit in FY28.
Planned state-of-the-art DCS plant for CDMO, plus Dahej upgrade for CDMO work at both sites.
Four R&D centres, including Chopanki and Dahej (both NABL), plus a discovery centre in a JV with a Japanese company (Japanese partner funds 80%).
demand_pricing: Volume fell about 6-7% in Q2, with value up 4-5%, as the company sold more premium products; weak rains hit herbicides and granules.
Inflation is visible in agri commodity prices; farmers are moving to premium products and fewer sprays, and farmer profitability is largely intact despite low yields.
Field activity in H1: more than 18,000 farmer meetings, more than 9,000 demonstrations and more than 2.5 lakh farmers met. Around 70 ICS crop-solution plots this year, up from about 30.
Third-party field team ranges from 750 to 1,300-1,400 by season; H2 expected near 750. Kaeros adds about 150 people (70-80 on roll).
Crude oil spiked to about $125 and freight costs rose, pressuring the business; management said the impact is still to be seen in the festive season.
Channel returns were high but lower than last year. Most returns were taken in Q2; Q3 expected to be normal. Secondary visibility is partial (DMS and QR coverage of 15-20%).

qa_highlights.question: What was the volume growth by B2B, B2C and export, and how did Maharatna products perform?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume was negative, down about 6-7%; value grew 4-5%. Gold products fell while Focused Maharatna and Maharatna grew, with Maharatna showing a decent rise in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Will volumes decline for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said this is not a volume-growth year, but value growth is expected, with H2 improvements from a mix of premium products and price pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kaeros outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Kaeros brand turnover is about INR75 crore in H1. The target is above INR125 crore this year, with standalone Kaeros around INR200 crore and a planned doubling next year. The national network is to be complete in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the OAT Agrio launch and the 9(3) registrations?
qa_highlights.answer: No immediate launch this calendar year. The schedule inclusion application is pending CIB inquiry, so the launch could slip a few months. Nissan's new product is due in kharif, followed by 9(3) mixtures.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export strategy and cost competitiveness versus China?
qa_highlights.answer: Shifting from white-label brand exports to technicals, with more than 10 registrations and about 15 AIs in work. CDMO deals are early-stage, mostly with Japanese players. Exports are about 5% of revenue, with a target of INR500 crore in five years.

qa_highlights.question: How much R&D is spent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the R&D expense shown is about INR12 crore, with some trial costs booked under marketing. More than 100 registrations are involved, with about 200 people across IIL and the OIL JV.

risks_watch: Volume decline of 6-7% in Q2 and full-year volume decline; dependence on value growth and price pass-through.
Working capital stretched: inventory INR814 crore and debtors INR719 crore, with NWC near INR1,000 crore; cash flow improvement not yet visible.
Dahej full capitalisation slipped from H1 to Q3; Sotanala timeline could slip further.
Regulatory timing for OAT Agrio and 9(3) products; registrations and schedule inclusion are pending.
Partial secondary-sales visibility (DMS and QR coverage 15-20%) and channel returns.
Crude and freight volatility, El Nino effects, and Kaeros scaling to the targeted INR125 crore brand turnover.
532851|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on premiumisation, Kaeros and CDMO, but cautious on volume and H1 earnings, with management conceding that recovery of the H1 loss is not visible. Several timelines (Dahej, Sotanala, OAT) were pushed back or qualified during the call.
key_quotes: So the volume growth will be down this year. I'll not be able to make it, but I'm very, very sure that there will be value growth, and we'll be able to make some improvements in H2 of this year.
Premiumization and Kaeros expansion will support profitable growth for IIL.
There are more than 55 products which have already hit the market, and there will be a few more.
So the target is to cross INR125 crores of brand turnover in Kaeros.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin guided around 33% for FY27 vs 33.7% in Q2 and 34.5% a year ago, with H1 gross margin up about 100 bps to 32.7%; management targets ~1% a year gain but crude spike and freight pressure are still to show in festive season.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Dahej plant is partly in production and full capitalisation is guided for December 2026 (Q3) after a shutdown; Sotanala formulation start targeted April 2027 (possible 1-2 month slip), so new capacity comes live within the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Volumes fell 6-7% in Q2 and management said full-year volume will decline, with growth coming only from value and premium mix.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue down about 2%, H1 PAT loss not expected to be fully recovered, and volume guided down; only H2 value improvement is expected, so a raise is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Crude at about $125 and rising freight costs are still to hit in the festive season, OAT Agrio may slip a few months, Sotanala may slip 1-2 months on NCR gas supply, and working capital days rose to 158 from 151.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Only 1-2 launches expected this fiscal with 3-5 next fiscal; Nissan's new product is due in kharif and OAT Agrio may slip a few months into next fiscal.

rows.label: Premium mix shift to Maharatna / Focused Maharatna
rows.why: Premium Maharatna and Focused Maharatna are above 60% of B2C mix with a 70% target, and management expects H2 value improvement from premium mix and raw-material pass-through despite 6-7% volume decline.

rows.label: Technical exports and CDMO ramp
rows.why: Exports are about 5% of revenue with more than 10 technicals registered and about 15 AIs in work; INR500 crore target in five years (40-50% CAGR) but CDMO deals are early-stage.

rows.label: Working capital release
rows.why: Working capital days rose to 158 from 151 and NWC is about INR1,000 crore vs INR966 crore a year earlier, with inventory INR814 crore and debtors INR719 crore; cash flow improvement not yet visible.

tone.note: Management was confident on premiumisation, Kaeros and CDMO, but cautious on volumes, H1 earnings and timelines, with Dahej and OAT Agrio pushed back; analysts probed volume trends, Maharatna mix and the Kaeros and export targets.

532853|2026-03.headline: Asahi Songwon Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 30.2% YoY to Rs 23 crore, with margin at 15.6% on price pass-through in Blue pigments.
532853|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was Rs 144 crore, up 19.4% QoQ, with EBITDA of Rs 23 crore (15.6% margin vs 8.58% in Q3 and 11.53% in Q4 FY25) and PAT of Rs 10.82 crore. For FY26, revenue fell 4.78% to Rs 535.48 crore while PAT rose 5.48% to Rs 17.78 crore. Management attributed the margin recovery mainly to raw-material price pass-through and operational efficiencies in Blue pigments, with a small inventory gain, and said the API price decline of the prior three years has reversed. Gokul Jaykrishna handed day-to-day CEO duties to his son Arjun Jaykrishna, while remaining Managing Director.

segments.name: Blue pigment (standalone, ATC Dahej)
segments.commentary: Revenue and profitability improved QoQ on stronger realisation with modest volume growth. Gross margin rose to about 34% from about 29% QoQ; management cited price pass-through, operating efficiencies and a marginal inventory gain. Management said utilisation is about 80-85% and no capex is planned for capacity.

segments.name: AZO pigments (subsidiary ATC)
segments.commentary: Full-year EBITDA positive and cash break-even reached. FY26 revenue Rs 78 crore with PBT loss of Rs 2.42 crore; management expects PBT break-even in FY27. Capacity is 2,400 tpa, utilisation about 65% per management, with a planned Rs 10-15 crore brownfield expansion to about 1.5x once utilisation reaches 75-85%.

segments.name: API (subsidiary Atlas, Chattral plant)
segments.commentary: Full-year EBITDA positive. Volumes grew about 18% CAGR over three years, but realisations fell 40-45% since acquisition; Pregabalin prices are about 15% above the bottom. Pregabalin is 60-70% of API business. Chattral intermediates run at about 60-70% and finished APIs at about 30%. Q4 API revenue was reported as about Rs 30 crore with EBIT of about 10%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q1 FY27 EBITDA across all three segments to at least maintain Q4 FY26 margins, with an aim to improve.

Blue standalone: management said peak EBITDA of about Rs 50-55 crore is the goal for FY27 if prices hold, on about Rs 400 crore revenue at 13-14% margin (analyst's framing, accepted as a goal, not a formal guide).

Long-term margin targets: about 13% EBITDA for AZO and 15-16% for API; Mitesh Patel said Chattral and Atlas could reach Rs 250-280 crore turnover at peak with no capex, at 15-16% EBITDA margin within 2-3 years.
CEP certification for Pregabalin expected by end of FY27 (current financial year), seen as a driver of volume and export access.
Management aims for Rs 1,000 crore group revenue within the next few years, with priority on sustaining revenue first.
capex_capacity: AZO capacity 2,400 tpa; brownfield expansion of about Rs 10-15 crore (plant and machinery only) to lift capacity to about 1.5x, triggered at 75-85% utilisation, expected within 3-4 quarters and funded by internal accruals.
Blue: no capex planned for capacity; incremental gains expected from debottlenecking and efficiency projects.
Chattral: intermediates about 60-70% utilised; finished API utilisation about 30%, which management sees as the key lever for fixed-asset turnover.
Peak debt was Rs 220 crore after the completed four-year capex cycle; debt is falling faster than internal estimates.
demand_pricing: Blue pricing is set quarterly with MNC customers; Q4 benefit was partly locked in, so further benefit expected in Q1 and Q2. Mitesh Patel put the price increase at about 20%, and management said prices across pigments and crude rose meaningfully on raw-material tightness.
Management said China raised prices about 30-40% due to lower export incentives and VAT rebates, roughly doubled ocean freight and higher crude-linked raw material costs.

US tariffs hit AZO and Blue exports, including via India-made value-added products; US business has revived since tariffs eased but has not returned to normal. AZO export customers have restarted testing.
Management said Europe remains in a structural slowdown; India remains the main AZO growth market.
Management says the cyclical slowdown appears to be bottoming, and no new pigment capacity is expected in the industry.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA gain came from raw-material price pass-through, and does it reverse if raw material prices fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun Jaykrishna said the strategy was to pass through as much raw-material inflation as possible via long-term supplier and customer relationships. He did not quantify the split and said revenue was under pressure while the bottom line held.

qa_highlights.question: Blue gross margin rose from about 29% to 34% QoQ. Is there inventory gain, and how do margins return to 35-38%?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun said margins reflect internal strategy, some inventory addition, and operating efficiencies. Gokul Jaykrishna later put the inventory gain as marginal, since the company held finished goods bought before the war.

qa_highlights.question: Did the Blue power and fuel cost fall to under 5% of sales in Q4 because of a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun said a one-time receipt of renewable-energy billing rebate, pending for two years, drove the drop. Management expects power and fuel as a percentage of sales to be lower than before but not at Q4 levels every quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is AZO FY26 revenue and PBT, and will it break even in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Nupur (company) said FY26 AZO revenue was Rs 78 crore and PBT was Rs (-2.42) crore. Management said it expects PBT break-even in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone Blue utilisation and possible FY27 EBITDA of Rs 50-55 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Gokul Jaykrishna corrected the analyst's 60% figure, saying Blue runs at about 80-85%. He called Rs 50-55 crore peak potential and the goal for FY27. Mitesh Patel put Blue price increases at about 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Subsidiaries: peak revenue and EBITDA potential at Atlas and Chattral?
qa_highlights.answer: Mitesh Patel said the two facilities can reach Rs 250-280 crore turnover at peak with no capex and 15-16% EBITDA margin within 2-3 years. Arjun said API EBITDA depends on pricing, and management said the subsidiaries could reach about Rs 50 crore EBITDA at peak.

risks_watch: Q4 margin gains were partly one-off: a renewable-energy rebate lowered Blue power and fuel costs, and an inventory gain contributed. Q1 FY27 is the test.
Pricing is volatile: management says there is no stability in prices or the business environment; a reversal of raw-material inflation could compress margins.
API utilisation at Chattral finished products is about 30%, and the company has not yet hired senior business development or marketing leadership; a senior hire is expected in the next quarter.
FY26 consolidated revenue fell 4.78% and EBITDA 6.12%; FY26 net margin about 3.3%. AZO and API are still loss-making or marginal, so consolidation depends on Blue.
CEP certification for Pregabalin (targeted by end FY27) and AZO export approvals in the US and Europe remain unconfirmed timelines.
Leadership transition: Gokul Jaykrishna stepped down as CEO and Arjun Jaykrishna took over as CEO.
532853|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on Q4 and the Blue business, but cautious on the subsidiaries and the wider market. Management was candid that AZO and API margins are far from targets and that the environment is volatile, and it avoided quantifying the inventory gain, the price pass-through split and the Blue revenue mix. Some answers were loose or corrected on the call.
key_quotes: The strategy and implementation we have been working on is going to strongly position us in the Blue business to continue to perform at a good level in the coming quarters and year as well.

So, the crude and the Pigment, I think both would be subs tantial contributors and they will be in the coming future, but I will request, if it is okay, that we do not share the exact breakup just for business.
The API business has delivered consistent volumetric growth continuously of 3 years.
We are far from that. And we need to make serious strategic decisions as well as good business operational moves to reach this.

532856|2026-09.headline: Time Technoplast Q2 FY27 consolidated net sales rose 32% to INR1,996 crore, with record quarterly EBITDA of INR265 crore and PAT of INR146 crore.
532856|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 net sales were about INR1,996 crore versus INR1,512 crore, EBITDA INR265 crore versus INR224 crore and PAT INR146 crore versus INR115 crore, all described by management as record quarterly highs. H1 FY27 net sales were INR3,690 crore (up 29%), EBITDA INR490 crore (up 17%) and PAT INR262 crore (up 25%), with volume growth of 13%. Growth was inflated by polymer pass-through pricing, with management citing a 20-25 day lag in passing raw material changes to customers. Management reiterated 15% volume growth guidance, announced a merger of subsidiary TPL Plastech into the parent, and updated on capex, non-core asset sales and acquisitions.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1,512 crore in Q2 FY26 (about +32%)
Net debt reduced by INR96 crore

segments.name: Composite products (LPG, CNG, hydrogen, fire extinguisher)
segments.commentary: Management cited about INR400-430 crore composite revenue in H1 FY27 and guides 25-30% growth. Order book of about INR210 crore; INR83 crore PSU order for Type 4 CNG cascades and INR2.5 crore NTPC hydrogen order secured.

segments.name: Value-added products
segments.commentary: Segment growth of 29% in H1 FY27; value-added is 29% of sales and established products 71%.

segments.name: Industrial packaging (drums, jerrycans, pails, IBC)
segments.commentary: Confirmed domestic and international orders of INR375 crore for the current calendar year; guidance 11-13% growth (about 12% average).

segments.name: PE/PP pipes
segments.commentary: Guidance 20-25% growth. Management says H1 is seasonally about 35-40% of pipe business; execution slowed in July-September due to rains and government payment and price-revision delays.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: India 64% and overseas 36% of sales. MENA 11%, Southeast Asia 18%, USA 9% of consolidated revenue. Overseas capacity utilisation about 86%; Middle East business down about 25% but offset by Far East and USA.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth guidance of at least 15% year on year for the next 3 years; management says the FY27 target is 15%.
With 15% volume growth, EBITDA growth is expected above 20% and PAT growth above 25%.
Segment growth guidance: packaging 11-13%, composites 25-30%, pipes 20-25%, others 10-12%.

Net capex about INR375 crore; after realising INR134 crore of non-core assets (INR18 crore done in H1), net capex about INR250 crore. Post FY27, capex limited to maintenance plus brownfield up to INR250 crore.

Automation and consolidation targeted to lift annual ROCE by 1.5-2%; EBITDA margin benefit of about 1% from power and manpower savings in FY28, and a further 1.5-5% from unit consolidation (management indicated 13% could reach about 15.5% next year).
Green power PPAs: about INR11 crore benefit this year, expected INR22-25 crore next year.
Composite market sizing: INR800-900 crore this year, INR2,500 crore in 3 years and INR4,000 crore in 5 years (management's estimate).
capex_capacity: Morai (Gujarat) composite plant completed and PESO approvals obtained; about 1,25,000 sq ft area taken to consolidate equipment from Daman and Silvassa. Management says expansion takes 6-8 months.
Indian capacity utilisation about 83%, overseas about 86%. Management says expansion is considered when utilisation reaches 90% for 6 months.
Automation of plants (INR75 crore identified, orders placed); 6 manufacturing locations consolidated last year, 6-7 more under review.
Systoverse Private Limited acquisition completed; business to start next month.
Ebullient Packaging acquisition dropped for now due to the war situation and under-performance; to be reviewed in 2-3 years. INR220 crore of QIP proceeds still pending for this acquisition.

TPL Plastech (75% owned subsidiary, drums/jerrycans/IBC) to merge into parent, effective 1 April 2026, subject to approvals. IBC manufacturing started at its Bhuj unit with potential of INR100 crore in 3 years.
14.2 kg LPG cylinder development delayed 3-4 months due to supply conditions; 250-350 litre hydrogen and CNG cylinder development in progress.
demand_pricing: Polymer prices rose through August and September on feedstock costs; management says pass-through to customers happens with a 20-25 day lag, and about 60% of inputs come from local producers.
Revenue growth (32%) well ahead of volume growth (13%) because of pass-through of polymer price increases.
LPG: OMCs (IOC, BPCL, HPCL) offer new connections only in composite cylinders due to steel-cylinder suspension; repeat orders from HPCL and other gas distributors at unchanged prices.
CNG cascades: strong CGD network expansion demand; Type 4 cascades cited as more efficient for CGD networks.

Pipes: government contract pricing and payment delays hurt Q2; management says EPC contractors are now receiving revised state prices and mentions a 30-40% polymer price increase that the company has not fully passed through.
Hydrogen: demand still developing; management expects clarity on hydrogen demand in mid to end 2027.

qa_highlights.question: How should capacity and capex over the next two years be viewed given the Morai plant and IBC completion, and is 15% volume growth safe?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed 15% as the minimum growth rate for the next 2 years, with composites at 25-30%. Morai was completed and PESO approvals obtained. Management said INR1,250 crore capex would support INR5,000 crore composite revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What incremental savings come from consolidation and solar, and could margin reach 15.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a payback under 4 years on automation, and under 1.5 years on the power PPA. Expected EBITDA benefit is about 1% from power and manpower in FY28, plus a 1.5-5% margin uplift from consolidation, with a 7.5-10% productivity gain at consolidated units. Management said the path to about 15.5% is plausible.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving composite growth, and is it product mix, exports or channel?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Type 4 PESO-approved cylinders, first Type 3 and Type 4 hydrogen cylinders in India, reach across LPG, CNG, hydrogen, SCBA and oxygen, and automotive supply capacity now available. 532867|2026-06.headline: V2 Retail Q1 FY27 revenue rose 58% YoY to INR997 crore, with PAT up 70% to INR41.9 crore and store count at 381.

532867|2026-09.headline: V2 Retail Q2 FY27 revenue rose 28% to INR905.6 crores on volume growth, but SSSG was -14.9% reported and mgmt cut FY27 SSSG view to 5-7%.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q3 be the best quarter ever and what is the margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed Q3 will be the best quarter ever in revenue and profitability. Full-year pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin should be above 7.5%, with H2 at least 8% versus about 7% in H1.

risks_watch: Reported SSSG of -14.9% in Q2 and H1 calendar SSSG of -3.7%; demand slowed in the last three months per management, with no single cause identified.
Working capital: inventory of INR1,447.8 crores, net working capital 88 days vs 81 days, and borrowings up to INR528 crores; normalisation targeted for March 2027 (75-80 days).
Store productivity: new stores at about 35-40% lower PSF than mature stores; management has stretched the maturity period for FY25 cohorts to 2.5-3.5 years.
Q3 festive and winter season is the test: October flat period-to-period; management will reassess store openings at end-Q3.
Depreciation rising sharply (INR68 crores vs INR37 crores) and expected to keep rising in Q3 and Q4 as store base grows.
Creditor days to fall to 45-65 days from 65-70 as cash is used for early vendor payments.
Input cost inflation of 3-7%; further price increases possible if raw material costs rise; V2Kart e-commerce still at pilot stage in 2 states.
Governance/disclosure: an analyst raised repeatedly the non-disclosure of the core senior team (6-7 people) and mature-store SSSG for H1; management committed to share in a future presentation.

532868|2026-03.headline: DLF posted a record FY26 collection of over INR 13,500 crore (+15% YoY) and zero gross debt in development, with FY26 sales bookings of INR 20,143 crore in line with guidance.
532868|2026-03.overview: Management reported a strong close to FY26, citing record collections of over INR 13,500 crore (+15%) and cash surplus of over INR 7,700 crore (+25%). FY26 sales bookings were INR 20,143 crore, in line with guidance despite deferral of a couple of launches, with Q4 sales of about INR 3,967 crore led by Dahlias. Q4 consolidated revenue was about INR 2,452 crore with reported net profit of INR 1,256 crore; FY26 net profit was INR 4,256 crore (+16%). The rental business shows a 95% occupancy portfolio of 50 million sq ft and a 4-5 year NOI growth guidance of mid-teens, with 20-25% CAGR on a longer basis. Management steered the Q&A away from presales volume toward margins and cash flows.

segments.name: Rental (annuity) business
segments.commentary: Rental portfolio of 50 million sq ft at 95% occupancy; FY26 NOI growth of about 34-35% driven by assets completed late FY25 reaching full lease. Non-SEZ office occupancy 98-99%, SEZ 88-89%, and income loss from vacancy down to ~3.5%.

segments.name: Development (DevCo)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales of INR 20,143 crore; Dahlias sales about INR 5,000 crore in FY26, guided to INR 5,000-6,000 crore in FY27. Management targets ~INR 9,000-10,000 crore of margin creation and INR 7,000-8,000 crore of DevCo FCF annually.

segments.name: Retail malls
segments.commentary: Existing mall income expected to grow 10-11% in FY27, plus three new malls. Midtown Plaza 95% leased and operational; Summit Plaza 95-97% leased, opening likely second half of July; Promenade Goa 50% leasing line of sight, completion around August.

segments.name: Office (Atrium Place, Downtown)
segments.commentary: Atrium Place (JV with Hines, 3.2 million sq ft) fully leased; three towers have OC and fourth tower OC expected Q2 FY27, generating ~INR 700 crore rent. Downtown Taramani 3.5 million sq ft ~500,000 sq ft leased, completion expected Q2 FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales guidance of ~INR 20,000 crore maintained; management said upside possible if demand stays strong.
Annual margin creation of ~INR 9,000 crore guided to continue.
Rental NOI guidance: mid-teens growth in NOI and 20-25% CAGR over the next 4-5 years, though management cautioned FY26's 34-35% growth should not be extrapolated.
FY27 exit rental of ~INR 8,200 crore across DCCDL and the rest of DLF assets combined.
Launch pipeline of almost INR 20,000 crore for FY27, including a large DLF City launch (INR 8,000-9,000 crore or higher), Arbour Senior Living, Westpark next phase, Dahlias, and possibly Goa.
Dividend: no formal guidance given; ~two-thirds of dividend is funded by Cyber City's dividend to DLF.
Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 (Towers 5-8) completion late FY28/early FY29; Taramani completion Q2 FY28.

Downtown Taramani 3.5 million sq ft: completion expected Q2 FY28; central atrium design change made.

Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2: 7.5 million sq ft integrated development (2 million sq ft mall, 5.5 million sq ft offices); Tower 7 (2.2 million sq ft) nearly fully leased; Towers 5 and 6 being leased; finishing late FY28/early FY29; iconic tower construction to start in ~2.5 years.
Westpark Mumbai pipeline above 5 million sq ft; ~900,000 sq ft launched so far, next phase of ~800,000 sq ft in FY27, then 500,000-600,000 sq ft.

demand_pricing: Dahlias (super luxury, Gurugram): 32 apartments sold in Q4 plus 2 Camellias; per-unit prices now ~INR 90-110 crore for the first phase units vs ~INR 60-75 crore at launch. Dahlias per sq ft pricing is about INR 1 lakh on super area vs Camellias ~INR 1.2 lakh (INR 80-150 crore per unit).
Office SEZ rentals: gap to Cyber City rentals narrowed to 10-12% for new take-up; Cyber City vacancy lowest in SEZ portfolio; Hyderabad SEZ vacancy 17-20%.
Chennai Taramani top-floor leases at INR 145-150 per sq ft; average realisation expected INR 125-130 per sq ft.

Management flagged that large tenants are reviewing internal processes, which could defer leasing decisions, though no portfolio impact so far; cited AI and Iran-US war as factors but said there was no impact yet.
Management declined to chase presales volume, saying margins and cash flows are the priority; said presales of INR 50,000 crore a year are possible given land bank.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the medium-term launch pipeline shown as ~INR 60,000 crore versus INR 67,000 crore earlier, and is the company less confident about the market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the figure is a status update on a INR 1,14,000 crore 5-year launch pipeline announced ~2 years ago; launches are paced to market absorption and execution capacity, with further phases identified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 launch and presales plan given the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Aakash Ohri said the pipeline is ~INR 20,000 crore, including a DLF City launch of INR 8,000-9,000 crore or more, Arbour Senior Living, Westpark next phase, Dahlias, and possibly Goa (approvals in place but a PIL pending).

qa_highlights.question: Why is presales growth limited to ~INR 20,000 crore versus peers at INR 30,000-35,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Tyagi said presales is not the right metric and the company is chasing margins and cash flows; it could do INR 50,000 crore a year if chosen, with delivery capability the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the FY27 presales is expected from Dahlias and how much from the launch pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Dahlias sales were about INR 5,000 crore in FY26 and are expected at INR 5,000-6,000 crore in FY27; management expects INR 13,000-14,000 crore to come from the ~INR 20,000 crore launch pipeline, as not all launches will sell out at launch.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the INR 11,200 crore in RERA escrow accounts and the cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Badal Bagri said the RERA cash unlocks from FY27-28; uses are shareholder returns, DLF rental capex (committed), and opportunistic margin-accretive land deals. Revenue recognition is on completed-contract method, with large projects like Arbour delivering from FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the dividend sustainable and how is it funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Tyagi said about two-thirds of the dividend comes from Cyber City's dividend to DLF, and no dividend guidance is being offered, though the trajectory has been of continuing growth.

Dahlias sell-out and per-sq ft price trajectory is a key driver of FY27 presales; management admitted Dahlias pricing has moved fast.
Rising brokerage and overhead costs in Q4 linked to collections and year-end provisioning; management said full-year overheads should stay around current levels.
