532868|2026-06.headline: DLF Q1 FY27 net profit rose to INR 794 crore (from INR 766 crore) while pre-sales were muted at INR 657 crore amid Aureva launch deferment.
532868|2026-06.overview: DLF reported a resilient Q1 FY27 with collections of INR 2,406 crore, operating cash flow above INR 1,300 crore and net cash of INR 15,200 crore, of which close to INR 11,000 crore sits in RERA escrow accounts. Pre-sales were INR 657 crore, held back by the deferred Aureva senior living launch awaiting approvals and a deliberate pacing of Dahlias sales. Rental revenue was INR 1,605 crore with EBITDA of INR 476 crore, and occupancy stayed above 95% by space and 97% by value. DCCDL posted revenue up 10% YoY to INR 1,917 crore and PAT of INR 717 crore, up over 20%, though this included one-time tax entries. Management said FY28 would be the reporting inflection as large projects begin contributing under completed-contract accounting.

segments.name: Office rentals
segments.commentary: Vacancy is very low; newer assets Cyber Park, Atrium Place, Downtown Gurgaon and Downtown Chennai are nearly 100% leased. Rentals in the portfolio grew about 8.5%-9% from Q1 FY26.

segments.name: Retail malls
segments.commentary: Midtown Plaza is fully operational, about 85% open and 96%-97% leased; Summit Plaza had a soft launch and is about 90% leased; Goa mall has OC, is 64% leased as of 31 July, and is targeted to open late 2026 or early 2027. Retail spend grew about 13.5%-14%.

segments.name: Residential (Dahlias, Golf Links)
segments.commentary: Dahlias is about 65% sold with 34 units sold in the quarter; price realisation is above INR 1 lakh per sq ft, reaching INR 1.20-1.25 lakh on higher floors, with entry ticket above INR 100 crore.

segments.name: Data centres
segments.commentary: DLF will act only as real estate developer and builder for data centres, not own technology or operate them; Data Center 3 in Noida expected to add rental around March-April 2027.

guidance_outlook: FY28 expected to be the reporting inflection point as large projects starting with Arbour contribute to P&L under completed-contract accounting.
Management hopes to stick to broad FY27 sales guidance; Goa residential shortfall would be about 10% of the INR 20,000 crore guidance and is expected to be covered.

CAM costs rose about 2%-2.5% due to minimum wage revisions; no tenant pushback reported because CAM is audited annually and passed through.
Pre-sales pacing for Dahlias to be held until Experience Centre opens after Diwali; next Privana phase expected early 2027 as a high-rise scheme.

qa_highlights.question: Is the slowdown in Dahlias sustenance sales (34 units vs typical 12-15 units per quarter) deliberate?
qa_highlights.answer: Aakash Ohri said the pace was consciously managed around the Experience Centre opening after Diwali; Dahlias is about 65% sold and entry ticket is now above INR 100 crore, with some additional sales held back pending paperwork.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Goa residential launch slip without hurting the INR 20,000 crore sales guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Tyagi said Goa accounted for only a couple of thousand crore, about 10% of guidance, and that the gap should be covered comfortably; all Goa approvals are in hand but the PIL is being addressed before taking customer payments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the stabilised run-rate of group rental income and what ramp-up remains?
qa_highlights.answer: Sriram Khattar said Midtown and Summit Plaza reach steady state by Q4 FY27, Goa by May-June 2027, and Atrium Place Tower 1 adds a full tower after its September OC; exit FY27 group rentals guided at INR 7,300-7,500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: When will Cyber City 2 and the next commercial pipeline start?
qa_highlights.answer: Sriram Khattar said Cyber City 2 (70-80 acres) sizing and launch remain undecided with a decision expected within the next year; construction in Hyderabad or Cyber City is planned for sometime next year.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about Dahlias sales velocity versus price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Aakash Ohri said about 3.5 years of sales were achieved in 15-16 months, with roughly 3 years remaining; Ashok Tyagi said there is no direct binary between velocity and price, and the next phase depends on physical and commercial progress, implying a 3-year cycle.

532868|2026-09.headline: DLF Q2 FY27 booked INR 3,800 crore sales and reported INR 2,298 crore revenue, aided by a one-time INR 738 crore fair-value gain in other income.

Management said accounting revenue remains back-ended under completed-contract accounting until the pre-Arbour projects complete in FY28. 532884|2026-03.headline: Refex Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA rose to INR141 crore (20.1% margin) and PAT to INR94 crore, driven by Ash & Coal Handling and wind turbine deliveries.
532884|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 standalone continuing-operations revenue of INR701 crore (+18% YoY) with EBITDA of INR141 crore versus INR62 crore a year earlier, and PAT of INR94 crore (+67%). For FY26, revenue fell to INR2,039 crore from INR2,259 crore as the company exited Power Trading and Refrigerant Gas, while EBITDA rose 68% to INR350 crore (17.2% margin) and PAT reached INR247 crore. Wind turbine deliveries began in February 2026 and contributed about INR233 crore in Q4. The demerger of the mobility business is awaiting NCLT hearing, with management guiding to completion in roughly 60 to 90 days.

Initial phase of execution; FY26 wind execution INR238 crore
Excluding discontinued trading revenue; reported segment revenue about INR2,000 crore

segments.name: Ash & Coal Handling
segments.commentary: Q4 segment revenue cited as about INR690 crore; order pipeline about INR1,500 crore including new long-term contracts (e.g., APGENCO 3-year order). Current throughput 68,000 to 70,000 tonnes per day versus earlier guidance of 90,000 to 95,000.

segments.name: Wind (Venwind Refex Power)
segments.commentary: Order book about INR1,860 crore with INR238 crore executed in FY26; management expects to execute the balance (about INR1,500 crore) in FY27. Current EBITDA margin about 8%; 5.3 MW platform; ALMM approval received; capacity target about 2 GW by next year-end.

segments.name: Mobility (EV)
segments.commentary: Crossed INR100 crore revenue in its third year of operation; being demerged via NCLT scheme, with the company stating all its compliances are complete. Shift to asset-light model with clean fuel and enterprise focus.

segments.name: Discontinued: Power Trading and Refrigerant Gas
segments.commentary: Management says it has fully exited Power Trading and liquidated refrigerant gas stock; part of a receivable is still pending and expected to close in the current quarter. Trading revenue reduction of about INR220 crore cited.

Wind localization is a 1 to 2 year journey expected to improve margins; no margin number given.
demand_pricing: Management says the company is India's largest ash-handling player; second-largest estimated at about 25% of Refex's size; fragmented peers working at 1 to 5 plants each.
Management estimates market share around 3% of a roughly INR75,000 crore TAM and aspires to reach double-digit share over several years.

Receivable days guided at 105 to 125 days standalone; wind receivables are short-cycle because they are backed by LCs.
Contract assets (unbilled revenue) were above INR700 crore; management describes it as a running account that is not expected to fall sharply.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said all orders are disclosed; some long-term orders such as APGENCO (3-year) were added at the start of the year and were not reflected in the figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook after the 20% Q4 print?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will be around the same, with a sustainable 15% to 18% range; the 11% to 12% prior guidance referred to net profit, not EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wind EBITDA margin and FY27 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Current wind EBITDA margin about 8%, expected to stay at similar levels; FY27 wind revenue to rise sharply versus FY26's INR238 crore as the INR1,500 crore balance is executed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the promoter pledge increase to 41%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pledges are released on loan closure, with payments made monthly; a large part expected to be removed over about 6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a financial or reputational impact from the IT search?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all disclosures were made at each stage and it sees no challenge from the IT matter for the company.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the warrant subscription not taken up and how will funding be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called non-subscription a deliberate decision; it said there is sufficient cash, bank limits and internal accruals, and no immediate fundraise planned.

532884|2026-06.headline: Refex Q1 FY27 standalone continuing revenue rose 76% YoY to INR619 crore, with EBITDA of INR105 crore (17% margin) and PAT of INR73.6 crore (+123%).
532884|2026-06.overview: Standalone continuing-operations revenue grew 76% YoY to INR619 crore and EBITDA rose to INR105 crore at a 17% margin, while PAT reached INR73.6 crore (11.9% margin). Ash and coal handling remained the largest contributor despite acute diesel shortages and logistics disruptions linked to geopolitical developments. Wind turbine execution started contributing INR295 crore in the quarter at near-zero margin, and the mobility demerger is progressing toward a shareholder meeting next month.

financial_highlights.metric: One-time bank processing charges (loan takeover by Indian Overseas Bank)

segments.name: Ash and coal handling
segments.commentary: Largest contributor to revenue and profit; volume run rate of 65,000-70,000 tonnes per day in Q1, with management targeting close to 90,000 by Q4 FY27 (some remarks cited 75,000-80,000 by Q4). Q2 expected to be slower, Q3-Q4 to scale up. Management guides EBITDA margin of 15-18% and net margin of 10-12%.

segments.name: Wind energy
segments.commentary: Q1 execution INR295 crore at near-zero margin; order book INR1,860 crore of which INR525 crore executed and INR1,300 crore remaining. FY27 execution guided at INR1,700-1,800 crore with 5-6% net margin targeted by year-end. Operates as a product supplier (turbine, tower, blades) with a 76-77% stake in the JV.

segments.name: Mobility (Refex Mobility)
segments.commentary: Asset-light premium corporate mobility; being demerged into a separate listed company. NCLT has approved convening shareholder and creditor meetings, with equity shareholder meeting scheduled for next month. Expected to exit discontinued operations by end of Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Refrigerant gas
segments.commentary: Fully discontinued as of the last quarter; part of discontinued operations.

guidance_outlook: Ash and coal handling run rate to reach close to 90,000 tonnes per day in Q4 FY27; Q2 to be slower, Q3-Q4 to pick up; management says the core business will maintain a CAGR at least as good as last year's (~28%).
Wind FY27 execution of INR1,700-1,800 crore; net margin 5-6% by end of FY27 and profitability by year-end; Q3-Q4 margins expected to improve as unbilled material gets billed.
Wind localisation: management expects about 85% of components localised within 12 months, with margins similar to the core business in about 2 years; blades to be made in-house.
Mobility demerger expected to be completed with discontinued operations gone by end of Q3 FY27.
Wind orders in advanced closure expected within 30-60 days; new orders would spill over into FY28.
capex_capacity: Silvassa wind assembly plant is leased; capex to date limited to about INR3.5-4 crore of repairs and maintenance; rated capacity about 1 GW, which management equates to roughly INR5,000-6,000 crore of revenue.
First 5.3 MW turbine erected by a customer at Koppal, Karnataka; management says it is operating as projected and a repeat order is possible.
Blades currently imported; localisation under way, with in-house blade manufacturing planned.
Ash handling capacity not a constraint per management; scaling depends on multiplying fleet and manpower. Working in 42 thermal power plants, about 30-35% of Indian TPPs.
Railway Rail-cum-Road (RCR) initiative started, with freight discounts opening Northeast routes.
demand_pricing: Ash handling realisation varies from INR450 to INR1,200 per tonne-km, driven mainly by distance and volume.
Ash handling order book INR1,635 crore; management says digital tender wins in the past four months should improve the Q4 order book.
Wind order book INR1,860 crore; management says large orders are expected this year, at least as big as last year.
Management welcomes new entrants in ash handling, arguing they expand awareness and market; says Refex is the only organised player.
Wind market tailwinds cited from hybrid renewables (wind, solar, storage) and the 100 GW by 2030 government ambition. Exports ruled out; focus is domestic only.

qa_highlights.question: What was the ash and coal handling volume run rate and the Q4 target?
qa_highlights.answer: 65,000-70,000 tonnes per day in Q1; target close to 90,000 by Q4 FY27 (also cited as crossing 75,000-80,000).

qa_highlights.question: Why is wind margin near zero in Q1 and what is the full-year margin target?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-operating and business development expenses were expensed; part of material is in transit and unbilled. Management targets 5-6% net margin (PAT) for the year, with better margins in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin guidance for ash handling, given conflicting statements?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it always guides EBITDA margin of 15-18% and net margin of 10-12%; Q1 EBITDA margin was 17%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wind order book and outlook for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: INR1,860 crore in hand, of which INR525 crore executed; INR1,300 crore to be executed in FY27. New orders would spill into FY28; growth expected to be very good, with no quantified figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a pledge reduction trajectory for promoter shares?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pledge was reduced last month, another disclosure due within 15 days, with further releases expected within two weeks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wind JV structure and technology arrangement?
qa_highlights.answer: Refex holds about 76-77%, the JV partner 23%; technology was transferred directly for payment, and the partner runs operations. Management did not disclose the partner's equity infusion on the call.

qa_highlights.question: How is the mobility demerger affecting P&L and capital allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Discontinued operations to end by Q3 FY27; the mobility entity will be listed separately via mirror shareholding. Capital allocation will be based on need, with wind capital requirements likely at entity level through working capital or term loans.

risks_watch: Diesel supply shortages and logistics disruptions from geopolitical developments affected operations; management said most of the impact was covered.
Wind segment margin only just breaks even in Q1; delivery of the 5-6% net margin target depends on Q3-Q4 billing of in-transit material.
Q2 FY27 volume seasonality in ash handling; ramp to 90,000 tonnes per day depends on fleet and manpower additions.

Promoter pledge reduction ongoing; management plans further disclosures in about 15 days.
Management gave inconsistent statements on wind margin basis (net vs PAT) and on Q4 run rate targets, which should be clarified in the next filing.
key_quotes: Target is there to close to 90,000.
Yes, it is a net margin, Sudhir bhai.
Margin is close to the same only, Sudhir -ji.

rows.why: NCLT has approved the shareholder and creditor meetings, with the equity shareholder meeting next month, and management expects discontinued operations to be gone by end of Q3 FY27.

532884|2026-09.headline: Refex Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 36% YoY to INR560 crore and PAT 13% to INR60 crore, despite monsoon-hit ash volumes.
532884|2026-09.overview: Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue from continuing operations was INR560 crore (up 36% YoY) with EBITDA of INR91 crore (16% margin, up 22%) and PAT of INR60 crore (up 13%). H1 FY27 revenue was INR1,179 crore (up 55%) and PAT INR133 crore (up 55%). Management attributed the weak Q2 volumes to monsoon disruption in ash handling, and said wind execution and the new RMC and green mobility businesses are at early stages. The demerger of green mobility awaits NCLT final approval, with the next hearing on 11 November 2026.

segments.name: Ash & Coal Handling (core)
segments.commentary: Q2 volumes were weak at about 35,000-40,000 tonnes due to monsoon, with volume recovering into H2. Management guides 20-25% revenue growth for FY27 and FY28, and a Q4 target of 90,000 tonnes.

segments.name: Wind energy (turbine equipment)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR201 crore and EBITDA INR11.32 crore after a loss in Q1. Order book is about INR1,100-1,200 crore; FY27 execution guided at INR1,300-1,400 crore, with margins of 4-5% EBITDA and 2.5-3% PAT.

segments.name: Ready-mix concrete (new)
segments.commentary: Pune plant (Charholi) started operations on 25 September 2026 (management also says 1 October); Hoskote and Kalyan followed. Asset-light lease model, 60 cum/hour capacity, with about 4,000-4,500 cum/month expected from Pune.

segments.name: Green mobility
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR36 crore with first positive EBITDA of INR1.3 crore. Management targets PAT-level profitability within a year; demerger into a separately listed company is pending NCLT approval.

Standalone EBITDA margin guided at 15-18%.

qa_highlights.question: Wind order pipeline and timing of closure?
qa_highlights.answer: Final price negotiation for a large-volume order; closure expected in 30-45 days, with management saying the quantum is substantial and will be announced. Existing wind order book is about INR1,100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Does the RMC business have margin potential and competitive edge over cement players?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited UltraTech and RDC Concrete earning about 10% profit on RMC; expects better margins through zero-capex, tech-driven operations. RMC is expected to contribute meaningfully from FY28; FY27 is set-up year.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and receivables: why is receivable at INR1,251 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cycle is 120-130 days, driven by retention money and billing/certification delays of up to 70 days; target is to hold about 130 days. Management said zero amount is overdue or at risk of bad debt.

qa_highlights.question: Finance cost rise versus cash balance and other income decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said vendors are now paid through TReDS, which raises finance cost (INR13 crore to INR17 crore QoQ) but lowers direct cost; the bank balance rose at quarter-end and fluctuates intra-quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter pledge status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR400-450 crore is secondary pledge for an acquisition, expected to be released in 3-5 months; about INR100 crore is borrowing-linked and to be cleared in 12-24 months. Management denied any forced-selling risk.

532885|2026-03.headline: Central Bank of India Q4 FY26 net profit fell to INR724 crore on a one-time INR632 crore DTA charge; FY26 net profit rose 15.43% to INR4,369 crore.
532885|2026-03.overview: FY26 business grew 15.60% to INR812,439 crore, with gross advances up 18.76% to INR344,516 crore and deposits up 13.38% to INR467,923 crore. Q4 net profit fell to INR724 crore from INR1,034 crore a year earlier, mainly due to a one-time INR632 crore hit from recognising deferred tax assets at 25% instead of 35%. Q4 operating profit rose 4.64% YoY to INR2,096 crore, but fell QoQ as treasury income (INR9 crore vs more than INR300 crore) and recoveries from written-off accounts (INR352 crore vs INR1,062 crore) dropped. Asset quality improved on a full-year basis: gross NPA 2.67% (down 51 bps YoY), net NPA 0.49%, slippage ratio 1.16% vs 1.45%.

marginal decline; Q4 about 2.9% excluding INR431 crore tax refund interest
GNPA -51 bps YoY; NNPA +6 bps per call (analyst noted rise)
includes 2% quarterly interim dividends for three quarters

FY27 capex budget INR1,442 crore and revenue budget INR1,276 crore for digital spend.

CD ratio 73.80% in March 2026 (66% in September 2025), roughly 74%; LCR 210% in FY26.
Term deposit growth above 14% to 15%; saving bank deposits crossed INR2 lakh crore for the first time, growing 10.05%.
Government business cell MoUs with state governments, railways and police/paramilitary forces are driving salary accounts.
No stress signals from the Middle East situation so far; no requests for overdue PCs or post-shipment facilities. Daily slippage of about INR250 crore recorded around 20 April.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating profit and net profit fall QoQ, and is there stress from geopolitics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower treasury income (INR9 crore vs more than INR300 crore in Q3) and lower written-off recoveries (INR352 crore vs INR1,062 crore). Net profit was hit by the INR632 crore DTA charge. No stress signals have appeared so far from the Middle East situation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fresh slippages rise QoQ to INR1,301 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Mukul Dandige attributed part of the rise to MSME accounts flagged in branch audits where credit submissions did not match business projections, and to some agriculture accounts. Government-scheme (MUDRA, PMEGP) accounts up to INR10 lakh also slipped; the normal run-rate is about INR800 crore a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL impact on the one-time charge and recurring credit cost?

Ongoing ECL-related provisions are estimated at INR600 crore to INR650 crore a year, offset by a tax benefit of roughly INR600 crore to INR800 crore. The full simulation is not complete.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NIM rise about 30 bps QoQ when yields and funding costs were flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Dandige said a INR431 crore income-tax interest refund booked in Q4 added to NIM. Excluding it, NIM was about 2.89% to 2.9% in Q4 vs 2.96% in Q3.

532885|2026-06.headline: Central Bank of India Q1 FY27 net profit rose 13.26% to ₹1,324 crore, with advances up 28.58% YoY and gross NPA at 2.60%.
532885|2026-06.overview: Central Bank of India reported Q1 FY27 global business of ₹833,320 crore (up 18.29% YoY), with deposits up 11.68% to ₹478,972 crore and gross advances up 28.58% to ₹354,348 crore. Net profit rose 13.26% to ₹1,324 crore, NIM was 3.06%, and ROE improved to 14.92% from 14.17%. Asset quality improved, with gross NPA at 2.60% (down 53 bps YoY), net NPA at 0.49%, and slippage ratio at 0.29%. Management said the quarter's advances growth was driven partly by a low base in corporate loans, and quarter-on-quarter advances growth was only about 2.85%. Liquidity coverage ratio fell sharply from 235% to 156%, as the bank deployed liquidity into loans.

financial_highlights.value: ₹276 crore (per Q&A); ₹621 crore vs ₹353 crore in segment comments

segments.name: Retail (RAM)
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 23.92% to ₹1,05,523 crore. Segment profit was reported at ₹1,377 crore vs ₹633 crore a year earlier in an analyst's reading of segment data.

segments.commentary: Agriculture advances grew 21.14% to ₹64,274 crore. Gold loan book is ₹36,000 crore; gold loans under agriculture are MCLR-linked, retail gold loans are not.

segments.name: MSME

segments.commentary: Corporate credit rose 46.52% to ₹1,12,770 crore from ₹76,966 crore, on a low base. Growth is concentrated in renewable energy, data centres, HAM projects and CRE. RAM-to-corporate mix is 68:32 against a 65:35 guidance (±5%).

segments.commentary: An analyst cited wholesale segment at minus ₹139 crore (vs ₹284 crore) and unallocated at minus ₹75 crore (vs ₹322 crore). Management said provisioning had not risen and did not clearly explain the change.

segments.commentary: Bank holds about 26% in Generali Central Life and Generali Central Non-Life, with ₹627 crore invested in total. Management expects higher income from both this year after the establishment phase.

guidance_outlook: Deposit growth guidance of 11% to 12% and advances growth guidance of 14% to 16% for FY27, which management said it will align with in the current quarter.
Quarter-on-quarter advances growth of about 3% expected to continue.
NIM guided at 3% and above; ROA guided at 1% and above.
Cost-to-income ratio to fall by 1.5% to 1.6% in the coming year, against a target below 56%.
Yield on advances expected to rise from 7.89% to about 8% by March 2027, led by gold loan and SHG yields of 8%+.

ECL transition planned from 1 April 2027; management estimated about 80 bps CRAR impact if provisioning is spread over five years or taken at once. Total ECL requirement estimated at ₹4,500-5,000 crore, with ₹1,525 crore already provided for Stage 1 and 2.
Technical write-off recoveries targeted at ₹2,200-2,500 crore for FY27; 600-700 property sales targeted against 460 last year.

Plans to open more corporate finance and mid-corporate branches.
Around 1,000 credit officers in specialised training to join in the first week of October 2026 for deployment at credit centres.
300 marketing officers hired and posted; 35 customer acquisition centres and 9 government business centres opened.
Board has approved establishing wealth management, credit card, NRI and marketing verticals; credit card entry is being initiated.
demand_pricing: Retail, agriculture and MSME growth of about 24%, 21% and 18% respectively; management expects similar rates ahead.
Growth engines named as gold loans and SHG, with dedicated divisions reporting to an Executive Director; South India cited as a gold-loan opportunity.
Deposit products: Cent Queen mobilised ₹1,457 crore and Salary Cent Prestige ₹787 crore.
Term deposits grew about 12%; around 85% of deposits are under ₹3 crore.
Undisbursed advances about ₹5,000 crore.
ECLGS 5.0: 34,824 applications sanctioned for ₹4,646 crore; guarantees issued in 30,561 accounts for ₹4,353 crore; disbursed in 27,567 accounts for ₹3,693 crore.
Business per branch ₹185 crore; business per employee ₹24 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is capital raising planned, given the Board's approval of up to about ₹7,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CRAR of 18.28% and CET1 of 16.24% are sufficient for guidance, so no capital raise is planned currently.

qa_highlights.question: Why did LCR fall from 235% to 156% and NSFR from 147% to 128%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said excess liquidity carries a cost and has been deployed; CD ratio rose from 64% to 74%. It said LCR remains above the regulatory threshold.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments drive the 28.6% advances growth, and what protects underwriting?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate grew 46.52% from a low base. Management cited a 0.29% slippage ratio, or 0.19% excluding agriculture KCC slippage of ₹200 crore, and better post-disbursement monitoring.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for deposit repricing and FCNR mobilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Term deposits are largely repriced at a 4.60% cost of deposits. FCNR(B) mobilisation is USD8.4 million so far, with a USD400 million target by September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Average yield on the corporate book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have corporate yield data; overall yield on advances is 7.89%, up from 7.78%, and is expected to reach about 8% by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost-to-income fall below 56%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited income steps (forex and BG cells, exporter meets, insurance and LC/BG business) and cost cuts (cash retention, ATM and currency chest use, utilities), targeting a 1.5-1.6% reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for credit cards and GIFT City?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit card and wealth management verticals were approved by the Board. GIFT City targets USD200 million deposits and USD500 million trade book over several years; about ₹470 crore has been disbursed there.

Treasury income of ₹276 crore is lower YoY on market conditions.
Segment profit data conflicts with management's explanation; the wholesale and unallocated swing was not clearly explained.
Recovery targets depend on technical write-off recoveries of ₹2,200-2,500 crore and property sales.

rows.why: Board approved wealth management, credit card, NRI and marketing verticals, and credit card entry is being initiated; FCNR(B) target is USD400 million by September 2026 against only USD8.4 million mobilised so far.

rows.why: LCR fell to 156% from 235% and NSFR to 128% from 147% as CD ratio rose to 74.10% from 64%; management says it will keep deploying excess liquidity, so further drop is a watch item.

rows.label: Technical write-off recoveries of ₹2,200-2,500 crore in FY27
rows.why: Recovery target is new and depends on technical write-off recoveries plus 600-700 property sales against 460 last year, so the outcome is conditional.

rows.why: Cost-to-income is 55.40% against a target below 56%; management cites forex/BG income steps and cash, ATM and utility cost cuts, but the ratio rose slightly YoY from 55.30%.

532885|2026-09.headline: Central Bank of India Q2 FY27 net profit rose 21% YoY to Rs1,469 Crore, with NIM at 3.01% and gross NPA at 2.39%.

Global advances grew 29.83% to Rs3,81,032 Crore and domestic deposits grew 14.41%, with CASA at 44.65%, below the 48% plus or minus 1% guidance. Asset quality improved on net NPA (0.31%) and slippage (0.24%), but credit cost rose to 0.53% as provisions were built for standard assets and ahead of ECL. Cost-to-income at 58.95% missed the sub-56% guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did provisions rise even as NPA and slippage improved?

qa_highlights.question: Is the ROA of about 1% sustainable into FY28 and FY29?

qa_highlights.question: Why is yield on advances low versus peers?

qa_highlights.question: Any stress in rural collections from El Nino or drought?

532891|2026-03.headline: Puravankara Q4 FY26 presales rose 190% YoY to INR3,547 crore; FY27 presales guidance set at INR11,200 crore and debt reduction target of INR750 crore.
532891|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was a strong quarter on sales and handovers, with presales of INR3,547 crore (up 190% YoY and 151% QoQ) and total income of INR1,541 crore (up 173% YoY) driven by 1,301 handovers. FY26 presales hit a record INR7,407 crore (up 55%) and collections a record INR4,258 crore (up 15%). Net debt was INR2,321 crore at March 31, 2026, down INR160 crore in the quarter, and cost of debt fell to 11.05%. Management guided FY27 presales of INR11,200 crore and a gross debt reduction of about INR750 crore, excluding new borrowing for business development. Collections, interest cost and FY27 delivery guidance drew the most pointed questions and several were deferred to offline follow-up.

segments.name: Residential sales
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 sales volume was 3.01 million sq ft (vs 1.42 million sq ft in Q4 FY25) at average realisation of INR11,787 per sq ft (up 37% YoY). FY26 volume was 7.25 million sq ft at INR10,213 per sq ft (up 21%).

segments.name: Handovers
segments.commentary: Handed over 1,301 homes (1.67 million sq ft) in Q4 FY26 and 3,747 homes (4.25 million sq ft) in FY26.

segments.name: Launches
segments.commentary: Launched three new projects (Purva SilverSky, Purva Northern Lights, Purva Estrella) and seven new phases in FY26, totalling 6.39 million sq ft. Northern Lights realisation is about INR10,700 per sq ft and it contributed INR1,100-1,200 crore to Q4 presales. Lokhandwala contributed slightly over INR800 crore in Q4.

segments.name: Commercial assets
segments.commentary: Aerocity has received OC and leasing has started; Zentech OC is expected within the month and is about 40-45% leased or sold. FY26 commercial sales and leasing was about 2.6 lakh sq ft.

segments.name: Starworth
segments.commentary: Not a reporting segment; order book is above INR2,000 crore and FY25 financials are on the website, with FY26 to follow.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales target of about INR11,200 crore, of which about 48% from sustained sales and 52% from new launches; about INR7,000 crore expected from the South and the rest from West and Commercial.
Gross debt reduction target of about INR750 crore for FY27, excluding incremental borrowing for business development; scheduled repayment is INR836 crore this year.

Collections expected to grow in double digits in FY27; management suggested 45-50% of the INR7,400 crore sales from the big launches could be collected in the first year (exact figure to be shared offline).
Estimated surplus cash flow of INR19,290 crore: INR8,816 crore from ongoing projects, INR2,131 crore from exiting commercial assets, and INR8,343 crore from the launch pipeline.
Launch pipeline of 14.85 million sq ft with GDV of INR22,547 crore; Bandra launch expected between Dussehra and Diwali after members vacate by end-June.
capex_capacity: Land bank of about 56.48 million sq ft, of which about 21 million sq ft is earmarked for the launch guidance, leaving about 35 million sq ft.

FY26 business development added over 12 million sq ft and about INR15,200 crore GDV across six projects, including Chembur (INR2,100 crore GDV), Malabar Hills (INR2,700 crore), Hennur Road JD (INR1,300 crore), Baglagere JD (INR1,000 crore), Attibele 53.5 acres (INR4,800 crore) and Northern Bengaluru JD (INR3,300 crore).
Malabar Hills: development agreement complete, registration in about 45 days, approvals expected in 9-12 months, pricing INR115,000-120,000 per sq ft on carpet area.
Two under-construction assets delivered, totalling about 2 million sq ft; FY27 residential delivery guidance to be shared offline.
Commercial: planning new verticals including data centres, warehousing and retail (about 3 lakh sq ft retail in Thane), with NCR (Delhi, Noida, Gurugram) as the expansion focus; no timelines given.
demand_pricing: Management says the Bengaluru market is steady rather than frenzied, with about 30% of the last launch sold; AI and GCC demand is seen as supportive.
NRI demand held up after the strong launch quarter; management says rupee depreciation may attract outside money but is watching global uncertainty.
Construction costs are rising about 6-7% due to diesel prices; management says margins and contingencies absorb this for now.
Project margins: new launches target above 20% gross margin (Northern Lights about 20-21%, Purva Estrella slightly above 20%); plotted development 30-40% gross margin.
Housing sales in top 8 cities were about 84,800 units, with homes above INR10 million at about 53% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: Launch timing and confidence in the launch pipeline, including Bandra?
qa_highlights.answer: Bandra launch targeted between Dussehra and Diwali, with a GDV of about INR2,700 crore for the saleable portion. Management says most of the pipeline (INR22,547 crore) should launch despite past delays from Bengaluru approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Collection outlook for FY27 given weak YoY growth and flat Western collections?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said collections will grow in double digits, with about 45-50% of the FY26 sales expected to be collected in the first year; the exact figure will be shared offline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest expense rise to about INR600-650 crore, and how does the NCD accounting work?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the increase reflects debt raised for business development, and that fair-value accounting for some instruments adds to P&L cost. Cost on that instrument is above 11.05%. Detailed working to follow offline.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR750 crore debt reduction apply to gross or net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it refers to gross debt, with scheduled repayment of INR836 crore this year; excess collections and project-level sweeps may add to that.

qa_highlights.question: Commercial leasing traction at Zentech and Aerocity?
qa_highlights.answer: Zentech is about 40-45% leased or sold before OC; Aerocity has many GCC RFPs of over 2 million sq ft and large deals are expected in the next couple of quarters.

risks_watch: Collections: FY26 collections grew only 15% against 55% presales growth, and the company has not given a collection number for FY27.
Interest cost of about INR600-650 crore on roughly INR3,900-4,000 crore gross debt; management is to provide reconciliation offline.
Launch execution risk in Bengaluru amid approval changes (e-Khata, Greater Bengaluru Authority) and the Bandra vacation timeline.
Cost inflation of 6-7% from diesel prices and geopolitical impact on the RBI's FY27 growth outlook (6.9%).
Delivery guidance for FY27 residential and the timing of Zentech OC and Aerocity leasing remain unquantified.

We are targeting a presales value of approximately INR 11,200 crores for FY26-27

On the balance sheet front, we are targeting a debt reduction of approximately INR 750 crores for FY26-27, excluding any incremental borrowing undertaken for strategic business development opportunities.

532891|2026-06.headline: Puravankara Q1 FY27 presales rose 28% YoY to INR1,439 crores and PAT turned positive at INR25 crores; FY27 presales guidance of INR11,200 crores reiterated.
532891|2026-06.overview: Presales grew 28% YoY to INR1,439 crores on 9% higher volume (1.36 million sq ft) and 18% higher realisation (INR10,589/sq ft). Collections rose 40% to INR1,199 crores and 745 homes (0.94 million sq ft) were handed over. Total income rose 63% YoY to INR877 crores, EBITDA margin expanded to 25% from 15%, and PAT was INR25 crores versus a loss of INR69 crores a year earlier. Management kept FY27 presales guidance and the INR700 crores debt-reduction target, while adding four Bengaluru land opportunities (GDV ~INR5,200 crores) and signing a sale of Purva Zentech to ICICI Prudential AMC at ~INR625 crores EV.

segments.name: West & Commercial
segments.commentary: Contributed INR393 crores of presales in Q1 FY27, including ~INR200 crores from Purva Estrella (per Rajat Rastogi's estimate). Aerocity received OC for 1.3 million sq ft; Miami has RERA and is on sale.

qa_highlights.question: Why did land payment reach INR574 crores in cash flow, and what is the outlook for land spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the amount paid for the four Bengaluru acquisitions from cash on hand; no land cost is unpaid, but future development spend will be booked as construction cost, and new land purchases would add land payments.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt will come off with the ICICI Prudential AMC Purva Zentech deal, and how will proceeds be used?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR250 crores of debt on that asset will be repaid from proceeds; the rest will be evaluated for debt reduction, business development or working capital, with closing expected this month.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Q2 launches (Westend, Hennur Road, Cityspire, Winworth) on track, and any approval issues?
qa_highlights.answer: Westend has RERA and is launched with good EOIs; Hennur Road delayed by Karnataka government change, clarity expected this week; Cityspire and Winworth only await RERA, expected this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR11,200 crores presales guidance and INR700 crores debt reduction still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Both held; launches slipping from Q1 moved to Q2 for one or two projects, and management said opportunity spend versus debt reduction will be reviewed from time to time.

qa_highlights.question: What margin is targeted over the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA margin guidance of 25-30% at portfolio level held, with product mix (plotted, JDA, outright, redevelopment) causing project-level variation.

qa_highlights.question: How much did Purva Estrella contribute to Q1 sales and how does it compare with the top projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Estrella contributed about INR200 crores in Q1 and about INR800 crores since launch; management could not confirm a separate top-three ranking, citing South's Northern Light and Provident Equinox and West's Estrella.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt reduction plan over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no zero-debt target; free cash flow will be split between new opportunities and debt, and debt is an important part of the business as the portfolio (about INR58,500 crores) grows.

qa_highlights.question: What is the leasing status and rate expectation for Purva Aerocity, and when is Phase 2?
qa_highlights.answer: OC for 1.3 million sq ft; about 2.5 million sq ft of RFPs filed with no lease signed yet; LOIs expected at INR60-65 per sq ft. Phase 2 (0.9 million sq ft) to start after 70-80% of Phase 1 is leased, possibly in the next few quarters; monetisation possible later.

532892|2026-03.headline: MOFSL FY26 operating PAT rose 16% YoY to ₹2,360 crores; Q4 operating PAT up 25% with a ₹661 crore exit run rate.

Asset and Private Wealth businesses grew profit 33% and now contribute about 50% of operating PAT, with Asset Management at 33% of group operating PAT versus 26% in FY25. Reported PAT including OCI was hit by notional MTM losses of about ₹1,000 crores on a ~₹9,000 crore investment book, which management said were largely recouped in April 2026. Long-term credit rating was upgraded to AA+ (stable). Q&A focused on SIP and MF flow share, yield compression from product mix, MTF and broking trajectory, digital broker competition, and treasury MTM.

532892|2026-09.headline: Motilal Oswal Q2FY27 operating PAT rose 29% YoY to ₹718 crore, led by Asset & Private Wealth, which grew 43% YoY.
532892|2026-09.overview: Operating PAT grew 29% YoY to ₹718 crore, with Asset & Private Wealth Management up 43% and now contributing about 58% of operating PAT. The company received a SEBI custodian licence in Q2 and plans to launch the custody business in Q4FY27, with no material contribution expected in FY28.

532893|2026-03.headline: VTM Ltd FY26 PAT fell about 75% to Rs 11 crore on US tariff discounts (~Rs 20 crore), with FY27 turnover guided up 12-14% and EBITDA margin targeted at 10-11%.
532893|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue growth of about 8% (base ~Rs 372 crore) but PAT of about Rs 11 crore, down roughly 75% YoY. The drop was attributed to an ~18% US tariff-related discount (~Rs 20 crore), chargeback discounts (~Rs 8 crore), a Rs 2.3 crore forex MTM loss on PCFC borrowings, a gratuity provision under the new Labour Code, and ~15% higher raw material costs. FY26 EBITDA margin was 7.43%, and management said the 18% discount to the US customer Quince is still in place, with negotiations ongoing and the current price point at about 10%. Management guided to 12-14% FY27 top-line growth, a 10-11% EBITDA margin, and a 6.5 million-unit order backlog as of 31 May.

US tariff rose to ~50-60% at one point and then settled at 18%; the company shared ~10% of the tariff burden with the customer through a discount of 18% that is still in place, against a current tariff of 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 operating margin return to FY25 levels of ~19% EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: uncertain. FY26 was 7.43%; target is 10-11%. CMD said 19% is pre-tariff and may be a stretch in the post-tariff era.

qa_highlights.question: What is peak revenue at full utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said greige runs at 80-83% utilisation so ~80% is the practical ceiling. Management said the top line would reach ~Rs 420 crore at peak, with a Rs 500-600 crore run-rate possible with the right mix and outsourcing.

qa_highlights.question: How is the margin split between greige and home textiles?
qa_highlights.answer: Greige fabric earns a traditional 7-9% margin. The EBITDA drop is mainly from home textiles, where the ~Rs 20 crore tariff-linked price cut was the main hit, plus gratuity (Rs 41 lakh) and PF settlement (Rs 32 lakh) costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 18% discount still in place when US tariffs have fallen to 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the discount is still in place, the customer is more price sensitive post-tariff, and negotiations are ongoing; pipeline sales carry the earlier tariff.

qa_highlights.question: Why are payables so low compared with group companies?
qa_highlights.answer: The CMD said both companies are cash-rich and pay vendors within 30-45 days, so terms are not favourable to group entities. Pacific Cotton is a separate US entity selling basic lower-value Amazon-brand items.

532898|2026-03.headline: POWERGRID delivered ₹28,206 crore capitalisation and ~₹40,000 crore capex in FY26, guiding FY27 capex to ₹37,000 crore and capitalisation to ₹30,000 crore.
532898|2026-03.overview: Management said FY26 capex (close to ₹40,000 crore against an initial ₹28,000 crore guide) and capitalisation (₹28,206 crore against a ₹25,000 crore commitment) both beat guidance. Standalone PAT rose 4% to about ₹15,921 crore and consolidated PAT rose 3% to about ₹15,928 crore, with total income of ₹47,684 crore versus ₹47,459 crore. Management flagged a natural RTM revenue decline as assets reach 12 years, offset by FY26 capitalisation that it expects to flow into FY27 revenue. The pipeline was described as ₹1.7 lakh crore of works in hand and ₹1.1 lakh crore under bidding, with new avenues in BESS, integrated storage under Section 62, and the first international PPP in Kenya.

segments.name: TBCB (tariff-based competitive bidding)
segments.commentary: Accounts for about 81% of the ₹1.7 lakh crore works in hand (₹1.37 lakh crore). Management said FY26 saw 9 TBCB wins out of 28 projects floated, at a total tariff of about 44% share.

segments.name: RTM (regulated tariff mechanism)
segments.commentary: Works in hand of about ₹28,000 crore. Revenue is on a natural downward trajectory after assets complete 12 years, offset in FY26 by ~₹1,700 crore of depreciation-related gaps covered by other income items.

segments.name: Telecom
segments.commentary: Revenue of ₹1,195 crore; first 400G interface in India, first international long-distance link to Bhutan, and a 1,000-rack data centre at Manesar expected to be visible in the next quarter.

segments.name: Consultancy
segments.commentary: Revenue of ₹1,755 crore versus ₹799 crore in FY25, with 39 domestic orders and 62 ongoing projects, and 8 international orders across 25 countries.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex initial guidance of about ₹37,000 crore; FY28 capex expected above ₹40,000 crore, with management indicating a ₹40,000-45,000 crore range.
FY27 capitalisation guidance of up to ₹30,000 crore initially; FY28 capitalisation expected to move to about ₹35,000 crore.
FY27 expected to show full revenue benefit of FY26 capitalisation, which came mainly in the later part of FY26.
Management said FY27-FY28 earnings growth is likely to be better than the last three years when asked directly; it did not quantify this.
Integrated storage (BESS) capacity target not yet given; management said numbers would follow once Section 62 regulatory clarity emerges.
Pang-Kaithal HVDC project excluded from the ₹1.7 lakh crore works in hand pending Government of India review.
capex_capacity: Capitalisation of 4,765 ckm of transmission lines and 72,055 MVA of substation capacity added in FY26; 9 new substations taking the total to 291, and total transmission lines at 1.84 lakh ckm and 624 GVA transformation capacity at 31 March 2026.

Transformer and reactor manufacturing capacity in India is about 300 GVA against demand of 400+ GVA a year; the company is moving to bulk procurement and project timelines were extended to 26-30+ months from 18 months.
Gross fixed assets crossed ₹3 lakh crore; 11 HVDC projects are running with about 101 GW of the 120 GW inter-regional capacity.
New substations commissioned include Bhadla, Ramgarh/Dausa (8 months from foundation), Bikaner-3, KPS-2, KPS-3, Narela and Ananthapuram.
Pilot 1,000-rack data centre at Manesar expected to be visible within the next quarter; 220 kV mobile GIS in place, with 132 kV and 400 kV mobile GIS expected within this calendar year.
demand_pricing: Works in hand ₹1.7 lakh crore (TBCB ₹1.37 lakh crore, RTM ₹28,000 crore, others ₹4,200 crore), excluding Pang-Kaithal HVDC.

Under-bidding pipeline of ₹1.1 lakh crore, including ₹5,270 crore of intra-State; major projects include Barmer Phase 4, Vizag Green Hydrogen, Jam Khambhaliya, Krishnagiri, Lakadia, ERWR and Nawada-Durgapur.
Management cited a ₹7.9 lakh crore opportunity under the 900+ GW by 2036 anchor programme and ₹6.4 lakh crore from Brahmaputra basin hydro; 22 HVDC schemes (127 GW) are in planning or bidding.
Intra-State TBCB thresholds are ₹150-250 crore by state; the smallest project POWERGRID has bid was about ₹60 crore.
Management said electricity share in the energy basket is about 22% and is expected to rise, supporting transmission demand.

On competition, management said it bids on risk-return framework and declined to quantify changes in TBCB tariff or IRR; equity IRR guidance of 11-13% was described as possibly better, with change-in-law as a cost pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the Q4 FY26 EBITDA decline and whether new TBCB projects use service concession accounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to the natural RTM tariff dip after 12 years of asset life; new BOOT-method TBCB projects are accounted for using the financial lease model.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and commissioning expectations for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex initial guidance of about ₹37,000 crore; FY28 expected beyond ₹40,000 crore, in a ₹40,000-45,000 crore range. Capitalisation guided at ₹30,000 crore for FY27 and about ₹35,000 crore for FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Gross block versus NCT cost variance on projects and inflation indicators?
qa_highlights.answer: No project-level variance was given; management said costs are factored into bids and surprises such as force majeure and change in law are addressed under the Transmission Service Agreement.

qa_highlights.question: Market share and whether competitive intensity in TBCB is rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has bid TBCB for about 14 years and selects projects by risk-return framework rather than volume; it did not indicate a change in intensity.

qa_highlights.question: Equity IRR on TBCB projects given cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said returns could be better than the 11-13% range, as cost-plus RTM rewards cost but TBCB rewards efficiency, and change-in-law provisions protect against surprises.

qa_highlights.question: Phasing of capex and capitalisation in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said timing depends on individual project completions, expects an even spread across quarters, and noted that the Q4-heavy FY26 was incidental.

qa_highlights.question: Regulated equity on standalone and consolidated basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Regulated equity exists only in standalone; TBCB projects have no regulated equity.

532898|2026-06.headline: POWERGRID Q1 FY27 PAT flat at Rs 3,598 crore (vs Rs 3,631 crore QoQ) as regulatory drag of ~Rs 560 crore offset Rs 790 crore transmission-charge growth.
532898|2026-06.overview: Consolidated transmission charges rose 3% QoQ to Rs 10,905 crore and total income to Rs 11,697 crore, but PAT was Rs 3,598 crore against Rs 3,631 crore in the prior quarter. Management attributed the flat profit to a ~Rs 560 crore regulatory drag: Rs 330 crore lower depreciation/interest recovery and Rs 230 crore of interest on provisional-vs-final tariff differential that is no longer available, plus a Rs 33 crore one-off write-back (KSK Mahanadi) in the base quarter. Capitalisation of Rs 5,277 crore in Q1 was about 3.1x the prior-year Q1 figure of Rs 1,683 crore, against a FY27 guidance of Rs 30,000 crore. Receivable days fell to about 12 from 19.41, with Rs 11,404 crore realised against Rs 10,963 crore billed.

segments.name: Transmission (regulated RTM and TBCB)
segments.commentary: Transmission charges up Rs 790 crore from new assets, offset by regulatory drag of ~Rs 560 crore; TBCB operational equity investment rose to Rs 9,965 crore from Rs 4,671 crore a year earlier, funded through internal accruals.

segments.name: Consultancy
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 252 crore; 16 domestic and 3 international orders, footprint in about 25 countries.

segments.name: Telecom (PowerTel)
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 391 crore; connectivity extended to Andaman and Nicobar and first international link to Nepal; 100% backbone availability claimed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex guidance Rs 37,000 crore; management says Q1 capex already more than 10% of the annual guidance... as stated on call, capex is more than 10% of guidance achieved in Q1 itself.
FY27 capitalisation guidance Rs 30,000 crore; Q1 at Rs 5,277 crore, with Koppal, Gadag and Bidar-Maheshwaram projects expected to be commissioned later.
Rs 300 crore of RTM revenue pending CERC deemed-DOCO orders, to accrue as regulator hears petitions.
Works in hand about Rs 1.75 lakh crore (TBCB Rs 1.46 lakh crore, RTM Rs 25,000 crore, others Rs 4,200 crore); bidding pipeline Rs 1.19 lakh crore; long-term outlook above Rs 15 lakh crore.
Estimated Rs 7.9 lakh crore of transmission capex to 2035-36 expected to be bid over the next 3-4 years; estimate excludes land compensation under new MoP guidelines.
risks_watch: Regulatory drag from ageing 2014-16 capitalisation and CERC order timing: Rs 560 crore in Q1 with further depreciation step-ups expected as assets mature past 12 years.
Capitalisation run-rate: Rs 5,277 crore in Q1 against Rs 30,000 crore FY27 guidance requires heavy back-ended commissioning dependent on RoW and land compensation.
Land compensation under new MoP guidelines is not in the Rs 7.9 lakh crore estimate and may raise costs; state adoption still settling.
Limited disclosure: management declined a separate TBCB consolidated P&L, drawing analyst pushback; the company will examine better disclosures.
Equipment supply and raw-material cost risk for transformers and GIS; Chinese OEM participation is a changing variable.

Evasive on specifics such as Barmer HVDC award date, BESS timing and the normative versus actual debt gap, promising follow-ups.

qa_highlights.question: How much is the regulatory drag in depreciation and revenue this quarter, and how will it evolve as 2014-16 assets age?
qa_highlights.answer: Management quantified the drag at about Rs 560 crore for Q1: Rs 330 crore depreciation/interest and Rs 230 crore interest on the CERC differential. It said assets capitalised about 12 years ago will continue to weigh, and framed this as part of the regulatory characteristic.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PAT flat if the change is profit-neutral, and what is the adjusted base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs 230 crore interest on the provisional-vs-final differential is no longer available and a Rs 33 crore write-back (KSK Mahanadi) in the prior quarter does not recur. It said the regulatory differential is the major factor, with a small depreciation/interest mismatch versus notional figures.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Rs 13,000 crore TBCB equity funded, and what is the Rs 7.9 lakh crore transmission capex timeline and land cost treatment?
qa_highlights.answer: All TBCB equity is funded from internal accruals with no parent-level debt. Management said the Rs 7.9 lakh crore to 2035-36 would be bid over the next 3-4 years and excludes land compensation under new MoP guidelines, which Delhi, Haryana and Gujarat have adopted.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Barmer HVDC award and BESS opportunity under the regulated route?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bids for the Rajasthan Phase IV Barmer Complex HVDC are submitted and under evaluation by the bid process coordinator, with no award date yet. On BESS, it said petitions have been filed before the regulator after NR and WR RPC consent, with timing dependent on regulator and stakeholder positions.

qa_highlights.question: Can TBCB consolidated revenue, EBITDA and PAT be disclosed separately, and what returns are earned on operational TBCB equity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a separate TBCB P&L or return figure. It said returns are calibrated across multiple projects and that it will examine better disclosures, while noting regulatory disclosures are already made.

qa_highlights.question: Is there scope for upside to the Rs 30,000 crore capitalisation guidance, and why is the gross block-to-depreciation gap so wide?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said transmission capitalisation follows project timelines and ROW constraints, citing Rs 5,277 crore in Q1 and Koppal, Gadag and Bidar-Maheshwaram to follow. On the gap, management said TBCB projects are under the lease accounting method, so depreciation is replaced by lease amortisation, and PAT is unaffected by the method.

Tariff is recovered per annum (Rs per annum, not Rs per MWh), so revenue is not linked to power flow; management says generation delays affect revenue only if the generator or load is late.

532899|2026-03.headline: Kaveri Seed FY26 revenue rose 16.25% to INR 1,303.77 crore, but PAT grew only 6.8% to INR 283.26 crore; management guides FY27 revenue growth of 15-20%.
532899|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations rose 6.84% YoY to INR 82.21 crore and the net loss narrowed to INR 25.65 crore from INR 29.25 crore. For FY26, revenue grew 16.25% to INR 1,303.77 crore, EBITDA rose 8.34% to INR 349.75 crore, and PAT rose 6.8% to INR 283.26 crore. Growth came from maize, hybrid rice, selection rice, exports and new cotton hybrids. Management said inventory is elevated by design, with higher yields and a deliberate buffer, and that FY27 growth will be volume-led because price increases are unlikely.

segments.commentary: New hybrids rose to 30.05% of cotton contribution from 10.3%. Management expects cotton to grow faster than the company, above 20% in a good case, driven by new hybrids across North, Central and South India.

segments.commentary: FY26 volume grew 18.84% and revenue 40.17%, the key growth driver. Kharif outlook is flat-to-sideways due to sentiment and fertiliser shortfall; rabi is seen as positive.

segments.name: Rice
segments.commentary: Hybrid rice revenue rose 18.3% despite Punjab restrictions; selection rice revenue rose 9.76%. Growth is expected from Punjab, UP, Bihar, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY26 exports grew about 90% and Q4 FY26 exports grew about 76%; management expects strong performance to continue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise about 17% when sales grew about 16%, and will the buffer persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Production was raised on purpose to hold buffer stock amid last year's competition for production areas; yields of 5-7% higher also added to inventory. Management said inventory is not a concern.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other current liabilities and customer advances fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Advances were INR 75-80 crore lower YoY because farmer cash flows are tight and the company has not pushed advances, which would require higher incentives, as margins have shrunk.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth be driven by volume or price, and what margin is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth will be volume-led with no price hikes; revenue guided at 15-20%, cotton above 20%. Lower production costs and stable other costs should lift margins; management did not give a specific margin figure.

qa_highlights.question: Are write-offs a risk on older cotton seed inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most inventory is new production with about 1.3-1.5 years of age against a 3-year cotton seed life, so write-off risk is low and any leftover stock will be used next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for maize in kharif, given high channel inventory and El Nino?
qa_highlights.answer: Kharif sentiment is weak, with sideways trend tied to El Nino uncertainty and fertiliser shortage; rabi is positive, and the company expects to grow in kharif by targeting new pockets.

qa_highlights.question: How are the Kaveri and Aditya brands positioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditya and Genomix are wholly owned subsidiaries that market B2B hybrids from R&D; Kaveri focuses on its main product line, and the subsidiaries sell different products but may compete among themselves.

532899|2026-06.headline: Kaveri Seed Q1 FY27 revenue fell to Rs 815 crore from Rs 945 crore (about -14%) on a weak El Nino monsoon, with EBITDA margin held near 35%.
532899|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 815 crore against Rs 945 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA at Rs 285 crore (vs Rs 332 crore) and net profit at Rs 271.3 crore (vs Rs 316 crore) as stated on the call. Management attributed the decline to a delayed, deficient monsoon that shortened the sowing window, cutting maize sales in Karnataka and weakening demand in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Gujarat. Cotton was flat YoY at Rs 213.43 crore while non-cotton was Rs 601.57 crore, and new products gained share in cotton and maize. Management said the quarter's margin was helped by lower production cost (down 4-5%) and that inventory is up about Rs 200 crore YoY, prompting lower production next year.

financial_highlights.change: same as last year, management said slightly above
about Rs 265-270 crore as of 30 June

segments.name: Cotton
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 213.43 crore, flat YoY. New cotton products were 37% of cotton sales vs 22% last year; North India (Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan) roughly doubled from a small base, while Gujarat and Maharashtra were hit by low rain and illegal Bt seed.

segments.name: Maize
segments.commentary: Sales fell sharply (about 40% decline per analyst question, not disputed by management); Karnataka sowing was about one-fifth done by mid-June. New single-cross hybrids are over 20% of maize sales.

segments.name: Hybrid rice
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 247.07 crore, the largest non-cotton segment. Two new hybrids KRH7344 and KRH7227 launched this season contributed 62% of new-product sales in rice.

segments.name: Selection rice
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 159.07 crore, marginal YoY growth despite poor rain in rice sowing areas.

segments.name: Bajra
segments.commentary: New hybrids are 65% of Bajra volumes, up from 61%.

segments.name: Vegetables
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 15.08 crore; management called it a small segment with some spillover possible in Q2 if rain improves.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the rest of FY27 quarters to be higher than the prior year's comparable quarters, with Karnataka recovery and Rabi maize supporting H2; the Q1 revenue gap is expected to narrow but no full recovery was committed.
Management said Q2 margins would be lower than Q1 margins, and that the YoY revenue gap would narrow, not turn positive, within FY27.
Karnataka Kharif recovery: about 1,500 tonnes sold this year vs about 2,600 tonnes last year, a gap of 1,100-1,200 tonnes worth about Rs 40-60 crore (figures given inconsistently on the call).
Export target of Rs 100 crore in vegetables and other crops within about 3 years; export margin expected at 25-30%, in line with current levels.
Management reiterated a long-term growth target of 15-18% (earlier referenced as 18-20%) over the next 2-3 years, with growth expected to return to last year's level.
Cash expected to rise only by about Rs 20-30 crore by Q2 to close to Rs 300 crore; any buyback is subject to a Board decision, with no amount decided.
capex_capacity: Inventory is up about Rs 200 crore YoY because production was taken up on expectations of a good El Nino-era season; management said production will be reduced next year.
Cost of production is down 4-5% YoY while dealer-level realisations are down 2-3%; management said FY28 production will be minimal and cost per unit should stay at last year's level.
Product pipeline described as among the best in 10 years, with Madhya Pradesh hybrids newer and not yet at scale.
demand_pricing: Monsoon deficit to June 15 shortened the Kharif sowing window and farmers bought fewer premium products; Karnataka tanks now filling after July rains, which management expects to support maize in Q2-Q3.
Maize price rose to about Rs 27-28 from Rs 16-17 at the start of the season, which management expects to support Rabi demand.
Cotton MRP is government-capped; management said Kaveri realises higher prices than many peers in the top three cotton segments.
Competition: illegal Bt cotton and smaller players have grown; management said no new hybrids from peers have taken share in the last 3-4 years, and that Kaveri has lost cotton share over 7-8 years.
Management said subsidiaries (sales of about 10-12 lakh cotton packets this year) operate as separate competitors, and that their revenue is booked independently.

qa_highlights.question: Why has profit not crossed the ~Rs 300 crore peak of 2014-15 despite non-cotton growth, and what can be achieved in 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cotton was about 90% of mix in 2014-15 at high margins versus about 20% now, with cotton margins shrunk; FY27 was a one-off weather year and should not be a benchmark.

qa_highlights.question: Is Kaveri losing focus on cotton given illegal seed, price caps and no new cotton hybrids; what about the inventory build of about Rs 1,200 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management admitted cotton share was lost over 7-8 years, said new hybrids were developed in the last 3-4 years, and said inventory is about Rs 200 crore higher YoY due to over-anticipated El Nino season; production will be reduced next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins not fall with lower sales, and is any crop's margin lower than last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA margin slightly expanded; gross margin up 2-3%, with higher employee and other costs as people were deployed ahead of an expected good season.

qa_highlights.question: Why are subsidiaries selling seeds alongside Kaveri, and what is the new-product definition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said subsidiaries are independent competitors that take discarded me-too hybrids; about 10-12 lakh cotton packets sold through subsidiaries this year. New products are those launched within the last 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did maize fall about 40% when peers grew, and what about Karnataka recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed weak rain in Karnataka, Andhra and Telangana (25-30% of last year's Kharif sales came from Karnataka) and no Madhya Pradesh or Maharashtra presence; Karnataka sales were about 1,500 tonnes vs 2,600 tonnes, a gap of 1,100-1,200 tonnes worth about Rs 40-60 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue outlook and cash/buyback position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 quarters should be above last year's, Q2 margins lower than Q1, and the YoY gap should narrow but not turn positive. Cash of Rs 265-270 crore as of 30 June may rise only Rs 20-30 crore to about Rs 300 crore by Q2; buyback is a Board decision with no amount decided.

Management flagged elevated maize and rice inventory (Rs 150 crore plus higher than last year) and higher cash-to-payables timing effects, and said export expansion into Bangladesh, Philippines, Indonesia, Tanzania and others is aimed at building its own brand.

532921|2026-09.headline: APSEZ Q2 FY27 revenue rose 24% to INR11,340 crore and EBITDA 23% to INR6,807 crore; FY27 revenue and EBITDA guidance raised by INR1,000 crore each.
532921|2026-09.overview: Management reported broad-based growth across domestic ports, international ports, logistics and marine, with consolidated revenue up 24% YoY and EBITDA up 23%. FY27 guidance was raised to revenue of INR44,000-46,000 crore and EBITDA of INR26,000-27,000 crore, and FY27 capex guidance was increased by INR3,000 crore, mainly for Indian ports. International ports had a record quarter with EBITDA more than tripling, while marine was hit in July-August by Strait of Hormuz disruption that left vessels idle. Management said domestic volumes were already growing double digits in October after a weak Q1 caused by the Middle East crisis, iron ore export curbs and coastal coal timing.

segments.name: Domestic ports
segments.commentary: Revenue up 13% YoY with a 72.5% EBITDA margin. Mundra ran at about 91-92% average utilisation in Q1-Q2, with some terminals above 100%.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,839 crore (+71%) and EBITDA INR878 crore, margin 47.7%. CWIT Colombo handled 2 million TEUs in 18 months and its capacity is being doubled from 1.6 to 3.2 million TEUs; Tanzania posted its highest-ever container volume.

segments.name: Logistics
segments.commentary: Revenue up 21% YoY. Truck revenue up 28% YoY and integrated freight network revenue more than doubled. Container volumes rose 15% QoQ in Q2 after the Q1 slowdown.

segments.name: Marine
segments.commentary: Revenue up 57% and EBITDA up 32% YoY, with fleet at 138 vessels. Margin fell QoQ in July-August as about 7-8 Astro offshore vessels were stranded by the Strait of Hormuz closure; management said margins recovered from September.

Management declined to derive a full-year EBITDA margin from the guidance range, calling H2 an assumption rather than arithmetic.

Vizhinjam Phase 2 delivery committed for December 2028; the EXIM yard at Vizhinjam has seen strong traction.
Vadhvan HAM bid for reclamation and nearshore development: no visibility on award; first work targeted 2028 or 2029.

Liquid cargo market share gained significantly; Hazira handles more than 140 liquid types.

Management did not quantify the INR depreciation impact on India port EBITDA; it said the effect was positive for revenue composition.
Colombo outperformance came from automation and efficiency, with volumes above expectations at lower unit cost.

qa_highlights.question: What changed in logistics, and is double-digit growth sustainable? Why would the full-year EBITDA margin fall to about 58.5% on the revised guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said logistics growth is structural, driven by ICD ramp-up (Virochannagar, Malur) and the integrated multimodal model; it said guidance is a hypothesis, not arithmetic, and asked analysts not to derive a 58.2-58.5% margin from it.

qa_highlights.question: Why was capex raised, and are international acquisitions on the radar?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex increase is India-only, accelerated for Mundra, Dhamra, Hazira and Vizhinjam because Mundra was at 90-92% utilisation and CT5 was coming. Management is evaluating more than 20 international assets against four tests: top/bottom-line growth at or above APSEZ's, geopolitics and macro, financing, and a leadership partner.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the international EBITDA margin to 47.7%, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Colombo was the main driver, as an automated terminal with higher volumes and lower cost; Australia also contributed. Management said Australia's margin should stay within 1-2 points, Haifa is unlikely to improve, and it needs two more quarters before giving entity-level guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did marine margin fall sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Astro offshore vessels (7-8 on standby) could not transit the Strait of Hormuz in July-August, leaving war insurance and fixed costs without revenue; margins improved from September as transits resumed.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a Mundra disruption from local yard operators' strikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an empty-yard issue had been resolved: 120 acres of empty yard are now inside the port and full, with another 200 acres planned, plus an integrated warehouse.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Indian market share flat, and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was not normal: container volumes were hit by the Middle East crisis and dry cargo by policy; October is recovering, and it expects market share gains in Q3 and Q4.

532926|2026-03.headline: Jyothy Labs Q4 FY26 revenue rose 7.7% to INR717 crores, but EBITDA margin fell about 330 bps to 13.5% on crude-linked input inflation and lower realisations.

Fabric Care and Personal Care recovered strongly, Dishwash was flat in value, and Household Insecticides losses narrowed to about INR5 crores from INR25 crores. Management took about 4% price increases in March, with the full effect expected from Q1 FY27, and declined to guide on FY27 margins.

532926|2026-06.headline: Jyothy Labs Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to 8.4% (down ~820 bps YoY) as gross margin dropped to 38.5% on crude-linked input inflation.
532926|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was margin-led weakness: gross margin fell 950 bps YoY to 38.5% and EBITDA margin to 8.4%, as input and packaging inflation outran price increases of roughly 3% realised in the quarter. Ex-Pril and FA, revenue grew 8.1% in value and 5.3% in volume. Fabric Care grew over 14% in value and 10% in volume, while Home Care ex-Pril grew 2.4% and Personal Care was subdued. Management said margins should recover gradually, with H2 better than H1, and that it expects double-digit revenue growth ex-Pril and FA for FY27. Segment reporting was changed to Fabric Care, Home Care and Personal Care from Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Fabric Care
segments.commentary: Value growth over 14% and volume growth 10% in Q1; detergent powders and bars grew double digits, and liquid detergents (Henko, Ujala, Mr. White, Morelight) continued high growth. Management said Fabric Care was priced up close to 5% on a portfolio basis.

segments.name: Home Care
segments.commentary: Grew 2.4% YoY excluding Pril, which exited effective 31 May 2026. Exo Liquid (bioenzyme, launched 3-4 months ago) is at early scale-up; the broader Exo franchise grew mid-to-high single digits in value and double digits in volume. Household insecticides were hit by extended summer and delayed rains.

segments.name: Personal Care
segments.commentary: Performance subdued in Q1 on price increases of about 9-10% and transient supply-chain disruptions; management expects recovery from Q2. Soap noodle prices have risen since June.

guidance_outlook: FY27 ex-Pril and FA: double-digit revenue growth expected; management said high-single-digit volume growth with 3-4% price.
EBITDA margins to stay under pressure through FY27 on elevated crude-linked costs; H2 expected substantially better than H1, subject to demand and commodity stability.
Margin recovery expected gradual and more meaningful from October if commodity prices stay stable; Q2 margin not expected to be materially lower than Q1.
Aim to return to historical margin levels, but management said a large part depends on crude prices.
Step up advertising and brand-building investment after A&P was moderated over recent quarters.
Total price increases since the start of the conflict about 4-4.5%, of which about 3% flowed through in Q1 and the rest in Q2.
capex_capacity: No capacity, capex or commissioning figures were given in the call.
Maxo incense sticks launched in July 2026 as a government-approved product; management said it is priced at par with competition.
demand_pricing: Rural demand resilient; urban demand subdued, and general trade growth muted, though ex-Pril and FA general trade was positive per the CFO.
Modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce among fastest-growing channels; e-commerce and quick commerce growing 25-30%.
Price cuts at SKU level by competition in some SKUs; company said it is at par with competition, which limited price increases to about 3% realised in Q1.
Pril exit: Henkel did not renew the agreement and the matter is before court; no sales beyond 31 May 2026.
Management said liquid detergents are now priced below powders, and premium SKUs across home care are being discounted.
Distributor stock maintained at 15-20 days; significant part of general trade sold on advance payment.

qa_highlights.question: Why is price increase only about 3% when HUL and GCPL took about 5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited competitive SKU-level price reductions; the CFO said the blended increase was about 4-4.5% in total, with Personal Care at 9-10% and other segments at 4-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the margin gap close without crude deflation?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the goal is to return to historical margins, but much depends on crude; raw material inflation was about 15-16% and the total impact was about 9-9.5% after 3% pricing and 3-4% efficiencies and mix.

qa_highlights.question: Has general trade declined, and what is happening in quick commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: General trade was muted on urban demand, but positive ex-Pril and FA; e-commerce and quick commerce were growing 25-30% with no material assortment or pricing gaps.

qa_highlights.question: Will double-digit revenue growth return from this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the aim is double-digit growth from the current quarter, with 3-4% price and high-single-digit volume; the FY27 target excludes Pril and FA.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company looking at M&A after the TTK brand sale to Wipro?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company evaluated the TTK business but did not pursue it because two divisions did not fit strategy and two overlapped; it continues to screen assets with stringent filters.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin pressure structural, and what is the path back to 18-20% EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is not a commodity business and 90% of revenue is crude-linked; it is working on diversifying away from crude-linked raw materials and expects margins to recover once crude cools.

risks_watch: Crude and packaging costs: higher-cost inventory flows through Q2, and soap noodle prices are rising from June.
Pril legal matter pending before court; Pril exit removes a revenue base that management excluded from its FY27 growth guidance.
Competitive pricing pressure in some SKUs, and a larger competitor entering dishwash.
Personal Care recovery after 9-10% price increases and supply chain disruption.

Whether A&P steps up after being cut to 6.5% of revenue from 10.8%.
