532926|2026-09.headline: Jyothy Labs Q2 FY27 operating EBITDA margin fell to 2.5% from 16.1% as gross margin dropped to 34.8%, despite 3.3% revenue growth to INR760 crore.
532926|2026-09.overview: Reported revenue rose 3.3% YoY to INR760 crore, but the Pril and Fa exit (brand licence expired May 2026) depressed reported volumes; excluding these brands, value grew 12.4% and volume 8.1%. Crude-linked raw material and packaging inflation compressed gross margin to 34.8% (48.1% last year, 38.5% in Q1), pushing operating EBITDA to INR19 crore and PAT to INR10.6 crore. Management took about 4% price increases, said pricing alone cannot close a 13-14% inflation gap, and called FY27 an aberration year. The Board approved a INR147 crore tender-offer buyback at INR215 per share, with promoters not participating.

segments.name: Fabric Care
segments.commentary: Led growth with 10.4% value growth; liquid detergents grew over 50% YoY (Henko, Ujala, MoreLight, Mr. White), and Ujala Young & Fresh fabric conditioner is performing well. Management said liquids carry lower margins than powder while the category scales.

segments.name: Home Care
segments.commentary: Excluding Pril, segment grew 15.3%, mainly on volume. Exo dishwash grew 23% on new variants, liquids, wider distribution and brand investment.

segments.name: Household Insecticides (HI)
segments.commentary: Coil share of HI portfolio fell to 30-35% from 43-45% a year ago as liquid vaporisers, aerosols and other formats scale; Maxo Agarbatti launched with a government-approved formulation. Profitability improvement is the priority.

segments.name: Personal Care (Margo)
segments.commentary: Grew a little over 11% in value on Margo pricing and a favourable GST base. Price increases of about 10-12% in Margo could not fully absorb palm oil and neem oil inflation; Margo Gentle glycerin soap (argan and moringa variants) launched in select markets.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the underlying business to sustain healthy growth in Q3 FY27, led by Fabric Care and new products.
Gross margins expected to remain under pressure in Q3; a full H2 margin recovery cannot be assumed unless commodity prices moderate and stabilise.
Margin recovery to be progressive; management said pricing alone cannot bridge a 13-14% inflation gap, and recovery is expected to begin in H2 depending on commodity stability.
Effective tax rate for H1 was 28.4%; full-year rate expected around 25-26%.
Working capital expected to gradually return to the 18-20 day medium-term range as conditions stabilise.
Internal aspiration to keep delivering double-digit growth; FY27 described as an aberration year, and no formal guidance given. INR5,000 crore revenue aspiration remains unchanged.
Dividend payout policy of 35-50% of profit retained; buyback of INR147 crore at INR215 per share via tender offer.
capex_capacity: Capital allocation: INR147 crore tender-offer buyback approved at INR215 per share; promoters and promoter group will not participate.
Management said cash will go to dividends, acquisitions, and investment in NPDs and new categories; M&A remains open, with no deal-size or return thresholds disclosed.
Working capital rose to 23 days from 15 days in March, mainly from higher raw material and finished goods inventory valued at higher input costs; debtor days fell over the same period.
Packaging is about 18-20% of cost base; HDPE and polypropylene prices up about 55-60% from pre-West Asia conflict levels.
demand_pricing: Rural outperformed urban; modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce grew strongly (modern trade double-digit); general trade subdued.
Price increases of about 4% taken in the quarter; further selective pricing and grammage cuts, especially in lower unit packs, under evaluation while balancing affordability.
Crude-linked inputs are 60-65% of consumption basket; inflation hit LABSA, SLES, soap noodles, palm oil, neem oil and packaging.
Renewed inflationary pressure in October 2026 adds near-term uncertainty; commodity prices had softened in July and early August.

Employee costs about 12% of revenue (up about 5.7% YoY); advertisement and promotion 7.4% of revenue (about 100 bps higher QoQ); other expenses about 13% of revenue vs 12.1% last year, driven by freight and export shipping costs.

qa_highlights.question: What steps are being taken to restore historical margins, and are new product launches or higher advertising part of this?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited NPDs with better margin profiles and a shift in product mix away from fixed-price LUPs, plus back-end cost efficiencies.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the price increase only about 4% when peers have raised prices, and how much more is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Pawan Agarwal said RM and PM inflation cost about 18% of sales, offset by 4% price and some mix, a net 13-13.5% gross margin hit. Pricing alone cannot close the 13-14% gap; recovery will be progressive, combining pricing, procurement, value engineering and mix.

qa_highlights.question: Has the liquid detergent mix diluted fabric care margins, and how should H2 margins be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Liquids carry lower margins than powder while scaling and requiring consumer-conversion spend; the Fabric Care margin hit is mainly input cost. Management declined to guide, calling FY27 an aberration year and saying margin recovery should start in H2 if commodities stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR5,000 crore revenue aspiration be reached, given Pril's exit and M&A timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the aspiration stands and M&A is not on hold; it is waiting for the right opportunity under a checklist. Growth will come from NPDs in categories not yet named, with launches in the last 2-3 years performing well.

qa_highlights.question: Has the Pril and Fa exit changed distributor terms, and what drove the working capital increase?
qa_highlights.answer: No change to distributor ROI or trade terms and no credit expansion; debtor days fell from March to September. The working capital increase is mainly raw material and finished goods inventory at higher costs.

qa_highlights.question: How does management view Margo's positioning in a crowded natural personal care segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said natural space still has loyal and young consumers, Margo will grow through extensions such as Margo Gentle, and other personal care opportunities will be addressed through other brands.

qa_highlights.question: Is crude dependence a major threat, and is management developing lower-crude products?
qa_highlights.answer: Crude-linked inputs are about 60-65% of the cost base. Management said R&D is developing lower-crude-dependence products with better margins, with some expected next year.

532927|2026-03.headline: eClerx Q4 FY26 operating revenue USD 122M, up 17% YoY but only 0.6% QoQ; FY26 revenue USD 469M, up 17.9%, with FY27 EBITDA guided at 24-28%.
532927|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue was USD 122 million, up 17% YoY and 0.6% QoQ, with INR revenue of INR 1,135 crores (up 24% YoY). tone.note: Management was confident on the 24% to 28% margin range, AI strategy and the Analytics segment (up 27% YoY), but candid that deal wins and ACV are down, shift-right is delaying decisions and FY26 ACV matching will be difficult; analysts pressed on deal economics and ACV trend.

532928|2026-06.headline: TARIL Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 10% YoY to INR559 crores, with EBITDA margin at 15.6%, as Changodar under-utilisation weighed on sequential growth.
532928|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue from operations was INR559 crores (+10% YoY) with EBITDA of INR87 crores (15.6% margin) and PAT of INR50 crores (8.9% margin). Consolidated revenue was INR572 crores, EBITDA INR110 crores (19.2%) and PAT INR64 crores. Sequentially growth slowed because Changodar capacity was reduced by expansion work, and management guides to recovery from August 2026 and normalisation from Q3 FY27. Order inflow was INR2,114 crores (+218% YoY) and the unexecuted order book reached INR6,630 crores (+26% YoY), including a PGCIL ultra-mega order above INR1,000 crores.

financial_highlights.change: Down sequentially, per management, due to Changodar utilisation

financial_highlights.value: around INR424 crores; debt-to-equity about 0.3x; debt-to-EBITDA about 1.1x
around 170 days (inventory about 85 days, receivables 130 days)

segments.name: Transformers (standalone, Changodar plant)
segments.commentary: Changodar utilisation is low due to expansion work; management says it will be 60-65% in FY27 and 80-85% in FY28. Changodar expansion capex is about INR150 crores, with completion expected by August 2026.

segments.name: Transformers (standalone, Moraiya plant)
segments.commentary: Utilisation was 57% per the presentation; management says it is running at about 60-65% and targets 80-85% going forward, with the Moraiya expansion scheduled for Q3 2027.

segments.name: Transformers (standalone, Odhav plant)
segments.commentary: Utilisation was shown at 100% in the presentation, per the analyst's reading of the utilisation chart.

segments.name: Subsidiaries (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Consolidated EBITDA margin of 19.2% against 15.6% standalone, which management attributes to integrated operations and subsidiary contribution.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: 25% revenue growth, 16% EBITDA margin (standalone, including other income) and PAT margin of 9-10%.
Consolidated EBITDA margin for FY27 could be around 20-21% or higher, per the CFO; subsidiaries may add about 100 bps.
Management targets about 30% growth in both domestic and export order inflow in FY27; export revenue to remain at 10-15% of business.
Revenue ambition of about $1 billion by FY29, which the CFO re-based to about INR8,000 crores because of a different rupee rate; FY28 guidance to be given in Q4 FY27.
Medium-term annual revenue capacity of INR5,000-6,000 crores from existing and expanded capacity; backward integration adds INR800-1,000 crores of third-party sales in phase two.
Backward integration is expected to add 200-300 bps to margins, starting from FY28.
Working capital target of 120-130 days on average, and inventory reduction expected from Q4 FY28.
capex_capacity: Existing transformer manufacturing capacity is 75,000 MVA+ across plants; the immediate priority is utilisation and throughput, not new transformer capacity.
CTC facility (8,000 MTPA Phase I; 24,000 MTPA Phase II) targeted for commissioning by Q2 FY27.

Pressboard and insulation facility (5,000 MTPA Phase I; 10,000 MTPA Phase II) targeted for Q3 FY27; RIP bushings (3,000 units p.a. Phase I; 6,000 Phase II) targeted for Q4 FY27; fabrication (25,000 MTPA Phase I; 50,000 MTPA Phase II) targeted for Q1 FY28. CRGO processing facility is already operational.
Backward integration is expected to cover 80-85% of raw material in-house; total investment INR900-1,000 crores, with finance leasing of about INR500 crores after leasing of plant machinery.
Raw material procurement has been secured up to December 2026, when backward integration facilities are expected to be running.
demand_pricing: Order book is executable over 18-24 months; the PGCIL ultra-mega order (above INR1,000 crores, 30 months) is an exception, per management.
Inquiries under negotiation total about INR23,000 crores, with an 80% domestic and 20% export mix; the historical win ratio is 10-15%.
Q1 orders: PGCIL above INR1,000 crores; GETCO about INR228 crores; RRVPNL INR175 crores; US export order from PDC AK LPIV, LLC about INR150 crores.
All Indian tenders are quoted on an L1 basis; management expects more PGCIL inquiries under negotiation.
Price variation clauses protect margins, per management; the company has also stocked raw materials to hedge geopolitical risk.
Q1 mix was heavy in 220 kV, 400 kV and 765 kV ratings because of Changodar constraints; mix is expected to spread across all ratings by end-August 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 revenue slowdown due to supply chain or geopolitical issues?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to lower Changodar utilisation, not supply; raw material is covered up to December 2026, so geopolitics is not affecting raw material much.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall to about 12% of sales?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there is no one-off; other expenses were about INR66 crores vs INR69.74 crores last year, so there is no major reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 16% EBITDA margin guidance standalone or consolidated, and does it include other income?
qa_highlights.answer: 16% is standalone at transformer level and includes other income; consolidated margin (19% in Q1) is higher, and the CFO guided consolidated FY27 margin to around 20-21%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the $1 billion revenue target still valid, and how does it reconcile with 25% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Target re-based to about INR8,000 crores by FY29 (from INR9,600 crores at old rupee rate), from INR5,000-6,000 crores capacity plus INR800-1,000 crores third-party backward integration sales.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory build-up and debt: how will working capital and capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is high as a hedge until backward integration is running; inventory reduction starts from Q4 FY28. Management says no increase in debt planned, with capex funded by cash, QIP balance of about INR145 crores, leasing (about INR500 crores) and internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: What is the HVDC timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 9 months are needed to complete repair work on HVDC, after which PGCIL would empanel the company for a first trial order; full HVDC manufacturing is 15-16 months away.

qa_highlights.question: Will Changodar utilisation normalise, and what about Moraiya at 57%?
qa_highlights.answer: Changodar is expected at 60-65% in FY27 and 80-85% in FY28; Moraiya at 60-65% (57% per chart) is expected to reach 80-85% after Q3, with raw material protection through December.

risks_watch: Changodar ramp-up: utilisation at 60-65% through FY27; the August 2026 start and Q3 FY27 stabilisation are key checkpoints.
Backward integration timelines: CTC (Q2 FY27), pressboard (Q3 FY27), bushings (Q4 FY27) and fabrication (Q1 FY28) are at risk from delays such as the earlier Changodar slippage.
Working capital and leverage: NWC of about 170 days, high inventory, borrowings rising from FY25; management targets 120-130 days.
CRGO steel anti-dumping investigation by DGTR may raise raw material costs; management has not quantified impact.
Geopolitical risk to raw material supply and execution beyond December 2026.
Margin sustainability in FY27 at 16% standalone if mix shifts toward lower-rated transformers as Changodar recovers, per analyst question; management said no risk.
532928|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term outlook and order book, but defensive on the Q1 sequential slowdown and reluctant to quantify the Changodar, Moraiya and CRGO impacts. Several answers were repetitive or unquantified, and the $1 billion target was revised to INR8,000 crores without a clear bridge.
key_quotes: We are committed to providing only those guidance parameters that we are confident of achieving, going forward, our focus is firmly on delivering on our commitments.
The impact was purely project related temporary in nature.
Importantly this does not reflect any weakness in demand or order inflow or execution capability.

rows.why: Management guides 25% FY27 revenue growth against Q1 standalone revenue of INR559 crore (+10% YoY), with Changodar at 60-65% utilisation in FY27 and 80-85% in FY28 and order book at INR6,630 crore (+26% YoY).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only 60-65% at Moraiya and Changodar, below the 80%+ threshold, and the immediate priority is throughput rather than new transformer capacity, so a fresh capex announcement is less likely in the window, though the INR900-1,000 crore backward-integration programme is already committed.

rows.why: Q1 standalone growth was only 10% YoY and sequentially slower, so the 25% FY27 guidance needs a sharp H2 ramp before any upgrade is credible.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.why: Q1 order inflow INR2,114 crore (+218% YoY) with a PGCIL order above INR1,000 crore (30 months) and INR23,000 crore of inquiries under negotiation at a 10-15% win ratio, with management targeting ~30% order growth in FY27.

rows.when: inventory reduction only from Q4 FY28
rows.why: NWC was about 170 days in FY26 (inventory 85 days, receivables 130 days) and inventory is being held as a hedge until backward integration runs, so the 120-130 day target is not expected within the window.

rows.why: A DGTR probe could raise CRGO steel costs, but management has not quantified the impact, and raw material is only covered up to December 2026.

tone.note: Management was confident on the order book (INR6,630 crore, +26%) and the medium-term outlook but defensive on the Q1 sequential slowdown from Changodar and reluctant to quantify CRGO and Moraiya impacts; analysts pushed on the margin bridge and the re-based INR8,000 crore revenue target.

532928|2026-09.headline: TARIL Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 66% YoY to INR709 crore and EBITDA margin widened to 16.1%, with order book at INR7,237 crore (+32% YoY).
532928|2026-09.overview: Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR709 crore (+66% YoY, +27% QoQ) and EBITDA was INR114 crore (+203% YoY), with margin at 16.1% versus 8.8% a year earlier, which management attributed to higher utilisation and operating leverage. H1 FY27 revenue was INR1,268 crore (+35% YoY) and EBITDA INR185 crore (14.6% margin). Order inflow in Q2 was INR1,169 crore (+97% YoY off a low base), and the unexecuted order book stood at INR7,237 crore, executable over 18-24 months. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 25% growth and 9-10% PAT margin, while working-capital days (about 154) remain the key drag on cash flow.

financial_highlights.change: vs 8.8% in Q2 FY26 and 13.3% in Q1 FY27
+47% YoY; margin 14.6% vs 13.4% in H1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: approx. INR575 crore (LT ~INR125 crore, ST ~INR449 crore)

segments.name: Power transformers / high voltage
segments.commentary: About 55-60% of the order book is 400 kV and above. Management said about 56% of power transformer execution in Q2 was in this class. Q2 margin gains were attributed to higher utilisation at the Moraiya plant.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports were about 8% of Q2 revenue and about 15% of the order book. Export inquiries are about 20% of the INR21,000 crore inquiry pipeline.

segments.name: Backward integration (CTC, bushings, tanks, pressboard)
segments.commentary: CTC plant to be commissioned around Diwali, with commercial manufacturing by Q4 FY27; about 60% of its 3,000 MTPA capacity is captive. Management expects 200-300 bps margin expansion once integration is complete.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance maintained: 25% revenue growth (target 25% and beyond) with 9-10% PAT margin, per management's reply to analyst questions.
Working capital cycle to fall below 120 days, targeted from end of FY27, with 110-120 days in the year; this is expected to make free cash flow positive.
Changodar expansion (about 35,000 MVA total capacity, incremental capex about INR150 crore) to start commercial production around Diwali; Moraiya EHV capacity to follow.
Management targets about USD1 billion revenue, expected late FY29 or early 2030, including bushings, pressboard, CRGO, CTC, and tank sales; no additional capex is planned.
HVDC converter transformer capability expected within 18 months; BESS transformer orders expected in the current quarter.
capex_capacity: Changodar: total capacity to reach about 35,000 MVA (incremental about 25,000 MVA on 12,000 MVA existing) for distribution, IDT, renewable transformers, and small power and LV transformers up to 132 kV, plus large power transformers up to 220 kV; capex about INR150 crore; commercial production around Diwali.
Moraiya: planned EHV transformer capacity of about 22,000 MVA after Changodar is complete; insulation/pressboard plant is adding about 30% manufacturing capacity at Moraiya once functional.
CTC plant (3,000 MTPA): machinery being installed; commissioning before Diwali, trial runs in Nov-Dec, commercial manufacturing by Q4 FY27, external sales from Q1 FY28.
Q2 FY27 production was about 9,500 MVA. Management's ideal utilisation is about 90%, targeted in FY28 or FY29.
HVDC: repair of a PGCIL transformer takes about 4-5 months, then 6-7 months of operation before qualification; re-engineering is under way.
demand_pricing: Order inflow: NPCIL Kaiga Units 5 and 6 generator transformers (first nuclear order, 400 kV+, competed with Crompton and others; repeatable). Megha Engineering order (35-month execution). Damodar Valley Corporation order (500 MVA and 200 MVA; 15-28 months). GETCO order (80 and 125 MVAr reactors, 500 MVA auto-transformers; 24-30 months). APTRANSCO LOI. PGCIL order of about INR1,000 crore (24-28 months; manufacturing from December FY28).
Inquiries under negotiation are INR21,000 crore, about 80% domestic and 20% export, split equally between government and private customers.

Realisation is about INR7 lakh per MVA on average. Price variation clauses are billed every quarter. Management attributed about 7-8% of revenue growth to price variation, with no list price increase in Q2.
Competition: management sees no major price war, since competitors also hold large order books. Kanohar competes in 132 kV and 220 kV.

Raw materials (transoil, CRGO, copper) remain high-priced; Middle East disruption has not hit imports materially, but timely availability of some critical raw materials is an issue. Inventory is sufficient until Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Details of Kaiga and Megha orders; is Kaiga repeatable?
qa_highlights.answer: Kaiga was competed against Crompton and others for generator transformers at 400 kV+; management expects repeat NPCIL orders. Greenfield nuclear transformer content is about 15-18% of the transformer cost.

qa_highlights.question: Mix of order book by voltage class?
qa_highlights.answer: About 55-60% of the order book is 400 kV and above; about 56% of Q2 power transformer execution was in this class.

qa_highlights.question: When will free cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to cut working-capital days from end-FY27, targeting below 120 days and 110-120 days this year, which should lead to positive cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation per MVA and capex on Changodar?
qa_highlights.answer: Average realisation about INR7 lakh per MVA; Changodar capex about INR150 crore for about 35,000 MVA capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance looks conservative given H2 run rate; can FY27 revenue reach INR3,200 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it maintains the INR3,200 crore FY27 revenue target and the 9-10% PAT margin. It needs to execute about INR900 crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a path to USD1 billion revenue and does it need more capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects USD1 billion by late FY29 or early FY30 from transformers plus bushings, pressboard, CRGO, CTC, and tank sales. It said no additional capex is needed.

risks_watch: Working-capital intensity: inventory about INR654 crore and receivables about INR1,053 crore against INR1,268 crore H1 revenue. Operating cash flow conversion is weak relative to PAT.
Commissioning timelines for Changodar (around Diwali) and CTC (Q3 FY27, commercial from Q4) could slip; the CTC timeline was questioned against earlier guidance of Q2 FY27.
Raw material price volatility and supply of critical inputs amid Middle East disruption; part of the order book has price variation clauses, but the rest does not.
Retention money of about INR200 crore (5-10% of order value) is tied up on the balance sheet.
HVDC and converter transformer qualification is roughly 1.5 years away; BESS orders are not yet in hand.
Pricing: about 7-8% of revenue growth came from price variation; underlying realisation trends need to be tracked.
532928|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on demand and order visibility, and on margins and the expansion timeline. Management was less precise on cash-flow timing, CTC commissioning dates (which shifted from Q2 to Q3 FY27), and HVDC qualification.
key_quotes: As of 30th September 2026, our unexecuted order book stood at 7,237 crore, up by 32% year-on-year, providing strong revenue visibility over the medium term.
EBITDA margin improved to 16.1% compared to 8.8% in Q2FY26 and 13.3% in Q1 FY27.
Following our Q2 performance, we remain confident of achieving FY27 guidance and continue to remain on track with our growth plans for the full year.
So, we are pretty much sure that we'll reach USD1 billion.

rows.why: Changodar capex about INR150 crore takes capacity from 12,000 MVA to about 35,000 MVA (+208%), with commercial production around Diwali; CTC 3,000 MTPA plant commissioning before Diwali and commercial manufacturing by Q4 FY27, though CTC timing already slipped from Q2 to Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book of INR7,237 crore (+32% YoY) executable over 18-24 months with Q2 order inflow of INR1,169 crore (+97% YoY), and Changodar adds about 25,000 MVA of capacity around Diwali on a 12,000 MVA base.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: CTC commissioning already shifted from Q2 to Q3 FY27, Changodar commissioning depends on a Diwali date, and H2 must deliver about INR900 crore per quarter (H1 averaged about INR634 crore) to hit INR3,200 crore, so slippage is a real risk.

rows.why: BESS transformer orders are expected in the current quarter but none are in hand, and HVDC converter transformer capability is about 18 months away with qualification about 1.5 years out, so launches are conditional.

rows.why: NWC is about 154 days (inventory ~93, receivables ~117, payables ~56) and management targets 110-120 days this year, which should make free cash flow positive, though it has been less precise on timing.

rows.label: PGCIL and nuclear repeat orders
rows.why: PGCIL order of about INR1,000 crore has manufacturing from December FY28, and management expects repeat NPCIL orders after the Kaiga win at 400 kV+, with inquiries at INR21,000 crore (about 20% export).

rows.why: Price variation contributed about 7-8% of revenue growth in Q2 with no list price increase, and it is billed every quarter, though part of the order book lacks such clauses.

532929|2026-03.headline: Brigade FY26 pre-sales fell 5% to INR 7,424 crore on approval delays; FY27 pre-sales guided to at least 20% growth, aiming for INR 9,000 crore.
532929|2026-03.overview: FY26 pre-sales were INR 7,424 crore, down 5% YoY, as launches slipped: 8.3 million sq ft launched against a 12 million sq ft plan, with about 3.3 million sq ft pushed into FY27 (mostly Chennai). Q4 pre-sales were INR 2,521 crore (up 44% QoQ by value) from 4 million sq ft of launches. Consolidated FY26 revenue rose 11% to INR 5,909 crore with EBITDA of INR 1,638 crore (28% margin), and PAT after minority interest was INR 644 crore. Operating cash flow weakened because of higher construction spend, and management expects it to rise in line with sales growth. Management says the approval issues are largely behind it, and it has guided FY27 launches of about 11.5-12 million sq ft.

segments.name: Real Estate (FY26)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR 4,002 crore (+11% YoY) with EBITDA INR 525 crore. Q4 turnover INR 1,026 crore with EBITDA INR 142 crore. Management says operating POCM margins are in the high-20s to around 30%, while reported margins are diluted by revenue recognition mix.

segments.name: Leasing (FY26)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR 1,303 crore (+12% YoY) with EBITDA INR 906 crore (+18%). Q4 turnover INR 337 crore with EBITDA INR 228 crore. Split: office INR 877 crore, retail INR 220 crore, management business INR 206 crore. Normalised EBITDA margin is above 80%; facility management (about INR 200 crore a year) runs at about 15%.

segments.name: Hospitality (FY26)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR 604 crore (+13% YoY) with EBITDA INR 207 crore. Q4 turnover INR 160 crore with EBITDA INR 60 crore. Q4 occupancy 78%, ADR up 8% QoQ, RevPAR up 13% QoQ; FY26 RevPAR +6% on ADR +7%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales: at least 20% growth over FY26, aiming for about INR 9,000 crore, conditional on current sentiment and market conditions holding.

FY27 residential launch pipeline of about 11.5-11.6 million sq ft with GDV of about INR 11,900 crore: Bengaluru 4.5 million sq ft, Chennai 3 million sq ft, Hyderabad 3 million sq ft. Launches are expected to be back-ended, with Morgan Heights Phase 1 (1 million sq ft) relaunch in Q1 FY27.

Commercial pipeline of about 10 million sq ft over FY27-FY28 with capex of about INR 6,000 crore over 4 years (INR 1,200-1,700 crore a year). About 4.5 million sq ft is targeted for FY27 and about INR 800 crore of rent is expected from it and ongoing projects; leasing aimed at least at double FY26 levels.
Operating cash flow expected to grow in percentage terms close to sales growth, a few hundred bps lower.
Debt-equity expected to stay well below 1x even as commercial debt rises; residential capex is self-funded, and commercial capex is a mix of debt and cash flow.
capex_capacity: Land bank of 57 million sq ft, of which residential is about 75%; focus on Bengaluru and Hyderabad, moderately Chennai.
FY26 launches: 8.3 million sq ft (GDV about INR 10,000 crore) vs plan of 12 million sq ft. Q4 launches: 4 million sq ft (GDV about INR 4,500 crore).

Launch timing: Hyderabad 2 million sq ft Kokapet plot in Q3 and 1 million sq ft Northern Hyderabad project in Q4; Bengaluru launches in Q2-Q3 (including East Bengaluru OMR in Q3); Chennai Morgan Heights relaunch in Q1 FY27 plus two projects in Q3 and Q4. North Bengaluru project is delayed by bylaw changes requiring redesign.

Office: Whitefield JV with Bain (50:50, pure equity partners) on 10.8 acres opposite ITPL, with about 2 million sq ft of office and a 250-key 5-star hotel, targeted for completion in about 40 months after approval. Leasing: about 3 million sq ft of new completions expected in FY27. WTC Bengaluru: Amazon vacated about 630,000 sq ft, with about 100,000 sq ft already leased.
demand_pricing: Pre-sales mix FY26: sustenance 57%, launches 43%. Q4 launch share of pre-sales about 55%. Geographic split (Q4 and FY26 approx. same): Bengaluru 65%, Hyderabad 20%, Chennai 15%.
Conversion of site visits steady at 10-12% across cities; NRI buyers around 10% of pre-sales value; some markets showing longer conversion cycles.

FY26 average realisation up 9% YoY to INR 12,107 per sq ft. Like-for-like price increase high single digits (8-9%); management plans 7-9% annual price increases after launch. Upcoming launch APR around INR 10,000 per sq ft vs inventory above INR 12,000 per sq ft; overall APR increase of 13% was partly mix-driven.

Ticket-size mix: ultra-luxury about 30% of portfolio, expected to decline. Most FY27 launch tickets below INR 3 crore; affordable up to INR 75 lakh, mid-segment up to INR 1.5 crore, premium up to INR 3 crore.
Unsold inventory about 7.5 million sq ft. Residential buyer base: GCC and IT are the largest; IT services about 26% of leasing portfolio.

Leasing: about 1.1 million sq ft leased in FY26; GCCs 58% of the lease book; top anchor tenants (above 1 lakh sq ft) are 65% of the portfolio. Lease rent escalation expected at 10-15% for Amazon's vacated space at WTC Bengaluru. Rental collections 99%.
Commercial monetisation (strata sales) annual run-rate about INR 550 crore; Twin Towers to be exited in FY27, keeping about 100,000 sq ft of common amenities.
Hospitality demand anchored in domestic travel; foreign arrivals and MICE were hit by Middle East tensions.

qa_highlights.question: Plan to fill WTC Bengaluru after Amazon exit, and expected rental uplift?
qa_highlights.answer: Amazon vacated about 630,000 sq ft; about 100,000 sq ft already leased on a couple of floors. Leasing is expected floor-wise or 2-3 floors at a time over the next couple of quarters, with 10-15% rent mark-to-market (up to 20% for half-floors).

qa_highlights.name: Cumulative GDV available for launch over two years and land replenishment?
qa_highlights.question: What is the cumulative GDV available for launch over the next two years, and what is the land replenishment strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Rolling four-quarter pipeline of 11.5 million sq ft and INR 11,900-12,000 crore GDV. Land bank of 57 million sq ft, of which about 75% is residential. Replenishment focused on Bengaluru and Hyderabad, moderately Chennai.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 9,000 crore pre-sales guidance conservative given unsold inventory and launch conversion history?
qa_highlights.answer: Management accepted it is somewhat conservative. It cited Chennai launches selling more evenly across construction, and launch slippage into H2 leaving less time to sell in-year. Management aims to push inventory sales and pull launches forward.

qa_highlights.question: Quarter-wise launch phasing and approval status for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Hyderabad about 1 million sq ft in Q3 and another 1 million in Q4; Morgan Heights 1 million sq ft relaunch in Q1; Bengaluru launches in Q2-Q3. The primary approval issues are considered resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Cash flow trajectory and collections trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Collections were flat as launches were deferred early in FY26; that cash is now converting. Operating cash flow is expected to grow in percentage terms close to sales growth, a few hundred bps lower.

qa_highlights.question: Reported margin weakness in resi and leasing, and when will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Resi reported margins reflect completion-based recognition of older, earlier-sold projects that did not capture recent price increases; POCM operating margin is around 30%. Leasing is above 80% on a normalised basis; reported margins are diluted by about INR 200 crore of facility management revenue at about 15% and about INR 35 crore of fit-out recoveries, plus a Q4 accounting gross-up.

qa_highlights.question: What are the near-term hotel trends, and what occupancy or ARR gains are expected for FY27 including the Kochi rebranding?

qa_highlights.question: Parvez Qazi: Bengaluru ticket-size mix and office capex phasing?

qa_highlights.question: Parvez Qazi / Biplab Debbarma: office assets beyond FY29 and construction status?

qa_highlights.question: Harsh Pathak: FY27 residential revenue recognition and margin; FY28 outlook?

qa_highlights.question: Harsh Pathak: INR28 Cr PE payment and INR317 Cr equity-method investment?
qa_highlights.answer: INR28 Cr is distributions to a JV partner. The INR317 Cr equity-method balance relates to Vibrancy Real Estates, where Bain Capital invested in Q1 and the entity became a JV, so it was reclassified out of consolidation.

qa_highlights.question: Vasudev: Q2 business development and timing of the ~INR2,000-2,300 Cr balance land payable?

532934|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 18.6% YoY to INR175.5 crore; FY27 guidance deferred to Q1 FY27 results.

Capacity utilisation improved to about 78%. FY26 consolidated revenue was INR567 crore, with growth held back by SOP deferrals and model-specific weakness. Profitability was hit by mark-to-market losses on investments and a one-time INR3.6 crore employee benefit charge from Labour Code implementation. The company also announced the JV stake divestment, a tooling hive-off and a battery merger, and said FY27 guidance will come with Q1 FY27 results.

qa_highlights.question: How is PPAP handling raw material inflation from the West Asia conflict, and what is the margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Supplier price increases are being passed through to keep customer lines running. About 50% is already covered by the pass-on policy, and the remaining 50% will be discussed once the situation stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: How will the JV stake sale proceeds be used, and will debt be reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt is INR103 crore and gross debt about INR195 crore. The company will keep debt around these levels for FY27 and hold the funds for strategic needs, with capex funded from internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: Why did tooling sales decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tooling sales are tied to SOPs. Q4 FY25 had a high base from SOPs, and a large Maruti model drove Q4 FY26. Management expects significant tooling sales in FY27 given the pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: When will the battery business break even, and what is the Q4 loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 battery loss was about INR40 lakh against INR1.2 crore a year earlier. The segment is expected to be profitable at standalone PBT level in FY27, with full utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 margin and utilisation expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is expected at 80-82% over the next year against about 78% in Q4. Margin gains are expected from utilisation, solar power and employee reforms. Standalone EBITDA margin excluding the wage code impact was 13% in Q4 versus 11% a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: What new programs, customers and content per vehicle exist?
qa_highlights.answer: VinFast and Euler were added in FY26 and Kia and Mahindra programs start in FY27. Content per vehicle averages INR2,500-3,500, with a range of INR1,000 to INR10,000.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 margin expected to improve from SOP ramp-ups and price recoveries; management declined to quantify EBITDA margin improvement due to raw material volatility.

About 68% of the approximately 380 bps auto-parts gross margin reduction has been recovered from customers; balance under negotiation, expected to settle during H2 FY27 (about 6 months lag). Management expects margin recovery by Q1 FY28.
New-SOP contribution to top line expected to rise from about 10% in H1 to about 15% in H2 FY27.
Battery business targeted to reach zero EBITDA in Q3 FY27.
Hutchinson sealing technology: first order-win breakthrough targeted in Q4 FY27.
Chennai plant expected fully operational by Q3 FY27; further capacity expansion to be evaluated in Q3 based on order book and utilisation.
Interim dividend of INR1.5 per equity share declared.
Two additional aftermarket regional warehouses planned (West and South) by end of FY27, with an East warehouse next year.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation about 78% in Q2 FY27 versus 73% in Q1 FY27 and 68% in Q2 FY26.
New Chennai plant progressing; expected fully operational by Q3 FY27.

Further capacity expansion to be decided in Q3 FY27 based on order book and utilisation.
Proceeds from JV stake divestment invested in short-term funds pending strategic deployment.

Raw material costs elevated; pass-through to OEMs lags, raising reported revenue without proportionate gross profit, which mechanically dilutes margin percentage.
Battery business faces volatility in cell prices, cell quality consistency, pricing pressure and shorter delivery timelines.
Counterfeiting of aftermarket products has emerged in the market; company has issued newspaper notices and added packaging countermeasures.
Order books typically execute over 1 to 4 years; development cycle shortened from about 3 years to about 2 years.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR429 crore H1 order wins translate into revenue over coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said orders typically execute over 2 to 4 years, with some executing within 1 year; ramp-ups are led by Maruti and Tata Motors programs.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margin recover, and when, given cost pass-through negotiations?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said 380 bps of auto-parts gross margin was lost, 68% already recovered, balance in negotiation with about 6-month settlement lag; margin recovery expected by Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margins improve further and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO declined to quantify, citing volatility, but expects significant H2 margin improvement from new SOPs and price recoveries.

qa_highlights.question: What is the progress on the Hutchinson sealing technology partnership?
qa_highlights.answer: Technical presentations held with customers in Q2; first Hutchinson-based order win targeted for Q4 FY27. Current wins rely on in-house products.

qa_highlights.question: What are the non-auto and export prospects for Industrial Products?
qa_highlights.answer: Targeting air handling units and electrical panels, including data-centre cooling demand; early exports to the US and African markets; about 30% of tooling revenue is from non-auto customers.

qa_highlights.question: What milestones are needed for the battery business to break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects zero EBITDA in Q3 FY27, after Q2 EBITDA loss narrowed to INR30 lakhs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the customer pipeline with JSW, MG, VinFast, and Volkswagen?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders received from JSW standalone and JSW MG Motors (Windsor); VinFast supplied and new business under negotiation; Volkswagen platform not yet announced; Tata Motors new platforms underway.

qa_highlights.question: Progress on aftermarket target of 10% of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Aftermarket currently about 5% of revenue; 154 distributors, adding distributors in Q3 and Q4, with online presence via Amazon and Flipkart and warehouse expansion.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery depends on settling pending OEM price revisions in H2 FY27; the lag is about 6 months.
Raw material and crude oil price volatility, linked to geopolitical disruptions, continues daily.
Battery business still loss-making; Q3 zero-EBITDA target and Avinya merger (by end Q4 FY27) subject to approvals.
Hutchinson-based order win is targeted for Q4 FY27 and has not yet been achieved.
Macro risks flagged by management: inflation, possible interest rate hikes, geopolitical uncertainty.
Counterfeiting of aftermarket products; watch distributor and online channel impact.
Higher share of low-margin tooling and battery revenue may continue to weigh on gross margin.

key_quotes: It is important to note that the pass-through of increased raw material costs to customers results in a corresponding increase in reported revenue without a proportionate increase in gross profit.

532937|2026-03.headline: Kuantum Papers Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 22% QoQ to INR48 crore (15.90% margin) on NSR of INR3,700/MT, despite input cost pressure.
532937|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operational income was INR301 crore, up 4% QoQ, driven by NSR improvement to INR3,700/MT, while input costs rose about INR2,000/MT amid the West Asia conflict. EBITDA reached INR48 crore (margin 15.90%, up 234 bps QoQ) and PAT INR14 crore (margin 4.75%, up 137 bps QoQ). For FY26, revenue fell 1% YoY to INR1,093 crore and EBITDA was INR162 crore (14.80% margin), with NSR down about INR2,000/MT and costs up about INR3,200/MT. Management guided to volume growth to about 2,30,000 MT and EBITDA margin of 18-20% over the next few years, with PM3 upgrade and pulp (DDS) commissioning slated for mid-June to July 2026.

segments.name: Notebook paper
segments.commentary: Share fell from about 22% of sales before the September GST change to about 7-8% now; management intends to exit the segment after machine upgrades, citing reversal of input tax credit at nil GST.

segments.name: Copier, high-end printing, specialty paper
segments.commentary: Copier share is growing steadily; Maplitho and size grades target high-end printing; specialty grades targeted at 20-30% of production volume.

segments.name: Paperboard
segments.commentary: Management noted MIP for paperboard continues with a one-year extension; paperboard was not discussed in detail.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top line expected at INR1,400-1,500 crore, rising gradually to INR1,600 crore; FY28 INR1,600-1,700 crore (management's medium-term view: INR1,600-1,700 crore).
Volumes to rise from about 1,62,000-1,63,000 MT to about 2,30,000 MT, a 40-50% increase, at utilisation above 90-95%.
EBITDA margin target of 18-20% over the medium term.
Operating cost reduction of 5-8% of total manufacturing cost once AI/digital projects are fully implemented, expected across machines by FY27-FY28.
Peak long-term debt of INR650-675 crore by end-2027, reducing INR100-200 crore a year thereafter; annual repayments of INR170-180 crore over the next 2-3 years.
Remaining capex of about INR125 crore to be spent in FY27; no new capex planned beyond current projects, though another expansion may be considered in about two years.
Tissue paper project deferred, not shelved, until debt is under control.
Wheat straw prices expected to ease after rice sowing starts in early June; Q1 season expected to be lean with pricing pressure.
capex_capacity: PM2 rebuild completed March 2026, capacity raised to 75 TPD; PM1 rebuild in December 2025 added about 20 TPD on average in Q4.
PM3 upgrade delayed due to German imported parts; now planned by mid-June/July 2026 (previously around May).
Displacement Digester System (DDS) for wood pulping under extensive testing, commissioning targeted by mid-June; pulp capacity to come on stream by PM3 commissioning (July).
Two-stage recausticizing plant and 80 TPD synchro sheeter commissioned; overall utilisation above 92% on PM1, PM2 and PM4 (OE levels).
Cost of PM3 upgrade not expected to escalate versus the earlier INR140-150 crore estimate.
demand_pricing: Pricing firmed in Q4 on higher demand, but May price hikes partly reversed; management says it holds prices at about INR69,000-70,000/ton.
Low-priced imports persisted through FY26, lowering domestic prices; West Asia freight disruption reduced import volumes in Q4, with risk of China/Indonesia trade diversion.

Anti-subsidy application expected to be processed by FY-end (March 2027); anti-dumping application on writing and printing paper typically takes 1.5-2 years; MIP for writing/printing paper still under review.
Global pulp prices at about USD600-700/ton, expected to stay in that range given new capacity additions.
Wheat straw prices up about 50-60% YoY, with the fuel-use competition now unwound; wood chip prices broadly stable.
Chemical input costs up about 3-5% for some chemicals; the company is absorbing rather than passing these through.
Dealer network of about 90 committed dealers plus about 20 irregular dealers; Gulf and North African export markets being developed.

qa_highlights.question: Are import pressures visible now, and will they hurt pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes from China and Indonesia did not arrive in Q4 due to West Asia freight disruption; the impact may return later, and the industry is pursuing Gulf export opportunities. Comment restricted to white paper, not paperboard.

qa_highlights.question: Current debt and capex plans for FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term debt was INR720 crore on 31 March 2026; peak debt of INR650-675 crore by end-2027. Remaining capex of about INR125 crore in FY27 and no new capex planned beyond existing projects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of PM3 and pulp capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: PM3 delayed due to German parts, now targeted by mid-June; pulp upgrade to come on stream alongside PM3 in July 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How will the new capacity be absorbed, given the demand environment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 95%+ utilisation; cited the dealer network, Gulf and Northern Africa markets, and a 25-30% specialty grade mix as offsets.

qa_highlights.question: How much opex can be cut from AI and capacity additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 5-8% of total manufacturing cost reduction once AI systems are deployed across machines, progressing machine by machine and mill-wide, with completion targeted by FY27-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company refinance or reduce cost of funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Average long-term cost of funds is about 8.5%; management is exploring FCNRB and cheaper funding options. Buybacks are not being considered for now.

risks_watch: Import pressure from China and Indonesia, and dumping, could return once freight normalises; the anti-subsidy outcome is a key dependency.
Ramp-up risk: volumes must rise 40-50% to about 2,30,000 MT, with pulp capacity and PM3 timelines already slipping.
Leverage is high: long-term debt of INR720 crore at about 8.5% average cost, with annual repayments of INR170-180 crore.
Lean season expected in the next 2-3 months with historical pricing dips; management expects reversal around September.
Input costs (chemicals, wheat straw, pulp) remain elevated; the company is absorbing chemical cost increases.
Notebook exit reduces the top line and may affect volume in the near term.
532937|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on operating momentum and medium-term targets, but cautious on near-term pricing and input costs; several answers were corrective or deferred, including the tissue project and the MIP and ADD outcomes. Management was defensive when challenged on capacity absorption and debt.
key_quotes: Encouragingly, pricing began to fir m up in the fourth quarter, supported by higher demand, though was dampened a bit by the cost-led adjustments due to the ongoing West Asia conflict.
So, you can expect the top line to be in the range of INR1,600 crores to INR1,700 crores thereabouts.
And we are not foreseeing any kind of stiff competition, particularly for us.
It's a conscious call not to remain in this segment.

rows.why: PM3 upgrade (INR140 crore, under construction) and DDS pulp commissioning are slated for mid-June to July 2026, lifting volume from about 1,62,000-1,63,000 MT to about 2,30,000 MT (40-50%), though PM3 has already slipped from May on German parts.

rows.why: Volumes guided to about 2,30,000 MT from 1,62,885 MT in FY26 (40-50% up) at 95%+ utilisation, but current utilisation is already above 92% and the ramp depends on PM3 and pulp timelines that have slipped.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says no new capex beyond current projects (about INR125 crore remaining in FY27) and tissue paper is deferred until debt is controlled; peak debt INR650-675 crore by end-2027 with INR170-180 crore annual repayments, so another expansion is only possibly considered in about two years.

rows.why: FY27 revenue guide of INR1,400-1,500 crore is 28-37% above FY26's INR1,093 crore, but it depends on unbuilt volume and the company is absorbing input cost increases with pricing pressure in the lean season.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: PM3 already slipped from May to mid-June/July 2026 and DDS pulp timelines are slipping; lean Q1 season with pricing dips, and import risk from China/Indonesia could return once freight normalises.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Specialty and high-end grades (Maplitho, size grades) are targeted at 20-30% of production volume, but no specific launch dates or new product numbers were given.

rows.label: AI/digital opex cut of 5-8% of manufacturing cost
rows.why: Management expects 5-8% of total manufacturing cost reduction as AI systems roll out machine by machine, with completion targeted by FY27-FY28.

rows.label: Peak debt INR650-675 crore by end-2027, then INR100-200 crore a year lower
rows.why: Long-term debt was INR720 crore on 31 March 2026 with annual repayments of INR170-180 crore; average cost of funds about 8.5%, and FCNRB refinancing is being explored.

rows.label: Gulf and North African export markets
rows.why: Being developed alongside a dealer network of about 90 committed dealers plus about 20 irregular dealers, but no export volume or revenue figures were given.

tone.note: Management was confident on operating momentum (utilisation above 92%, 18-20% margin target) but cautious on near-term pricing, input costs and import risk, and defensive when challenged on capacity absorption and debt; analysts pushed on capacity absorption, debt and cost of funds.

532937|2026-06.headline: Kuantum Q1 FY27 operational income rose 36% YoY to INR304 crore, but EBITDA was flat at INR40 crore (13.2% margin) as input costs outran price gains.
532937|2026-06.overview: Paper sales volume grew 35% YoY to 42,922 metric tons, and blended NSR improved about INR3,400/ton QoQ. Cost per ton rose about INR4,200 QoQ on raw material, chemical and fuel inflation linked to the West Asia conflict, so EBITDA stayed broadly flat YoY and PAT was INR6 crore. Management cut its FY27 top-line expectation to INR1,300 crore-plus from the earlier INR1,400-1,500 crore and pushed the 16-18% EBITDA margin target to the year-end. PM3 rebuild completion, pulp capacity additions and anti-dumping applications were the main operational updates.

segments.name: Paper (writing & printing, copier, maplitho)
segments.commentary: Realisation around INR68,000-69,000/ton per management, targeted to reach INR72,000-75,000 in 4-6 months. Specialty grades are just under 20% of mix (18-19% stated), target 30%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top line revised to INR1,300 crore-plus, versus earlier INR1,400-1,500 crore guidance; management said realisations are running below earlier expected levels.
EBITDA margin at least 16-18% by year-end; management says Q3 onwards is when these margins should be visible, not Q2.
FY28 top line expected INR1,400-1,500 crore; FY29-30 conservatively INR1,500 crore at current pricing, INR1,600-1,650 crore if pricing rises to about INR75,000/ton.
Peak debt about INR760-770 crore; scheduled repayments about INR170-175 crore per year for the next 2-3 years; debt to fall below INR300-350 crore within 3 years.
AI-led opex reduction target of 4-5% by March 2028.
Pulp capacity to rise to about 410-415 TPD from 365 TPD.
capex_capacity: DDS (Double Displacement Digester) for wood pulping commissioned in Q1.
Native starch system commissioned on PM2 and PM3.
Folio ream wrapping machine installed in the finishing house.
PM3 shut for major rebuild; management expects commissioning within about a week of the call (mid-August 2026), completing the upgradation programme.
Pulping capacity of about 200 TPD each for agro and wood, said to be sufficient for all four machines.
EC clearance for PM3 upgrade filed and awaited.
Clonal propagation: record 17.28 lakh saplings in the quarter; plantation area about 19,650 acres after adding about 1,300 acres.
demand_pricing: Demand supported by education, publishing and office consumption; management expects demand to stay supportive.
Chinese imports diminishing, attributed mainly to shipping and container cost issues; imported copier/maplitho price seen at $610-620/ton near port.
Anti-dumping and anti-subsidy duty applications filed for writing and printing paper, covering 40-140 GSM; management hopes for a favourable decision, assumed 5-year duration.
Maplitho hit by inverted duty structure after GST change; management says Kuantum is reducing notebook paper exposure and passing GST losses to customers.
Management says pricing held flat QoQ into Q2 with no discounting; dealer channel inventory described as lean.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance maintained, and what EBITDA margin is achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is positive with PM3 commissioning, targeting at least 16-18% EBITDA margin by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is peak debt and the repayment path?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak debt about INR760-770 crore; repayments of about INR170-175 crore a year for 2-3 years, with debt below INR300 crore within 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the revenue guidance fall from INR1,400-1,500 crore to INR1,300 crore-plus?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisations are running below earlier expected levels and EBITDA margins are strained by West Asia-driven costs; management says figures are conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall while a competitor's rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to Punjab-specific raw material cost increases, mainly wheat straw, which it says is easing; it expects a gradual reduction in procurement cost.

qa_highlights.question: What share of cost increase is due to the West Asia crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of the INR4,200/ton cost increase is attributed to West Asia; INR3,400/ton has been passed through in pricing QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Will wheat straw prices come down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said procurement prices fell in Q2 versus Q1 after negotiations with suppliers, with further easing expected as rice straw and corn cobs arrive in September-October.

risks_watch: Cost pass-through: about INR800/ton of the INR4,200/ton cost rise was not recovered in Q1 price gains; watch whether Q2 NSR and margins recover.
Execution on PM3 commissioning (mid-August) and full-capacity ramp; Q2 is expected to be weak with machine and boiler shutdowns.
Revenue guidance cut and inconsistency with earlier FY28-30 projections.
Q2 seasonally weak demand; management says October onwards is when the industry picks up.
Pending EC clearance for PM3 and pending anti-dumping and anti-subsidy duty decision.
Debt of about INR760-770 crore at peak and interest burden on PAT.

key_quotes: We should be reaching closer to about at least between 16% to 18% by the year-end.
Peak debt, we are currently looking at about INR760 crores or INR770 crores maximum.

532937|2026-09.headline: Kuantum Papers Q2 FY27 revenue fell 8% QoQ to INR279 crores and PAT was INR2 crores, as PM 3 shutdown and input costs hit a lean quarter.
532937|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 operational income was INR279 crores, down 8% QoQ, as the PM 3 rebuild (28 June to 21 August 2026) cut volumes by about 6,000 tons. EBITDA was INR35 crores at a 12.4% margin, down 84 bps, on lower realisations and higher raw material and fuel costs linked to the West Asia conflict. PAT was INR2 crores (0.8% margin). H1 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR533 crores, but H1 PAT was only INR9 crores because depreciation and finance costs rose. Management guided to a 7% to 11% price increase over Q3 and Q4, of which about 4% was taken in late September.

financial_highlights.change: lower due to higher depreciation and finance costs

segments.name: Writing and printing paper (core, four PMs)
segments.commentary: Q2 production was 40,600 tons, with the remaining machines running at 100% utilisation. Management said orders were booked in advance and all output was sold. Specialty paper is about 17% to 18% of the mix, against a target of 25% to 30% in 12 to 15 months.

segments.name: Paperboard / kraft
segments.commentary: Management said a minimum import price (MIP) is already notified for kraft and paperboard varieties. No segment financials were given.

guidance_outlook: Price increases of 7% to 11% targeted by end of year, across Q3 and Q4. About 4% was taken in late September and is being sustained. The next hike is expected after Diwali.
H2 FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 14%. Management also said industry margins should recover to 18% to 20% in FY28. Analysts' 17% to 18% H2 figure was not confirmed.
Revenue target of over INR1,300 crores for FY27 reiterated. Management said Q3 should be far better than Q2, with lost volume of about 6,000 tons to be regained.
Cost savings of about 1.5% to 2% on total chemical consumption expected from the single-vendor TCM chemical solution.
Depreciation of about INR80 crores per year. Debt repayment of INR180 crores in FY27 is on track, with a similar amount in FY28. Management said deleveraging will begin after the next two years.
Target of about 1 crore clonal saplings a year in the next two to three years. Current production is 17.93 lakh saplings in the quarter.
capex_capacity: PM 3 commissioned 28 August 2026, rebuilt in 59 days against a 65-day plan. All four paper machines are now upgraded, adding a film press, I-table, table vision, web break monitoring, calendaring and automatic starch cooking.

Marketable output is about 600 tons per day at the optimised product mix, against a design capacity of 675 tons per day on an anchor GSM of 64. Orders are shifting to 52 to 58 GSM, which lowers tonnage.
Double Displacement Digester system improved wood pulp yield by 1% and cut steam use from 1.8 to 0.8 metric tons per tonne of pulp.
Environmental projects (lime kiln and CNCG gas handling) are in progress, with about INR139 crores of CWIP, to be completed in Q3 FY27. Management said there is no further major capex planned.
Environmental clearance has been applied for and is at an advanced stage. The 20 MW turbine generator and a 30 TPH boiler were overhauled during the quarter.
demand_pricing: Q2 was seasonally lean and the industry faced cost inflation. Management said Q2 had almost no price increase, with the first hike taken in the last week of September.

Imports have fallen because of higher ocean freight from the Gulf conflict, and exports have also fallen, so domestic supply is more balanced. Anti-dumping duty applications on writing and printing paper are with the government, with 3 to 6 months expected for completion.

Wood (about INR12,000/tonne) is expected to stay flat or fall as availability improves. Wheat straw prices are temporarily elevated after unseasonal rain and a labour shortage, and are expected to normalise after Diwali.

Starch is about 2% to 2.5% of paper cost. Sulphuric acid from West Asia added about 2% to sales cost. Fuel costs rose about 3% to 3.5%. Input coal costs rose about 2.5% to 3%. Coal mix is about 85% coal and 15% agro.
Chinese capacity is being cut (Chenming and Nine Dragons closures), and Indonesian exports are steady.

qa_highlights.question: What is the West Asia war impact on costs, and what was the wood-cost offset?

532942|2026-09.headline: KNR Constructions Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR587.9 crore with 16.4% EBITDA margin, lifted by a ~INR46 crore one-off from a cash-surplus EPC claim.

Management said the margin is flattered by a one-off of about INR46 crore (INR76 crore revenue less INR30 crore cost); excluding it, EBITDA margin is about 5.5%. Consolidated debt fell to INR1,975 crore from INR2,438 crore, while net debt/equity rose to 0.9 from 0.49 and working capital days rose to 133 from 78. Order book is INR15,234 crore including the two new HAM projects and the Kusmunda mining project, and management guided FY27 revenue to INR2,200-2,300 crore.

532944|2026-06.headline: OnMobile Q1 FY27 revenue fell 3.8% QoQ to INR 124.1 crore and EBITDA margin dropped to 1.2% as ONMO+ launch costs hit; PAT loss INR 28.9 crore.
532944|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR 124.1 crore, down 3.8% QoQ, with mobile entertainment at INR 84.6 crore (down 6.5% QoQ) and gaming at INR 39.4 crore (up 2.4% QoQ). EBITDA was INR 1.5 crore (1.2% margin), pressured by ONMO+ launch expenses, while PAT was a loss of INR 28.9 crore including a one-time INR 14.1 crore severance charge from restructuring. ONMO+ Smart Console went live on 26 June 2026 in India, in the last four days of the quarter, and management is pursuing retail (Diwali target) and B2B operator deals. Cash fell to INR 135.5 crore after ONMO+ investment and short-term credit repayment, and a debenture issue of INR 65 crore at about 13.8% was raised.

segments.name: Mobile gaming (subscription)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 39.4 crore, up 2.4% QoQ, with 13.8 million subscribers. Marketing spend cut to below 50% of revenue (from about 65% two years ago) by pausing unprofitable accounts; target EBITDA margin 10-25% for FY27.

segments.commentary: Launched 26 June 2026 on D2C in India; no console sales volumes disclosed. Pricing cited at about $3.99/month subscription, with box revenue of $50 or $75 for 12-month pack.

qa_highlights.answer: Management paused accounts with weak return on ad spend across more than 50 live accounts; reaching 2 million MRR may take three to four quarters, not guaranteed.

qa_highlights.question: Recovery of about INR 45 crore owed by DeOSphere?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the amount must be settled within the next two quarters; no detail on the recovery route was given.

qa_highlights.question: Severance of INR 14.1 crore looks high versus salaries of INR 22 crore; which team was downsized?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the INR 14.1 crore is a full-year figure covering India and international, with some European severance reaching two years' salary. Spain labour rules were cited as a driver.

qa_highlights.question: Manpower cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: People costs to remain at 20% to 22% of revenue, though ONMO+ hiring may add headcount.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise INR 65 crore debt at about 13.8% with INR 135.5 crore cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt funds ONMO+ and repays short-term facilities; part of cash sits in geographies with transfer restrictions.

qa_highlights.question: Is a QIP planned, and at what size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the fundraise should be USD 5 million to 10 million, combining QIP and strategic investors; current valuation seen as too low.

532944|2026-09.headline: OnMobile Q2 FY27 revenue rose 3.4% QoQ to INR 128 crore, but management says YoY growth is still negative and ONMO+ revenue is not yet visible.
532944|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 3.4% QoQ to INR 128 crore, with Entertainment & Communication at INR 87.7 crore (+3.5% QoQ) and Gaming at INR 40.7 crore (+3.2% QoQ). Gaming subscribers rose 5.4% QoQ to 14.5 million, and EBITDA improved to INR 2.4 crore from INR 1.5 crore. Management said the combined ONMO+ launch spend (marketing, retail network) keeps consolidated EBITDA and PAT depressed, and that external fundraising will be needed in the next quarter. Analysts pressed on YoY decline, subscription growth, ONMO+ pricing, and capital structure, and management gave little numerical disclosure on ONMO+.

segments.name: Gaming (incl. ONMO+ subscription)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 40.7 crore, up 3.2% QoQ; subscribers up 5.4% QoQ to 14.5 million with growth spread across 20+ operators. Management said it deliberately sacrificed some growth by exiting low-ROI accounts, and that ONMO+ console revenue is not yet visible in reported numbers.

qa_highlights.question: When will YoY growth return, and will FY27 grow, stay flat or decline versus FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: No explicit YoY answer; management said ONMO+ launch investment makes blended EBITDA and PAT limited, and that FY27 will see some ONMO+ revenue with the bigger impact in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Does ONMO+ revenue start in FY27 and will margins improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Some ONMO+ revenue expected in the two remaining FY27 quarters; margins will improve once revenue scales, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why is subscription revenue not growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prioritised profitability, exited inefficient accounts with high marketing cost and collection/currency issues; gaming subscription target remains 15-20% YoY growth, with subscriber growth running above revenue growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ONMO console only on Flipkart and what is the Spain strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Launch on Flipkart was a learning test; Savex deal includes Amazon in coming weeks, website going live in a couple of weeks; Spain uses retail, online ads and store promoters across multiple channels.

qa_highlights.question: Should ONMO+ be separated into subsidiaries with outside capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed the businesses could be separated and said it will meet investors in coming months for funding at OGL or subsidiary level (UAE, India, US, Spain or Europe), with the decision still open; it declined to disclose ONMO+ numbers for strategic reasons.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected on the console?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 15-25% EBITDA margin, depending on whether it pursues top-50 gaming markets with full retail or a limited B2C plus B2B model.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Savex partnership?
qa_highlights.answer: Savex is a large Indian retail distributor (HP, Lenovo, Apple, Meta glasses) reaching over 1,000 retail locations and e-commerce/quick commerce, expected to push the ONMO box across India.

532947|2026-09.headline: IRB Q2 FY27 PAT rose 85% YoY to ₹260 crore, with finance cost down 14% to ₹388 crore on deleveraging.
532947|2026-09.overview: Consolidated income rose 8% YoY to ₹1,945 crore and EBITDA grew 13% to ₹1,102 crore in Q2 FY27. Lower finance cost and a sharp rise in InvIT distributions drove profit growth, while depreciation rose 26%. Management said the InvIT asset monetisation of ₹4,605 crore EV brought in ₹2,744 crore of non-dilutive equity consideration to the group. Bid activity on TOT projects restarted after a backstop MLFF compensation mechanism was firmed up by NHAI, but no BOT or HAM bid had been submitted yet.

segments.name: InvIT & related assets
segments.commentary: Segment income ₹356 crore, up 17% YoY. Private InvIT average daily toll collection was ₹13.1 crore vs ₹9.2 crore, about 42% growth on a like-for-like basis excluding 3 assets moved to Public InvIT.

segments.name: BOT (toll)
segments.commentary: Segment income ₹721 crore, up 15% YoY. Mumbai-Pune and Ahmedabad-Vadodara gross toll collections grew 14% and 16%, about 15% across the wholly owned portfolio.

segments.name: Construction (EPC)
segments.commentary: Segment income ₹821 crore, flat YoY. EPC order book stands at about ₹1,200 crore.

segments.name: Distributions to IRB
segments.commentary: Private InvIT declared ~₹231 crore; IRB's 51% share ~₹118 crore vs ₹26 crore (about 354% growth). Public InvIT declared ~₹269 crore; IRB's ~16% effective share ~₹43 crore vs ₹32 crore (about 35% growth).

guidance_outlook: Interest cost: management said the Q2 finance cost (₹388 crore) is the new quarterly run-rate and will decline further with scheduled SPV repayments.
Net debt-free status by FY30 is reaffirmed; management said interest cost will keep falling quarter after quarter.
O&M margin guidance of about 20% is maintained.
Cash ROE target of 8% to 14% over the next 4 to 5 years (ROE timeline cited as FY32 in the question) is reaffirmed, driven by operating leverage as debt amortises.
Asset base targeted at ₹1,40,000 crore by 2030 from ~₹94,000 crore currently.
Next set of TOT bids expected to be out soon and concluded before March 2027, per management's discussions with the authority.
capex_capacity: Asset base is about ₹94,000 crore with average concession life of about 20 years, per management.

Public InvIT (IRB InvIT Fund) acquired two operational highway assets from Private InvIT (IRB Infrastructure Trust) at aggregate EV of ₹4,605 crore; raised ₹2,000 crore equity, and IRB invested ₹351 crore in the preferential issue.
Capital recycling is said to position the group to pursue new opportunities worth about ₹8,000 crore.
Private InvIT originally had 9 projects; 5 have now moved to Public InvIT, leaving 4.
Two HAM projects on IRB's balance sheet are nearing completion, expected in about 6 months; they would then be eligible for transfer to Public InvIT.
Ganga Expressway completed during the year, now contributing to Private InvIT distributions.
demand_pricing: Management attributed toll growth to steady traffic demand and inflation-linked tariff mechanisms.
TOT bidding resumed after NHAI firmed up a backstop compensation mechanism for the multi-lane free flow (MLFF) system; three TOT bids that had been under bidding for a long time have been concluded.
Management said there is no BOT or HAM bid where IRB has submitted a bid so far, though it continues to evaluate opportunities.
On HAM/EPC, management was not sure recent concession agreement changes would keep out frivolous bidders.
Management said the low-hanging fruit in BOT is behind, and more complex BOT projects will be selected more carefully.
Total order book is about ₹43,400 crore, including EPC order book of about ₹1,200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of TOT and project awarding, and has bidding intensity changed with tighter criteria?
qa_highlights.answer: TOT bids were delayed over MLFF compensation talks, now resolved with a backstop mechanism from NHAI. Three long-pending TOT bids have been concluded and the next set is expected before March 2027. No BOT or HAM bid has been submitted yet.

qa_highlights.question: Is the lower interest cost the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, Q2 interest cost is the new run-rate. It fell due to the VM7 transfer to Public InvIT last year, SPV repayments at MP and AV, and a lower rate at IRB MP after refinancing; further declines are expected.

qa_highlights.question: Is there BOT toll opportunity ahead, or will the business rely on TOT and the backlog?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the low-hanging BOT fruit is over and it will be selective on complex projects. It sees asset monetisation as the focus and points to about 20 years of revenue visibility from the ₹94,000 crore asset base.

qa_highlights.question: Will IRB move into non-road businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will stay in road and highway infrastructure and has no plans to diversify into unrelated businesses, citing a focus on picky project additions.

qa_highlights.question: Which Private InvIT or balance-sheet projects could transfer to Public InvIT soon?
qa_highlights.answer: Four projects remain in Private InvIT. Two HAM projects on IRB's balance sheet are nearing completion in about 6 months and would be eligible for transfer once criteria are met.
