532953|2026-03.headline: V-Guard Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 14.1% YoY to INR1,755 crore and PAT 23% to INR112 crore, with FY26 EBITDA margin at 8.8%.
532953|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was strong, with revenue up 14.1% YoY to INR1,755 crore and EBITDA excluding other income up 19.3% to INR171 crore, while FY26 revenue grew 7% and EBITDA rose 2.6% to INR527 crore. Growth came almost entirely in the second half after a weak summer in the first half. Management is pursuing price hikes of roughly 13% to offset input cost inflation linked to the West Asia conflict, with about 75% landed so far. Net cash rose to INR231 crore and the board recommended a final dividend of INR1.5 per share.

segments.name: Electronics (Stabilizers, UPS, Inverters, Batteries)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 22.3% YoY with all categories growing; about 3% of growth was price and the balance volume, per management. Solar inverters are a newer line, not yet at INR500 crore.

segments.name: Electrical (Wires, Pumps, Switchgears, Modular Switches)
segments.commentary: Largest revenue contributor; Q4 revenue grew 15.9% YoY. Wires face rising competition from new entrants, though management sees the category as low-margin and scale-dependent.

segments.name: Consumer Durables (Fans, Water Heaters, Kitchen Appliances, Air Coolers)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 4.1% YoY; fans and air coolers declined while water heaters and kitchen grew strongly. TPW fans are short of supply due to a plastic raw material shortage.

segments.name: Sunflame (Kitchen Appliances)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 8.6% YoY; the CSD business is still slowing, but non-CSD grew about 16%. GT integration is complete and sales integration is still underway.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for 10-12% volume growth and 1-2% price growth (about 15% total) over time, with higher price growth likely in FY27 due to cost inflation.
EBITDA margin: management says at least 10% is the target for the next year if summer is good, but declined to commit to 11-12%; cited prolonged high cost as a reason for caution.
Expects a good growth year for Consumer Durables on a low base, and a strong start to FY27 given Q4 momentum and a supportive summer forecast.
Cost discipline: no major manpower increases planned; variable pay will fall if top and bottom line targets are missed.
Price increases: about 75% of the required ~13% price hike landed so far; the remaining ~25% is expected as high-cost inventory flows in during May-June.
Raw material supply secured through June for most items; sulfuric acid and certain TPW fan plastics remain tight.
capex_capacity: Management said bulk of new capacity investment is done and ramp-up is under way; capex will still absorb some cash in FY27.
Company spent close to INR300-400 crore over the last 8 years on plants and manufacturing integration.
BLDC is about 40% of ceiling fan sales; BLDC chimneys launched; BLDC mixer grinders not yet launched.
Lighting entry is still work in progress, with launch targeted around early next quarter (Q1 FY27).
No acquisitions planned; any opportunity would be assessed case by case.
demand_pricing: Input costs up 8-13% across representative categories; management says the West Asia conflict has caused commodity inflation and supply shocks, worse than the Ukraine-war period.
Price hikes of about 10-12% (some up to 15-20% industry-wide) face retailer pushback; the company gave case-by-case support in regions where summer has not started.
South India summer demand is strong (sales started early March/April); non-South is mixed due to rain, with East a key market for summer products.
Channel financing covers about 35% of the debtor book (customer-linked, not category-linked); collections were strong in the March quarter.
Kerala is about 15-16% of revenue; no impact seen so far, with summer in Kerala supportive. Non-South contributed 48% of FY26 revenue; South grew 16.2% and non-South 11.8% in Q4.
Competition: wire entrants and lighting peers are entering; management expects consolidation to be slow and sees the top 4-5 brands per category as the survivors.

qa_highlights.question: What price hikes have been taken across segments, and is another round needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Input costs up 8-13%; about 75% of the required price increase has landed, with the remaining 25% expected as high-cost inventory arrives in May-June.

qa_highlights.question: Has the Kitchen Appliances segment come out of its slump?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes demand is improving, with traction for both V-Guard and Sunflame; Sunflame now uses V-Guard's sales network.

qa_highlights.question: Is Kerala softness affecting demand after March?
qa_highlights.answer: No impact seen so far; Kerala is about 15-16% of revenue and summer there has been supportive. Q1 is primarily a summer quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margins reach double digits in one to two years?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 FY26 EBITDA was about 9.5%; management is confident of at least 10% once raw material prices normalise, but declined to guide 11-12%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the solar business size and growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar is below INR500 crore, about 36 months old; management expects it to be among the larger categories in 3-4 years, focused on residential B2C.

qa_highlights.question: Is raw material availability a risk to production?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulfuric acid and polymers are tight; supply is locked up for about a month or more, and management sees no supply challenge through Q1.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation from the West Asia conflict; about 25% of the required price hike is still pending and could face pushback.
Weak non-South summer start; East market is key for summer products and any slip would hurt Q1 FY27 volumes.
Shortage of TPW fan plastic and sulfuric acid could cap output; management expects supply to be about 105 units against 110 demanded.
Rising competition in wires from a large new entrant at the end of 2026 and lighting peers.
Sunflame CSD decline and the pace of benefits from sales integration (expected over the next three quarters); the NPD pipeline lands in H2 FY26 onwards.
Channel inventory is mixed: ceiling fans well stocked after the December 2025 BEE star-rating transition; TPW fans out of stock.

532953|2026-06.headline: V-Guard Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23.5% YoY to INR1,810 crore and EBITDA margin widened to 10.5% from 8.4%.
532953|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 23.5% YoY to INR1,810 crore, with about 14% price and 9% volume contribution per management's blended split. EBITDA excluding other income rose 54.5% to INR191 crore, and PAT rose 76% to INR130 crore. Gross margin held at 36.9%, flat YoY, as management says roughly 75-80% of input cost inflation has been passed through. Management raised FY27 growth expectations to above 15% and reaffirmed a 9-10% EBITDA margin, while noting wires volumes were nearly flat under a large price increase.

segments.name: Electronics (stabilizers, UPS, solar)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 22.8% YoY with all major categories contributing; solar is growing fastest on a small base, and solar pumps for Maharashtra government are only a couple of crore so far.

segments.name: Electricals
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 27.7% YoY, aided by higher copper prices; wires saw very high price growth with near-flat volumes, while ex-wires grew at high double digits and switchgear, modular switches and pumps grew volumes robustly.

segments.name: Consumer Durables (fans, water heaters, kitchen, air coolers)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 19.2% YoY; induction cooktops spiked, other kitchen categories grew healthily, fans grew reasonably (pedestal fans short on inventory), and air coolers lost share due to weak North demand and competitor price delays.

segments.name: Sunflame
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 18.3% YoY on a low base; management says integration is complete and a sales acceleration programme has started, with margin recovery expected to be more gradual than top-line recovery.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was a one-off: copper purchases shifted to domestic suppliers who give credit, instead of imports paid by LC, and payables are expected to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Why not gain share in wires by passing on less price?

rows.why: FY27 revenue growth raised to 'a bit more than 15%' from Q1 growth of 23.5% (about 14% price, 9% volume), with pricing actions 80-85% complete.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged wires price-war risk from new entrants, a possible festive-season launch, West Asia commodity volatility and ad spend rising to 2.5% from 2.2%, though EBITDA margin guide of 9-10% was held.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: FY27; solar rooftop BESS in next 2-3 months
rows.why: Lighting launch is planned in FY27 and a solar rooftop next-generation battery (BESS) launch is planned in the next two to three months, targeting about INR1.5-2 lakh per home.

rows.label: Payables and net cash normalisation
rows.why: Management called the high payables a one-off from copper sourcing shifting to ~95% domestic from 70-80%, and net cash of INR670 crore (vs INR155 crore a year ago) may normalise.

rows.label: Sunflame margin recovery
rows.why: Sunflame revenue grew 18.3% on a low base and integration is complete, but management expects margin recovery to be more gradual than top-line recovery given CSD and non-South general trade pricing lags.

532953|2026-09.headline: V-Guard Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 38.2% YoY to INR1,853 crore, but gross margin fell to 34.3% on input costs and mix.
532953|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 38.2% YoY to INR1,853 crore in Q2 FY27, with H1 at INR3,664 crore (up 30.5%). EBITDA excluding other income rose 53.7% YoY to INR168 crore, with margin at 9.1% versus 8.1% a year earlier, while PAT reached INR112 crore (up 71%). Gross margin contracted to 34.3% from 37.6% a year ago and 36.9% in Q1, which management attributed to input costs, lagged price pass-through and mix. Management said a further 3-4% price increase is needed to close the gap and that H2 volume growth will moderate to about mid-teens.

financial_highlights.change: vs 37.6% in Q2 FY26 and 36.9% in Q1 FY27
Wires growth mainly price-led (cables ~40% price, flat volume)

segments.name: Electronics (Stabilizers, UPS, Inverters & Batteries, Solar)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 60% YoY in Q2 with all categories positive; solar and inverter-battery led. Management said EBITDA margin fell about 380 bps QoQ on mix, delayed pass-through of component price hikes and rooftop solar's different margin structure. Sustainable margin guided at 16-17% in a normal year and 18% in a good year.

segments.name: Electricals (Wires, Pumps, Switches, Switchgear)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 41.2% YoY; wires growth was mostly price-driven (cables pricing close to 40%, volumes flat). Ex-wires, about 10% price and 25% volume growth across other categories was cited.

segments.name: Consumer Durables (Fans, Water Heaters, Kitchen Appliances, Air Coolers)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 20% YoY. Management said CD margins were low last year due to Water Heater launch A&P, so the margin improvement is largely base effect; Q2 price increases lagged, to be addressed in Q3. Sunflame grew 20.5% YoY, with gas stove sales flat and induction demand shifting.

segments.name: Solar Power Systems (within Electronics)
segments.commentary: Management declined to give segment revenue or margin figures; said solar is still nascent, mainly sold in South India to system integrators, and 75% of sales are 3-10 kW residential systems. Northern and Eastern launches are planned.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Launched about 3-4 months ago with only 40-50% of planned SKUs landed, in a few districts of a couple of states. Full rollout targeted around April-May; management expects decent revenue from Q1 FY28.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 volume growth expected to be lower than H1, around mid-teens, with revenue supported by price increases.

capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at about INR150 crore.

A&P spend about 2.3% of revenue, broadly unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gross margin outlook; is the dip temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Gap versus plan was about 3% in Q2: 1% mix and 2% lagged price pass-through. Further input cost increases in September and October mean price hikes are being landed to neutralise them. Management said a 3-4% gap remains and that commodity movements could go either way.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Electronics margin decline is structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited delayed pass-through on electronic components, out-of-season categories taking longer to reprice, and mix from rooftop solar. Sustainable Electronics margin is 16-17% normally and 18% in a good year.

qa_highlights.question: What is H2 volume growth expected to be?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 volume growth will be lower than H1, around mid-teens, with price increases supporting revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Solar business material, and what margins does it earn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give solar revenue or margin figures, calling it early-stage and saying it is too premature to discuss margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will V-Guard reach double-digit EBITDA margin in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 EBITDA is close to 9.5-10% and it is on course this year; it did not give a FY28 double-digit target, and stated that investments in new categories are charged to the P&L.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Sunflame growth drivers and product refresh status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Sunflame's growth of over 20% comes from non-gas-stove categories as gas stove sales were flat and demand shifted to induction. Product refresh has partly landed, with more over the next 6-12 months.

Lighting rollout (full SKU and geographic expansion targeted around April-May 2027).

rows.why: Gegadyne has about 3 customers with purchases not yet material, and volumes are possibly due within a few months, which is conditional and unquantified.

532955|2026-09.headline: REC H1 FY27: disbursements of INR56,457 crore (+67% vs Q1) and net NPA at 0.11%, but management concedes NIM pressure from 3.22% level.
532955|2026-09.overview: REC reported H1 FY27 with loan book at an all-time high of INR6.17 lakh crore (up 6% YoY) and PAT of INR7,541 crore for the half. Management cited disbursements of about INR90,000 crore in H1 (power sector ~INR80,000 crore), with net credit-impaired assets down to 0.11% from 0.24% a year earlier. Management guided FY27 loan book growth of 10-12% and NIM of about 3.2%, while acknowledging NIM pressure from competition, derisking and rising borrowing costs. The call also covered the pending PFC merger, with the draft scheme awaiting Cabinet approval.

financial_highlights.change: NIM stable per company; management flagged compression
down from INR12,350 crore at 30 June

segments.name: Conventional generation
segments.commentary: Loan book grew about 4% since 31 March 2026; about 11% of Q2 disbursements; thermal is about 24.7% of the book (~INR1.52 lakh crore) per Projects Director.

segments.name: Renewable energy
segments.commentary: RE portfolio at INR86,660 crore as of 30 September 2026, growing ~15% in the half (27% YoY per Chairman); 17% of Q2 disbursements; solar 35%, hybrid 18%, pumped storage 14%, hydro 13%.

segments.name: Distribution / Infra & logistics
segments.commentary: Distribution took 22% of Q2 disbursements; infra and logistics about 10% of the book (~INR62,000 crore), growing ~6% since 31 March 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 loan book growth guided at 10-12% (6% achieved in H1).
FY27 disbursement target of over INR2 lakh crore; company expects to reach ~INR2.1 lakh crore, which would exceed last year's INR2.11 lakh crore record only marginally.
NIM expected to hold around 3.2%; management said NIM pressure exists and it would not claim NIM will rise.
Management expects Q3 and Q4 disbursements not to be lower than Q1 and Q2; ~INR70,000 crore of documented projects yet to be disbursed.
Planned sanctions of INR1.7-2 lakh crore in H2; committed pipeline of INR2.56 lakh crore, of which ~INR69,000 crore still to be documented.
Dividend declared for FY27 so far totals INR7.75 per share, including INR3.5 for Q2; 30% payout ratio mandated by GoI.
Stage 1 provisioning around 1% on incremental loan book (ECL); straight 1% provisioning expected to continue.
Merger with PFC: both boards approved; NOC received from RBI and stock exchanges; draft scheme pending Cabinet approval. Management says merged entity will remain government-controlled.
capex_capacity: NEP: minimum ~80 GW additional thermal capacity planned (baseline 215-217 GW to 274-283 GW); ~22-24 GW under construction; REC fund requirement estimated at INR1.8-2.2 lakh crore at INR8.34 crore/MW.
Company targets raising thermal/generation book to ~INR2.5 lakh crore by 2032.
Cabinet approved INR1.85 lakh crore transmission project; detailed guidelines from MNRE still awaited.
NTPC Meja project won: about INR27,000 crore disbursement, half to be shared with PFC.
Rooftop Solar Scheme: ~55 lakh installations achieved against 1 crore target by end of this year; ~95 lakh applications.
demand_pricing: Management attributed FY26 loan growth of only 3% to ~INR1 lakh crore of prepayments despite record INR2.11 lakh crore disbursements; H1 FY27 prepayments were ~INR19,000-20,000 crore.
Competition is intense: banks flush with liquidity, power sector seeking low rates; management said NIM will see pressure.
Management expects yields to hold; loan book is largely floating (about 25%) while about 24% of borrowings are floating, with rising rates seen as favourable.
Thermal yields slightly higher than RE; I&L yields above RE but below thermal; company declined to give specific yield differentials.
Management claims state power utilities borrowed ~INR10 lakh crore in last 3 years, with REC lending INR4.5 lakh crore (~45% share).

qa_highlights.question: What is driving NIM compression and how will the NIM trajectory look?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajesh Kumar said ~24% of borrowings are floating (INR term loans and some ECBs) versus ~25% of the loan book floating, so rate rises are offset; a zero-coupon bond last year gave ~10 bps benefit and the company is seeking withholding-tax exemption on ECBs and a green bond basket mandate.

qa_highlights.question: How will conventional thermal AUM and disbursement grow over the next 2-3 years given slow state capacity additions?
qa_highlights.answer: T.S.C. Bosh cited ~80 GW minimum additional capacity under NEP, implying INR1.8-2.2 lakh crore REC financing needs by 2031-32, with a 30:70 equity-debt assumption.

qa_highlights.question: Will 10-12% growth continue post-merger with PFC in FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman declined to give numbers for the merged entity, citing synergies in borrowing, lending and capital base, and restricted guidance to FY27 for REC.

qa_highlights.question: Why is management confident of 10-12% growth given competition from unlisted players and banks?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said prepayments had peaked (INR19,000 crore in H1 FY27 vs ~INR1 lakh crore in FY26), banks face sectoral limits, and power, transmission and biogas (INR23,000 crore scheme) are growth drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Will yields fall further on competitive pricing to state utilities?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajesh Kumar said rebate/concession proposals to state sector are largely settled and yield curve is rising, so limited yield downside is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Is H2 disbursement momentum seasonal or sustainable, and how does the pipeline look?
qa_highlights.answer: Bosh said Q1 weakness reflected documentation delays and peer competition; ~40% of disbursement pipeline is under documentation, and the Chairman cited ~INR70,000 crore of documented projects yet to start disbursement.

qa_highlights.question: How will credit cost evolve now that resolutions are done?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajesh Kumar said ~1% ECL is being provided on incremental loans (~INR300 crore in Q2 on ~INR26,000 crore growth), with ~80% of ECL being reserve-type given state-sector exposure; straight 1% provisioning expected going forward.

risks_watch: NIM compression below 3.2% as competition and rising borrowing costs bite; management admits 'there will be pressure'.
Merger with PFC pending Cabinet approval; government control to be maintained, with final scheme details awaited.
Currency: forex hedging enhanced above INR96/USD; management says no new major forex hit expected but volatility remains.
Smart meter resistance from consumers and perception issues; allocation and completion data not disclosed on call.
Transmission and Green Energy Corridor guidelines from MNRE still awaited; REC's share of INR1.85 lakh crore transmission scheme unclear.
Q3/Q4 disbursement pace versus the INR2 lakh crore-plus target; prepayment trend post rate-hike cycle.

I am confident that the prepayments scenario has peaked out, and now that we are entering increasing interest rate cycle, I don't think prepayments will be a major issue for us.
We are very confident of touching double-digit growth, and we are hopeful that we should be able to show around 10% to 12% growth by the end of this year.

rows.why: Capex is not discussed for REC itself; the utilisation read is not applicable to a lender.

rows.why: NIM is guided only to around 3.0-3.2% with management conceding pressure, and H1 loan growth of 6% must roughly double to hit 10-12%, so the loan book target is at risk if prepayments or competition persist.

rows.why: No new product or model launches were discussed; the biogas scheme and green bond basket are funding or growth items, not launches.

rows.why: Both boards approved, RBI NOC and exchange NOCs received, and the draft scheme awaits Cabinet approval; management says the merged entity stays government-controlled, but gave no post-merger growth or NIM numbers.

rows.label: NTPC Meja project and transmission financing
rows.why: NTPC Meja win is worth about INR27,000 crore of disbursement, and the INR1.85 lakh crore transmission scheme is Cabinet-approved, though MNRE guidelines are still awaited and REC's share is unclear.

rows.label: Credit quality improvement and provisioning
rows.why: Net credit-impaired assets fell to 0.11% from 0.24% a year earlier and Stage 2 assets dropped to INR3,235 crore from INR12,350 crore at 30 June, with about 1% ECL on incremental loans (~INR300 crore in Q2) continuing.

tone.note: Management was confident on the disbursement pipeline and asset quality but candid that NIM faces pressure from competition and rising borrowing costs, and it was evasive on post-merger targets and government control. Analysts probed the path to 10-12% growth given H1's 6% and the NIM trajectory.

532966|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 PRS revenue rose to about INR230 crore, with PRS at ~31% of revenue and 30+ coaches dispatched; wagon dispatches muted at 1,284.
532966|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 was a milestone for the Passenger Rail System (PRS) vertical, which contributed about 31% of revenue and dispatched more than 30 coaches. PRS revenue was stated as roughly INR230 crore, up from about INR170 crore in the prior quarter and about INR130 crore before that. Freight Rail System (FRS) dispatches were deliberately muted at 1,284 wagons, with production planned at 600-650 wagons per month until a large Indian Railways wagon tender is announced. Standalone TRSL order book stood at INR13,335 crore (PRS INR10,395 crore, FRS INR2,470 crore), and the group order book including JV share was INR26,635 crore.

segments.name: Passenger Rail System (PRS)
segments.commentary: About 31% of Q1 revenue, ~INR230 crore PRS revenue; standalone PRS is about 80% of the standalone order book. Order book is Vande Bharat (5-year supply, consortium with BHEL, TRSL share ~51% of car value) and Metro (2-year supply, 100% TRSL).

segments.name: Freight Rail System (FRS)
segments.commentary: 1,284 wagons dispatched against 1,000-per-month capacity; production scaled to 600-650 per month. Order book 5,300 wagons, with private orders being pursued alongside an awaited Indian Railways tender.

segments.name: Shipbuilding (Titagarh Naval Systems Ltd)
segments.commentary: Shipbuilding hived off to a wholly owned subsidiary; INR470 crore Indian Navy order with first ship due over 30 months, so no execution this year. New Falta shipyard under construction, targeted fully operational in Q1 or Q2 FY28.

segments.name: Wheelset JV with RK Forgings
segments.commentary: Hot trials ongoing in Chennai forging line; sample production from August 2026. Trial production in Q2 FY27, invoicing expected within FY27. Capacity 2.20-2.28 lakh wheels; 80,000 wheels per year required under a 20-year Railways contract, about 40% of capacity underwritten.

guidance_outlook: Coach production to rise to 45-50 coaches per quarter during FY27, and to total capacity of 850+ coaches per annum by FY2028-29 (management cited 2029-2030 in Q&A).
Management said the 200-odd coach target remains intact, with a 10% plus/minus tolerance.
Bulk of Bangalore and Gujarat (Ahmedabad and Surat) metro execution expected in FY27, spilling into early FY28; Gujarat trains executed in parallel.
Mumbai metro prototype expected Q4 FY27 to Q1 CY2027; Vande Bharat first train expected around end of calendar 2026.
Pune Metro extension (12 trains) to be delivered Q3-Q4 FY28; in-house aluminium subassembly line to be fully commissioned by Q1 FY28.
Wheelset JV phase 2 on track; management expects invoicing of wheels within FY27.
Management declined to give forward revenue guidance; cited 850 cars (~INR8,500 crore potential) and 12,000 freight wagons (~INR4,000-4,500 crore potential) as capacity, not forecast.
capex_capacity: Freight wagon capacity 1,000 per month, currently run at 600-650 per month for overhead absorption.
Pune Metro: all machines acquired for in-house production from extrusion to complete coach; line to be fully commissioned by Q1 FY28.
Propulsion: 2 rakes of EMU propulsion equipment supplied; MEMU propulsion sets planned for end-Q1 or beginning-Q2 FY27.
Wheelset JV Phase 2 capacity 2.20-2.28 lakh wheels; hot trials ongoing in Chennai forging line.
New Falta shipyard work started; MD and CEO Commodore Hemant Khatri appointed, ex-Hindustan Shipyard CMD.
demand_pricing: Indian Railways wagon tender remains awaited; management said requirement may be deferred by a few quarters but not dropped, citing 3 billion tonne freight target against about 1.5 billion tonnes today.
MRVC tender cancellation: management said total addressable market is unchanged, only product mix shifts; freight and passenger capacity are not fungible.
Metro: government plan to expand metro network from 25 to 50 cities cited as demand driver; individual metro order split not disclosed.
Wheel pricing: about INR1 lakh per wheel at peak utilisation (ballpark); Railways selling price per kg is public, margins expected in line with standard forging companies.

qa_highlights.question: Why are orders not translating into turnover growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 80% of standalone order book is PRS, a new business; coach dispatches up ~400% YoY and ~43% QoQ, and PRS revenue is expected to grow every quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will FRS wagons be scaled down further if no new order comes, and are there penalties?
qa_highlights.answer: No further scale-down planned; 600-650 per month plan puts delivery only a couple of months ahead of schedule. Private orders being pursued alongside the awaited tender.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 200-odd coach target intact, and what are the status of Bangalore, Gujarat and Mumbai?
qa_highlights.answer: Target remains intact within 10% plus/minus. Bangalore and Gujarat to be largely complete this FY with spillover into Q1 FY28; Mumbai prototype to start in parallel, and civil delays of 2-3 months not seen as significant.

qa_highlights.question: How is Vande Bharat accounted for with BHEL, and how is the AMC treated?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply is a consortium, so revenue and profit flow proportionately into top and bottom line; AMC sits in a JV and is accounted as share of JV profit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wheelset JV profitability trajectory and break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins in line with standard forging companies such as RK Forgings; no break-even utilisation figure given. Selling price per kg to Railways is public.

qa_highlights.question: What is the visibility for metro orders beyond FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to upcoming tenders across Western, Southern, Central and North India and the government plan to expand metro cities from 25 to 50; no year-wise order numbers given.

532967|2026-06.headline: Kiri Industries Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 63% YoY to INR 295 crore, with PAT of INR 270 crore driven mainly by INR 284 crore other income.
532967|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 63% YoY to INR 295 crore on realisation-led growth in dyes, dyes intermediates and basic chemicals, with standalone material margin at 31.9% versus 23.5% a year earlier. Standalone EBITDA was only INR 17 crore (5.86% margin), so PAT of INR 270 crore was largely a function of INR 284 crore other income, mainly treasury gains and inter-corporate loan interest. Consolidated revenue rose 55% to INR 312 crore with EBITDA of INR 37 crore (7.84%), and the group is substantially debt-free after repaying Claronex Holdings' borrowings. The copper and fertiliser project moved into structured construction, with financial closure still incomplete (over 50% of debt commitments received).

rows.why: Standalone material margin rose to 31.9% from 23.5% a year ago and 20.4% in Q4 FY26, with H-Acid prices at INR 800-900/unit versus INR 350-400 earlier, but management says sustaining margins depends on passing through crude-linked input costs and standalone EBITDA was only 5.86%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: 35 KT copper tube plant June 2027 (Q1 FY28); 2.25 lakh tonne
rows.why: Copper project is under construction with INR 1,400 crore deployed to date against about INR 12,000 crore total, and management gave concrete commissioning dates, though it withdrew the INR 20,000-25,000 crore FY28 revenue guidance because vendor timelines are moving.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: FY27 average; first copper revenue around May-June 2027
rows.why: Dyes utilisation is about 60% and targeted at 70-75% for FY27 if markets support, which implies roughly 17-25% higher volume on the same capacity, and copper output starts around Q1 FY28 with India consuming about 1.8 million tonnes a year.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: The copper project is already committed at about INR 12,000 crore with financial closure over 50% complete, so new capex is more likely to come from balance-of-plant or infrastructure spend (captive jetty, desalination, conveying system) than a fresh announced programme; dyes utilisation of about 60% gives no pressure for brownfield capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management withdrew the INR 20,000-25,000 crore FY28 revenue guidance and said projections are moving with vendor timelines, so there is no upward revision signal.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The FY28 revenue guidance has already been withdrawn for copper, rod and tube timelines depend on vendor delivery, and financial closure is still incomplete with over 50% of debt committed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Copper tube (35 KT, June 2027), rod (2.25 lakh t, August-September 2027), part refinery (1.75 lakh t, around January 2028) and copper foil trial production (10 KT, around March 2028) are all scheduled, but timing is vendor-dependent.

rows.label: Debt repayment begins 2029 after moratorium
rows.why: Group is substantially debt-free after repaying Claronex Holdings' borrowings, and copper project debt repayment starts in 2029 given moratorium, with cash flow ramping stepwise over FY28-FY30.

rows.label: Copper concentrate supply contracts
rows.why: MoUs cover about 1 million tonnes against about 1.5 million tonnes needed at full utilisation, so firm contracts must convert before the plant runs; the gap is about 0.5 million tonnes.

rows.label: MCB Copper-Gold mine off-take litigation
rows.why: Development has not started and 70% off-take for Kiri is being contested by Celsius in court, so management declined to speculate on the outcome and no near-term volume contribution is supported.

tone.note: Management was confident on the copper timeline and Q1 margin gains but evasive on forward numbers, withdrawing the FY28 revenue guidance and declining to speculate on the Celsius litigation; analysts pushed on standalone earnings quality, since PAT rests on INR 284 crore other income against INR 17

532967|2026-09.headline: Kiri Industries Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 48% YoY to INR 288 crore, with EBITDA turning positive at INR 7 crore on H-Acid price spike.
532967|2026-09.overview: Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was about INR 288 crore (up 48% YoY), with material margin at 29.1% versus 26.4% a year earlier and EBITDA of about INR 7 crore (2.4% margin) against a loss of INR 14 crore. Consolidated Q2 revenue was INR 299 crore (up 40%), EBITDA about INR 2 crore, and loss after tax INR 39 crore before associates, which included a non-cash treasury fair-value loss of INR 57 crore. Management said H-Acid price gains were only partly reflected because of earlier fixed-price orders, with the benefit expected to flow into Q3 and Q4. Copper and fertilizer project phase one remains on track for 1H FY28, and the company took a 40% stake in Makilala Mining in the Philippines.

segments.name: Dyes and dye intermediates (standalone and JV)
segments.commentary: Q2 standalone material margin improved to 29.1%, but sequential material margin was hit by a narrower price-cost spread in dye intermediates. Intermediate capacity utilisation is below 60%, and about 95% of intermediates are consumed captively.

segments.name: Copper and fertilizer project
segments.commentary: Equipment deliveries have started at site, with civil, foundation and structural works progressing. Phase one is on track for 1H FY28, and downstream facilities are due to be operational next fiscal year.

segments.name: Makilala Mining (Philippines, 40%)
segments.commentary: Expected to produce 140,000 t of copper concentrate, of which about 100,000 t would come to India, covering roughly 6-7% of the company's 1.6 million t requirement from 2028-29.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q3 and Q4 FY27 to show significantly higher performance than Q1 and Q2 as H-Acid price gains flow into dye realisations with a one-to-two-quarter lag.
Long-term EBITDA margin target of at least 8-10% on consolidated dye revenue of INR 1,300-1,500 crore at peak; Q2 margin was about 3-4%.
H-Acid prices are expected to stabilise by calendar 2027 at levels above earlier prices; no visibility of China stabilisation before March 2027.
Demand for dyes and intermediates is expected to stay stable through 2H FY27.

Downstream copper facilities of about 2.6 lakh t are targeted for operation next fiscal year; smelter and fertiliser units are targeted for 2028-29. Post-start production guidance is 5 lakh t copper and 11 lakh t fertiliser.
Around 80% of copper concentrate and semi-finished requirements are said to be secured through LME-week supplier discussions.
capex_capacity: Makilala MCB project capex is about USD 280 million; Kiri's equity share is expected to be a little above USD 40 million, with the balance to come from strategic partner equity, domestic partner equity and debt (still under evaluation).
Intermediate capacity is operating below 60% because of raw material shortages, and management is working to raise utilisation for merchant sales.
India H-Acid capacity is about 60,000 t a year against domestic consumption of about 30,000-40,000 t a year.
Phase one of the integrated copper and fertiliser project is on track to start in 1H FY28; equipment deliveries have begun.
Acquired 40% in Makilala Mining Company Inc (Philippines) and incorporated Andamina SPA in Chile during the quarter.
demand_pricing: H-Acid prices have moved from about INR 400-500/kg to INR 1,600-1,800 over the last three to four weeks, per management, with China output below 50% of its roughly 100,000 t requirement due to continuous-nitration regulation.
Vinyl sulphone is above INR 450, but input costs (sulphur, aniline) have risen sharply, so spreads have not expanded proportionately.
Reactive dye prices are around INR 1,500-1,600, and dye prices follow intermediate prices with a two-to-three-month lag.
Over 50% of dye sales are exported; the company has a two-to-three-month running order book.
Dystar remains a major customer, and Lonsen Kiri is its single largest global supplier.
Copper cathodes: duty-free Japanese imports of about 200,000 t a year are insufficient, so other origins with duty are needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is consolidated EBITDA still weak despite the H-Acid price rise, and are Philippine legal costs a factor?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said legal expenses in Q2 were under INR 3 crore and not the main reason. The lag comes from earlier fixed-price dye orders, with the price effect expected to show in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will Kiri appoint a CEO or CFO at Makilala to get operational control?
qa_highlights.answer: Kiri is a minority holder but sits on the board. A new management team was jointly appointed with the partner, including a CEO, Yulo Parese, formerly of Carmen Copper, and a new CFO, and Kiri has deputed staff through Carabao Corporation.

qa_highlights.question: Will the H-Acid disruption in China last, and what is the cost structure of continuous nitration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said China output is below 50% of its roughly 100,000 t need. Visibility is absent before March 2027, and prices may stabilise by calendar 2027 at levels above earlier prices. Continuous nitration adds capex, not operating cost.

qa_highlights.question: Will Kiri shift its strategy toward selling intermediates?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Dyes are the core business and about 95% of intermediates are consumed captively. Spot sales of intermediates are opportunistic and only occur after dye orders are met.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and equity requirement for Makilala, and what is its production profile?
qa_highlights.answer: The MCB project capex is about USD 280 million, with Kiri's equity a little above USD 40 million. Makilala would produce 140,000 t of copper concentrate, with about 100,000 t coming to India.

qa_highlights.question: How will copper price moves affect the project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the LME-minus-to-LME-plus spread is constant, and purchases and sales are hedged through a dedicated desk, so the exposure is operational rather than price-driven.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on H-Acid prices holding, and a China capacity restart could reverse the spread gains.
Standalone PAT is heavily affected by mark-to-market treasury losses (INR 57 crore in Q2).
Litigation: Celsius has appealed the arbitration awards linked to the Makilala stake.
Funding for the USD 280 million Makilala project is still being evaluated (equity versus debt split).
Preferential allotment at INR 475 per share is still in progress; a shareholder asked for a rights issue instead.
Dye prices are passed through with a two-to-three-month lag, so Q3 is only partially expected to reflect the H-Acid increase.
532967|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the long-term copper and fertiliser growth path and on H-Acid pricing, but cautious and somewhat defensive on near-term consolidated margins, which it attributes to order lags. Management gave specific forward figures (8-10% margin target, Q3/Q4 recovery) but was vague on China's timing and on the funding structure for Makilala.
key_quotes: The project remains on track for phase one commencing in first half FY'2028.
So, quarter 3 and quarter 4, both will have significantly higher performance compared to quarter 1 and Quarter 2, where the absorption has taken place.

It is 100% hedge business on the purchase and sale side so that you do not either make anything on the higher fluctuation, on the higher side or you do not lose anything on the lower fluctuation, on the lower side but your spread continues to remain constant and consistent.

financial_highlights.value: INR 248 crore (per transcript; supported by Q1 treasury gains)

Unrealised fair-value loss on treasury investments (Q2)
Share of profit from associates (Lonsen Kiri, 40% stake)

rows.why: Standalone material margin rose to 29.1% from 26.4% and H-Acid price gains are expected to feed through in Q3 and Q4, though vinyl sulphone input costs (sulphur, aniline) have risen sharply and dampen spread gains.

rows.why: Copper and fertilizer project phase one is on track for 1H FY28 with equipment deliveries already started at site; downstream copper facilities of about 2.6 lakh t are targeted for next fiscal year.

rows.why: Intermediate utilisation is below 60%, so the near-term need is raw material, not new plant; but the Makilala MCB project (about USD 280 million, Kiri equity a little above USD 40 million) still has its funding split under evaluation, so a funding or capex decision could be announced.

rows.why: Management expects Q3 and Q4 FY27 to be significantly higher than Q1 and Q2 as H-Acid prices rose from INR 400-500/kg to INR 1,600-1,800 and flow into dye realisations, with 8-10% long-term dye EBITDA margin targeted.

rows.why: Q2 consolidated EBITDA was only about INR 2 crore (3-4% dye margin) and the H-Acid recovery depends on a one-to-two-quarter pass-through lag, while a China capacity restart could reverse the spread gains.

rows.why: Expected to produce 140,000 t of copper concentrate, with about 100,000 t to India, covering roughly 6-7% of the company's 1.6 million t requirement from 2028-29.

rows.why: H-Acid moved from INR 400-500/kg to INR 1,600-1,800 in three to four weeks, China output is below 50% of its roughly 100,000 t need, and dye prices follow with a 2-3 month lag.

rows.why: The preferential allotment is still in progress and a shareholder has asked for a rights issue instead, so the equity route and its dilution remain open.

532976|2026-06.headline: Jai Balaji Q1 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to INR1,683 crore; adjusted EBITDA up 46% to INR154 crore, PAT up 21% to INR85 crore.
532976|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 24% YoY to INR1,683 crore, with adjusted EBITDA up 46% to INR154 crore (about 9% margin) and PAT up 21% to INR85 crore (about 5% margin), attributed to price normalisation and operational efficiency. Ferroalloy and pig iron realisations rose sharply YoY, while DI pipe demand stayed subdued on slow government ordering and fund releases. Management declined to give volume or EBITDA guidance, citing uncertainty, but said pipe prices are at the bottom and cannot fall further. Expansion capex was revised up to INR1,112 crore from about INR1,000 crore, with completion expected by Q3 FY27 and the balance by end-2026.

financial_highlights.change: Net term debt was INR3,408 crore in FY21

segments.name: Ductile iron pipes (DI)
segments.commentary: About 15% of Q1 turnover; utilisation about 30% of the enhanced 5.5 lakh tpa capacity. Order book about four months at current dispatch rate. Management said pipe margins were similar to pig iron margins in Q1.

segments.name: Specialised ferroalloys
segments.commentary: About 27% of revenue; utilisation above 80% in the last quarter. Ferroalloy prices up 46% YoY. Management guided a long-term margin of 15-20%, and exports go to more than 42 countries.

segments.name: Pig iron
segments.commentary: About 19% of revenue; realisations up 16% YoY.

segments.name: TMT bars
segments.commentary: About 14.8% of revenue. Management expects West Bengal sales to rise to 50-70% of TMT volume from 15-20% previously.

segments.name: Commodity mix (sponge iron, billets, coke, scrap, fines)
segments.commentary: Sponge iron 7.4%, billets 3.5%, coke about 7%, scrap and fines about 1% of revenue. Sponge iron and billet realisations were broadly stable.

guidance_outlook: No volume guidance for DI pipes or ferroalloys for FY27; management said demand visibility is too uncertain.
No EBITDA-per-tonne guidance for pipes; management said prices are 25-30% below levels of a year and a half ago and 'cannot get worse'.
Ferroalloy utilisation expected at 80-90% once the new module is commissioned around December-January.
Management indicated revenue of INR7,000-7,500 crore in a normal market once expanded capacity is complete by end-2026; no FY28 or FY30 targets were given beyond this.
Post-monsoon recovery in DI dispatches and payments expected, with improvement from Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: DI pipe capacity raised from 5 lakh tpa to 5.5 lakh tpa.

Specialised ferroalloy capacity rising to 1.9 lakh tpa from 1.66 lakh tpa; blast furnace to 7.5 lakh tpa from 6.3 lakh tpa; sinter to 12.08 lakh tpa from 9.08 lakh tpa. All expected commissioned by Q3 FY27.

Expansion outlay revised to INR1,112 crore from about INR1,000 crore (cause: equipment shipment delays, inflation, rupee depreciation, technical upgrades). About INR1,076 crore already spent, mostly from internal accruals; INR35-40 crore balance by end-2026.
Three railway sidings in operation; about 400 acres of land largely occupied for new capacity.
Management said the INR20 crore trial plastic-alternative pipe plant has sold no pipes and is in abeyance.
demand_pricing: Government DI pipe ordering is slow. Management said INR10,344 crore has been released by the Centre this year, and a FY26 backlog (only INR1,560 crore released in the budget) remains the constraint.
Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 extended to December 2028 with outlay of INR8.69 lakh crore (including INR3.5 lakh crore central assistance); AMRUT 2.0 also cited as a driver.
Competition intense while pipe utilisation stays at 25-35% industry-wide; management said intensity eases above 65-70% utilisation.
Jal Jeevan Mission receivables: management estimated 25-35% of outstanding dues collected, with the rest expected over the next 2-4 months.
Ferroalloy demand described as strong with repeat orders; management said 80-85% capacity is utilised.

qa_highlights.question: When will increased government spending translate into DI pipe dispatches?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a post-monsoon recovery in dispatches and payments, with improvement from Q3 FY27, after central fund releases and state matching shares.

qa_highlights.question: Will pricing pressure persist given competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition will persist until industry utilisation reaches 65-70%. Management said pipe prices are at rock bottom and Q1 pipe margins were similar to pig iron margins.

qa_highlights.question: Can you give DI pipe EBITDA per tonne guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management called pipe EBITDA guidance speculative given the 25-30% price fall and said it would reassess next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin profile of specialised ferroalloys versus conventional steel?
qa_highlights.answer: Conventional steel margins are 5-7%, specialised ferroalloys 15-18%. Long-term ferroalloy margin guidance is 15-20%, with a 1-2% swing from raw materials or freight.

qa_highlights.question: Why did capex rise to about INR1,100 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The increase was about 7-8%, from delayed equipment shipments from China, inflation, higher freight, rupee depreciation, and technical upgrades.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DI pipe order book?
qa_highlights.answer: About four months at current dispatch rates. Q1 DI production was 41,000 tonnes, about 30-33% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is current debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Repayable term debt is INR188 crore. Working capital is INR375-400 crore, sanctioned limits about INR525-550 crore, and net utilisation stays below INR500 crore with INR70-80 crore cash or unutilised limits.

risks_watch: Government fund releases and state payments: DI demand depends on clearing the FY26 backlog and recovering dues.
Pipe pricing at 25-30% below a year and a half ago, with management saying no further downside yet giving no guidance.
Capex overrun risk: budget rose to INR1,112 crore from about INR1,000 crore, and commissioning by Q3 FY27 depends on imported equipment.
Ferroalloy margins (15-20%) depend on raw material costs and freight; management said margins could move 1-2%.
Management did not give FY28 or FY30 capacity or profit targets; the INR7,000-7,500 crore revenue figure is conditional on a normal market.

So, from here things cannot get worse, it has to improve.

So, the net utilization always remains below INR500 crores, while the sanctioned limit stays around INR550 crores.

532977|2026-03.headline: Bajaj Auto Q4 FY26 revenue rose 32% to INR16,006 crores with EBITDA of INR3,323 crores at 20.8%, but management flags April-onward commodity inflation of 3.5-4% of revenue.
532977|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 set records for revenue, EBITDA and volumes, with 2W, 3W and exports each growing about 20% in volume and 30% in revenue. Margins held at 20.8% helped by a stronger rupee (realised INR90.6/USD vs INR86.5 a year ago), richer mix and operating leverage, offsetting net commodity inflation of about 40 bps and absorbed PM E-DRIVE subsidy loss on electric 3-wheelers. Management guided to a sharply weaker operating backdrop from April: domestic motorcycle growth seen at 7-9% near term versus about 20% in Q4, plus 10-15% supply loss, and commodity inflation of 3.5-4% of revenue, about 40% of which has been priced in so far. The board also approved a 100% payout of FY26 profit (dividend INR150/share plus a INR5,633 crore buyback at INR12,000/share).

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Crossed 6 lakh units for second straight quarter, +25% YoY, highest-ever quarterly export revenue; FY26 revenue USD2.2 billion (record). KTM exports from India ~17,500 units in Q4 vs near nil a year ago; Nigeria back above 1 lakh units in Q4 but FY26 flat vs FY25.

segments.name: Domestic motorcycles (2W)
segments.commentary: Industry grew ~11% in FY26 and ~20% in Q4. Bajaj 150cc+ share recovering; 10 Pulsar variants/upgrades launched Oct-Mar now 50% of sales. Q4 KTM+Triumph domestic volumes ~43,000 units, +43% YoY (record).

segments.name: Electric (2W + 3W)
segments.commentary: Now ~20%+ of domestic revenue with double-digit EBITDA margin for last two quarters; Chetak EBITDA-neutral. Chetak Q4 retails above 1 lakh (record), March above 50,000; share ~23%, up 170 bps QoQ. FY26 Chetak revenue INR4,000 crores, over 5 lakh units.

segments.name: 3-wheelers
segments.commentary: Electric 3W No.1 in registrations through Q4 and April; industry 3W growth 25%+ in Q4 and April. Commercial vehicles crossed 5 lakh units in FY26; Q4 volumes +28% YoY; CNG share close to 90%.

segments.name: Spares
segments.commentary: Sales INR1,700+ crores, +16% growth, record EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Bajaj Auto Credit (BACL)
segments.commentary: AUM nearly INR19,000 crores (roughly doubled); FY26 PAT INR665 crores vs INR58 crores; CRAR 19.5%; ROE ~23%; 1.8 million customers.

guidance_outlook: Domestic motorcycle industry growth estimated at 7-9% in the near term (based on April outcomes), versus about 20% in Q4; growth expected mainly from 125cc+ and 150cc+ segments, which management expects to grow about twice the industry rate.
Exports targeted at 2.2 lakh units per month in Q1 FY27 (from 2.0 lakh), with Gulf loss of about 5,000-6,000 units per month.
Material commodity cost inflation of about 3.5-4% of revenue (Q1 vs Q4); about 40% offset by pricing so far; management says the next price action may be the last, if needed.
Supply constraints (LPG, manpower, logistics) impaired April serviceability by 10-15%; expected to ease over time.

Buyback of INR5,633 crores at INR12,000/share needs shareholder approval; process expected to conclude by end-July with payout around second week of July; final dividend INR150/share (INR4,192 crores) after July AGM.
KTM turnaround results expected to show up in the latter part of 2026. KTM and BMAG to move to quarterly reporting with one-quarter lag.
New Pulsar 125cc and 150cc+ launches targeted from July.
capex_capacity: Chetak capacity now 50,000 units per month; management expects to max it out and says a substantive capacity increase is needed, with plan to be announced later.
Brazil plant capacity ~60,000 units per annum (about 50,000 usable), expected to be fully used within 12 months; further expansion considered by mid-year for FY27-28.
FY26 capex about INR500 crores, split equally between ICE and EV; over INR2,300 crores invested in BACL and BAIH BV.
Larger 3-wheeler capacity (7 and 9 series) is becoming a constraint; expansion underway.
demand_pricing: Price hikes effective 1 April across products; management says 30-40% of the GST-cut benefit could be rolled back, weighing on demand.
Realisation of USD/INR around 94-95 currently vs INR90.6 average in Q4; company is unhedged and realises at market.
Commodity moves: noble metals up 35-45%, aluminium up 35-45%, copper ~20%, steel ~15% in the current quarter.
Nigeria fuel prices up about 30%; Nigeria running at 35,000+ units per month for motorcycles plus 5,000+ 3W.
Brazil at 5th position in share in April; Latam 11 consecutive quarters of growth; Mexico and FTA outlook cited as upside.
Competitive pressure: management says 125cc bikes from China are a competitive threat in export markets.

qa_highlights.question: How has the price hike affected demand, and are exports seeing similar effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said motorcycle industry growth fell from Q4 to April and that 30-40% of the GST benefit may roll back. Upper-half and 150cc+ demand remains strong, while Latam and Nigeria are healthy.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company hedged on currency?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Dinesh Thapar said the company is not hedged and realises at market rates.

qa_highlights.question: Will exports outgrow domestic volumes in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not forecast the split but said exports are on a strong footing, targeting above 2 lakh units per month in Q1, and that the 150cc+ domestic segment is also performing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan to lift Chetak beyond the ~30,000/month run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is 50,000 units per month and management expects to max it; a larger capacity expansion is under study and will be discussed later.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 125cc affordable motorcycle launch this year, and what is the PLI amount?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to name a model but said new 125cc and 150cc+ Pulsar launches are coming from July. CFO said PLI for FY26 is about INR900 crores, still being aggregated.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin pressure remains from the 3.5-4% commodity inflation, and what is the margin tolerance?

H2 FY27 should be 'similar to better' than H1 if Q2 conditions persist; management said H2 will 'definitely be better than H1'.
Q3 volumes are expected to run in line with Q2 until the festival season ends; demand uptick expected after that and Q4 is seasonally strongest.

Solar (9 MW) targeted for Q4 FY27 commissioning, expected to meet about 40% of power needs and deliver about ₹8 crore annual EBITDA benefit (about 80 bps), with full benefit from FY28/FY29 (call remarks vary).
Captive talc (Andhra Pradesh) and quartz/feldspar (Rajasthan) mines expected to start production from December 2026.
Malaysia quarry capacity to rise from 4,000 MT to 8,000 MT by FY29, with plant commissioning by FY30.
No buyback planned; promoter stake increase discussed but no timeline given.
capex_capacity: ₹100 crore CapEx programme: about ₹30 crore deployed so far (₹12 crore captive solar, ₹7 crore two mine acquisitions); ₹17 crore more planned in Q3, all on solar, taking deployment to nearly half. Management said remaining ~70% to be deployed over 15-18 months; funded by internal accruals and selective debt.
Captive solar: 9 MW across 5.5 MW Rajasthan and 3.5 MW Gujarat, total investment about ₹29 crore, targeted for Q4 FY27 commissioning.
Capacity additions planned in calcium carbonate, engineered kaolin, talc and nano functional additives over the next two to three years.

Advanced materials: graphite produced internally on a small scale; high-purity quartz in development; bid placed under India's REPM PLI scheme (about 20 bidders), results expected in a couple of months.
demand_pricing: Pricing is case by case: management said it can pass through exceptional power or fuel hikes for some customers, but in highly competitive products competitors are not raising prices.
Raw-material and freight costs rose sharply due to import dependence; imports are about 40% of raw material (China, Malaysia, Vietnam), local sourcing about 60%.
No order book disclosed; customers give fixed quarterly volumes, which management said are unchanged for Q3 and will grow in Q4.
Export freight rose; freight per MT went from ₹2,108 to ₹2,346 QoQ.
Management attributed the gap between customer revenue growth (double digits, on retail price hikes) and its own growth to its B2B pricing and product mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why has 20 Microns' sales growth lagged its paint, polymer and pipe customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said customer financials do not map directly; customers raised retail prices, but 20 Microns cannot pass the same increases. Polymer, rubber and construction-chemical customers grew double digits in Q2, while paint customers did not grow due to subdued demand.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans for buybacks or a promoter stake increase?
qa_highlights.answer: No buyback plans as of now. A promoter stake increase is discussed regularly and is one area management will look at 'in the near future'.

qa_highlights.question: What were the H1 cost increases for furnace oil, gas and freight, and what does the solar benefit depend on?
qa_highlights.answer: Furnace oil rose from about ₹42/kg to ₹56/kg (+33%, ₹1.34 crore); gas from ₹69 to ₹122/kg (+77%, ₹0.62 crore); freight per MT from ₹2,108 to ₹2,346 (+11%, ₹2.92 crore). Total ₹4.78 crore, about 200 bps. Solar grid tariff is about ₹3.45–3.5 net of O&M, per the CFO's answer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 margin and revenue outlook, and how much of the 18% CAGR starts when?
qa_highlights.answer: No numerical range given. Management said H2 will be better than H1 if Q2 conditions hold and the 18% CAGR is supported by projects and mines, with the 70% remaining capex deployed over 15-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: How are value-added products performing, and what is their margin contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said specialty products have started to contribute to margins; Nano grew in double digits with higher profit, but raw-material and freight costs offset gains. Margins should improve once these costs stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Q3 and what is the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: No order book is disclosed. Q3 is expected to run like Q2 until the festival season ends; Q4 is typically the strongest quarter.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin compression from energy (furnace oil, gas) and freight costs; management has not quantified the recovery path.
Import dependence (about 40% of raw material) exposes costs to USD pricing and freight; supply chain disruptions cited.
Paint segment demand remains subdued; price-competitive products limit pass-through of cost increases.
Working-capital and cash-flow catch-up expected as inventory normalises; not yet visible in numbers.
Execution risk on ₹100 crore capex, solar commissioning in Q4 and mine start-up from December 2026.
Pending PLI result for rare-earth permanent magnets; high-purity quartz and graphite are early-stage with no timelines disclosed.

533023|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR 1,197 crore (+15.2% YoY), but margins compressed on material cost and a pricing lag from the Middle East conflict.
533023|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue reached INR 1,197 crore, the highest single quarter, up 15.2% YoY, with PBT of INR 196.6 crore (+16.4%) and PAT of INR 146.3 crore (+15.5%). FY26 revenue was INR 4,302 crore (+9.2%), PBT INR 693 crore (+13.9%) and PAT INR 517 crore (+12.2%). Management attributed the Q4 margin fall (about 230 bps QoQ) to material cost increases from supply constraints and the Middle East conflict, plus a January salary increase, with customer price recovery still under negotiation. The board approved a 5:1 bonus issue and a final dividend of INR 4 per share post bonus.

segments.name: OE (original equipment)
segments.commentary: Q4 OE sales grew about 25% YoY; FY26 OE sales grew 17.5-17.6% to INR 1,978 crore, outperforming an industry where >6t vehicle production rose 16.6% to 463,000 units. Q4 >6t production hit a record 151,000 units (+26.9%).

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Q4 aftermarket grew about 21% YoY to INR 151 crore; FY26 revenue INR 583-584 crore (+15.5-15.6%). Network expanded by 51 distributor branches and 14 service centres.

segments.name: Exports (goods)
segments.commentary: Q4 exports fell about 6% YoY per the call, with Europe up about 6% and the Americas down about 22%; FY26 exports INR 1,025 crore (-11.1%). Management guided to moderate improvement, with early US recovery signs in Q4.

segments.name: Export services (engineering)
segments.commentary: Export of services grew 22.5% YoY in Q4 and 15.4% for FY26, driven by engineering work for global centres; service income for FY26 was INR 509 crore (+10%).

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating margin expected to be broadly flat, with at most single-digit growth; management was cautious given the Middle East conflict and government calls for expense control.
FY27 capex guided at INR 180-190 crore, covering new product capex plus replacements and upgrades.
April and May 2026 volumes were described as better than prior years, with Q1 expected to be a good quarter.
Final dividend of INR 4 per share post bonus; bonus issue 5:1 with record date 24 June 2026 and deemed allotment 25 June 2026, subject to approvals; AGM and dividend record date 10 July 2026.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex planned at INR 180-190 crore, split between new products and replacement/upgrade spend.

Oragadam multidivisional plant: new lines for crankshaft machining, ASP cartridges and vacuum pump commissioned; management said Mahindra World City utilisation is near peak and further expansion will be at Oragadam.
Jamshedpur rainwater harvesting pond of 1,200 kL to meet about 40% of plant water needs; Ambattur organic waste converter commissioned.
Assembly capabilities strengthened at Jamshedpur and Lucknow; OMA maturity assessment completed with a good score across Ambattur, Mahindra World City, Lucknow and Jamshedpur.
demand_pricing: Q4 margin fell about 230 bps QoQ on higher material costs (aluminium up from about INR 233/kg to INR 274/kg, roughly 18% of material cost) and a January salary increase; price recovery talks with customers are ongoing and lag costs.
ESC is voluntarily fitted in POL/tanker trucks today; regulation kicks in from October 2027 for vehicles above 6t, and management expects value per vehicle to rise as ESC penetration increases.
ADAS: management has won full-suite business from 2 OEMs; discussions are ongoing with most other OEMs, with several competitors also engaged.
Management said OEMs are increasingly splitting ESC and AEBS/ADAS across partners, while AEBS/ADAS (5 mandated features) is typically sourced from a single partner.
Q3 to Q4 value per vehicle drop was attributed to one-off retrospective selling price variances recognised in Q3; excluding them, value per vehicle was roughly flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 margins fall about 230 bps QoQ, and what is the FY27 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher material costs from supply constraints and the Middle East conflict, plus a January salary increase, with no one-offs. FY27 margin is expected to be broadly flat with single-digit growth, with caution on the macro outlook.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA growth lag revenue growth in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost increases from the war and commodity prices came ahead of customer price recoveries, creating a timing lag that management expects to correct over time.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Q4 segment growth rates and blended export decline?
qa_highlights.answer: OE grew about 25%, aftermarket about 21%, exports fell about 6%, and export services rose 22.5%. Europe grew about 6%, the Americas fell about 22%, and the blended export decline was about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of diesel price hikes on demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said higher diesel prices would hit freight rates and truck utilisation, which could slow vehicle purchases with a lag. Replacement demand for inefficient old trucks could offset this.

qa_highlights.question: How does ADAS and AEBS sourcing work with ESC?
qa_highlights.answer: ESC and ADAS can be sourced from separate suppliers, but AEBS and ADAS are typically awarded to one partner able to demonstrate all 5 mandated features.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for US exports and the FY30 India localisation target?
qa_highlights.answer: The US export gap versus two years ago is still about 20%, though US vehicle production has risen for four months. Management said new RFQs are coming in and the group's India growth commitment stands.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict and commodity cost inflation (aluminium) squeezing margins until customer price recoveries are agreed.
Diesel price hike may reduce freight rates and truck utilisation, delaying vehicle purchases.
US export volumes still about 20% below two years ago; Americas down about 22% in Q4.
Timing of ESC and ADAS mandate from October 2027 and the pace of further OEM ADAS awards.
Q3 one-off selling price variances distorted value per vehicle; watch the Q1 FY27 reading.
Supplier constraints and gas shortages seen earlier in FY26 could recur.

533023|2026-06.headline: ZF CV India Q1 FY27: Total income up 5.7% to ₹1,101.8 cr; PAT fell 14.7% to ₹104.5 cr on a high base FX gain, while aftermarket rose 15.6% to ₹158.4 cr.

financial_highlights.metric: Total income excluding FX and one-time items
PBT excluding FX and one-time items
FX gain/loss and one-time items in Q1 FY26 vs Q1 FY27
financial_highlights.value: Q1 FY26: FX gain ~₹39 crore plus one-time income ₹4.7 crore; Q1 FY27: FX loss ₹1.98 crore and one-time income ₹1.2 crore

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Sales of ₹158.4 crore, up 15.6% YoY; highest-ever monthly aftermarket sale of ₹63.06 crore in June 2026. New launches under SPARK include Disc Brake Rotors, TRW products, Clutch Master Cylinders, CV Brake Pads, Hydraulic Steering Systems and trailer Quick Fittings.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue of ₹271.4 crore, up 9.7% YoY, led by Double Diaphragm Spring Brake actuators, Uni-Stop Disc and CAM Brake Chambers, and Air Compressors; Uni-Stop Disc Brake Chamber ramp-up for North American customers. Growth came from the Chennai SEZ plant per management.

segments.name: Domestic CV >6T (OE)
segments.commentary: Sales grew 8.6% YoY versus industry CV >6T growth of 8.4%; management cited new product realisations (Exhaust Brake Valve, ECAS variants) and higher e-compressor penetration.

segments.name: Engineering services exports
segments.commentary: Growth of 12.5% YoY, driven by expansion of engineering activities delivered from India to global centres; services growth running at about 7.5% QoQ per management.

qa_highlights.question: Will ESC addressable market extend across CV segments including LCV, and will 12V content differ from 24V?
qa_highlights.answer: Shankar Venkatachalam said the ESC win is pneumatic ESC only; 12V is mostly intermediate CVs, and content per vehicle stays the same. LCV focus is on hydraulic ESC (already in series supply for some OEMs) and booster/tandem master cylinders.

qa_highlights.question: Will ZF's ESC market share mirror its pneumatic braking share, and will AEBS/ADAS also be won?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to retain its majority position across ABS plus ESC with most major OEMs. AEBS/ADAS is seen as separable with many standalone suppliers; ZF is nominated with some e-bus makers for EBS plus ESC full suite.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ESC localisation level and when does manufacturing start?
qa_highlights.answer: Localisation is about 40-50% today, moving above 75% by SOP; manufacturing starts in Q3 of next year with local EMS partners.

qa_highlights.question: Export outlook and order book for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Momentum is returning, driven by North American actuation products and air compressors from the Chennai SEZ plant; no quantified double-digit guidance given due to geopolitical uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic OEM growth and US/Europe market trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic CV growth was 8.6% in the quarter versus vehicle growth around 8.5%; US and Europe markets each declined about 10%, with US the larger decline, but ZF overall export sales were better.

qa_highlights.question: What were the headwinds and the base-quarter one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Headwinds were aluminium and gas price spikes, oil-linked consumables and chemicals costs, plus blue-collar shortages. The base quarter had about ₹39 crore FX gain (billing at 1.08x) plus actuarial one-timers, totalling ₹43.7 crore, versus ₹1.98 crore FX loss now.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost and other expenses rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited increments; ~₹8.4 crore employee cost recovery is offset by ₹8.5 crore recovery shown elsewhere, net ~₹17 crore India cost increase. QoQ other expenses rose ~₹12.4 crore from FX loss, CSR, consultancy/IT, director commission and service-location rent.

guidance_outlook: Management expects services growth to remain around the current ~7.5% level in coming months, supported by vehicle solutions, integrated brake controls, operations and performance improvement, advanced products and cybersecurity services.
Management declined to give a numeric export growth guidance for FY27 citing geopolitical uncertainty, but said outlook looks positive with a strong rebound expected in the US and Europe.
ESC manufacturing to start in Q3 of next year (FY28 per the call's timing); localisation at ~40-50% currently, expected to exceed 75% by SOP.

Commodity and FX cost pass-through: part recovered, balance under active discussion with OEMs; recovery typically has a two-quarter lag but has taken longer due to the West Asia conflict; expected to be secured over the next quarter.
Selective aftermarket price increases effective July 2026; PERFORM26 initiative targets CIS, productivity, value engineering and material cost optimisation.
Early Q2 signs: July 2026 vehicle production averaging 40,000-42,000 units, about 10,000 above a typical July; August and September seen at similar levels.
capex_capacity: New assembly lines for ASP cartridges and vacuum pumps productionised at the Oragadam multi-divisional facility; e-compressor and brake signal transmitter production scaled up.
New assembly lines for brake actuators and valves commissioned across the manufacturing network; strategic investments at Jamshedpur, Lucknow and Pantnagar improved flexibility.
Lucknow plant commissioned a 2,100 kilolitre rainwater harvesting system; Ambattur plant moved from LPG cooking to electric induction (about 16 tons LPG saved annually).
ESC homologation testing commenced for multiple customers at the ZF Proving Ground; Hemi Anechoic Chamber at ZF Test Track received NABL accreditation.
demand_pricing: Industry CV >6T production grew 8.4% in Q1 FY27; trailer market demand fell about 9% on slower mining, monsoon disruption and higher input costs.
Blue-collar manpower shortage across India in April and May affected industry production.
Aluminium rose from around ₹260/kg to over ₹360/kg per management; about ₹25/kg has come off since July, with easing expected if geopolitical tensions ease.
US and European markets each declined roughly 10% YoY per management, with US declining more; US market now ramping up.
ESC: business nominations secured from three major OEMs; management says ZF will retain majority position in ABS plus ESC market; content per vehicle unchanged across 12V and 24V.
EV bus sales reached 1,417 units in the quarter per management.
risks_watch: Commodity and FX cost pass-through from OEMs: partial recovery so far, balance still under negotiation; margin pressure from aluminium, chemicals and energy costs.
FX volatility: Q1 FY27 carried a ₹1.98 crore FX loss versus a large prior-year FX gain, so reported PAT is sensitive to FX items.
Geopolitical uncertainty affecting US/European export recovery and commodity prices; management declined to quantify export growth for FY27.
ESC ramp: manufacturing starting Q3 of next year, localisation must rise from 40-50% to above 75% by SOP; AEBS/ADAS nominations unconfirmed.
Trailer segment weakness (about 9% market decline) and labour shortages; monsoon-driven volume dip expected in July-September, though early July data looked stronger.
Leadership change: CFO Sweta Agarwal replaced by Rakesh Mishra effective September 1, 2026.
key_quotes: Despite these headwinds, we are at par with the market, supported by improved realizations from new product introductions such as the Exhaust Brake Valve and ECAS variants, along with increased market penetration of our e-compressor solutions.
The Aftermarket business delivered a strong performance in Q1 FY26-27, with sales of ₹158.4 crore, representing a 15.6% year-on-year growth.
